name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the backrest to 30–45° and leave the seat flat. If you slide down the bench, raise the seat one notch.
Sit with the dumbbells standing on your thighs near the knees, then lie back and kick them up to your shoulders with your knees.
Plant your feet flat, wider than your hips, knees bent about 90°. Glutes, upper back and head stay on the pads.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the backrest. A small natural arch in your lower back is fine.
Start with the dumbbells beside your upper chest, palms facing your feet, handles in one line and forearms vertical.
Press up and slightly in until your arms are straight over your shoulders. Stop with the dumbbells a few centimeters apart instead of clanging them.
Lower over about 2 seconds along the same arc until the handles reach your upper chest, elbows about 45–60° from your torso.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest, then onto your thighs as you sit up. Never drop them from straight arms.

name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the bar in the hooks at a height you can unrack with your arms almost straight, then lie down with your eyes under it.
Plant your feet flat and wide, under or a little behind your knees. They stay put until the bar is back in the hooks.
Take an overhand grip with your thumbs wrapped, hands a little wider than your shoulders. On an Olympic bar that's often near the ring marks.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and pin them to the bench. A small lower-back arch is fine, but your glutes stay down.
Unrack on straight arms and bring the bar out until it sits over your shoulders. Breathe in and brace your stomach.
Lower the bar over 1–2 seconds to the bottom half of your chest, around nipple level, elbows 45–60° from your sides and forearms vertical.
Touch lightly without bouncing, then press up and slightly back toward your face until your elbows are straight and the bar is over your shoulders.
After the final rep, lock out, move the bar back until it touches the uprights, and only then set it down in the hooks.

name: Machine Chest Fly
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level when you sit down.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Exhale and slowly bring the handles together in front of your chest by contracting your pectoral muscles.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction, ensuring your arms are parallel to each other.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: High Low Cable Chest Fly
instructions: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to a high position above shoulder height.
Attach D-handle attachments to each pulley.
Stand in the center of the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
Step forward slightly to create tension in the cables, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Position your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Exhale and bring your hands together in front of your body in a wide arc, maintaining the bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, controlling the weight throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 15-30 degree angle and position it under a barbell rack.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability.
Grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and hold it directly above your chest with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly to your upper chest, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the barbell is near your chest, then press it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells standing on end on your thighs, close to your knees.
Lie back and push each knee up into its dumbbell as you go, so the weights arrive at your chest instead of being swung up.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width or a little wider, knees bent about 90°. Head, upper back and glutes stay on the pad.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and leave them there. A small arch in your lower back is fine.
With the handles in one line and knuckles to the ceiling, press up and slightly in to straight arms, dumbbells almost touching.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower them out and down beside your mid to lower chest, forearms vertical and elbows about 45–60° from your sides.
Stop when your elbows dip just below the bench, or sooner if your shoulders complain, then press the next rep without a bounce.
To get up, bring the dumbbells to your chest, curl your knees up and rock to sitting with the weights back on your thighs.

name: Plate-Loaded Chest Press
instructions: Load the same plates on both horns. The levers move independently, so mismatched plates mean one arm pushes more than the other.
Set the seat so the handles rest level with your mid-chest, roughly at nipple height.
Sit with your hips all the way back and your back and head on the backrest. Plant your feet flat, about hip width, knees near 90°.
Take the horizontal handles overhand, knuckles up, hands a little wider than your shoulders and wrists straight over your forearms.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the pad before the first rep, and leave them pinned there until the set is over.
Press both handles along the machine's arc, which rises slightly and brings your hands closer, until your arms are almost straight. Your shoulders stay on the pad.
Take about 2 seconds to bring the handles back beside your chest, elbows just behind your torso, until you feel the stretch. Touch the bottom lightly and go again.
When the set is done, guide both handles back onto the rest stops. Don't let go of either handle until both levers are resting there.

name: Smith Incline Chest Press
instructions: Set the bench to an incline angle of about 30-45 degrees under the Smith machine bar.
Position yourself on the bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, ensuring wrists are straight and aligned with forearms.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and position it directly above your upper chest.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly to your chest, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the bar is just above your chest without bouncing.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position, ensuring arms are fully extended but not locked.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Push-Up
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by pulling your belly button towards your spine to maintain a neutral spine position.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your torso. Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Ensure that your body remains in a straight line throughout the movement without sagging or arching your back.

name: Incline Hammer Chest Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height so the handles line up with your shoulders.
Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the floor and your back firmly against the back pad.
Grip the handles with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Start with the handles at shoulder height, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping your wrists straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring not to lock out your elbows.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys of the crossover to the lowest notch, clip a single D-handle to each cable and pick the same weight on both stacks.
Take the handles underhand, palms forward, and stand in the middle, half a step in front of the pulleys, with both stacks lifted.
Stagger your feet half a step, knees soft. Chest up, shoulder blades back and down, hands by your hips, elbows slightly bent.
Lock that elbow bend in and sweep both hands forward, up and in along a wide arc, as if scooping something up toward your chin.
Stop when your hands meet in front of the upper chest at shoulder height, palms up, and squeeze for about a second without shrugging.
Take 2–3 seconds to bring your hands down until they are back by your hips and the upper chest feels a light stretch.
Only your shoulders move. Torso, hips and feet stay put, and the weights don't touch the stack until the set is done.
When you finish, step back toward the pulleys so the stacks settle before you let go of the handles.

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Extend your arms above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Bring the dumbbells back to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Middle Chest Fly
instructions: Set the cable pulleys to shoulder height and attach single grip handles.
Stand in the center of the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Step forward slightly to create tension on the cables, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Position your arms out to the sides with palms facing forward, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Exhale and bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping elbows slightly bent.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement, ensuring handles meet at chest level.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with control, allowing your arms to open back to the sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Dumbbell Chest Fly
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting them on your thighs.
Lie back on the bench and lift the dumbbells above your chest with palms facing each other.
Slightly bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement to protect your joints.
Bring the dumbbells back up in a controlled manner to the starting position, squeezing your chest at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level.
Sit back against the pad with feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Engage your core and press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended without locking your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Decline Chest Press
instructions: Load the same plates on both levers, or set the pin on a stack machine, and adjust the seat so the handles start level with your lower chest, just below the nipples.
Sit with your hips all the way back and your back and head on the pad. Feet flat, about hip to shoulder width apart, knees bent close to 90°.
Take the handles overhand, hands a little wider than your shoulders, knuckles up and wrists stacked straight over your forearms.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the pad. Your elbows sit about 45–60° from your sides, slightly behind the handles.
Press both handles forward and down along the machine's arc until your arms are almost straight in front of your lower chest. Shoulders stay on the pad and the elbows never lock.
Take about 2 seconds to bring the handles back beside your lower chest, where you should feel a stretch across the bottom of your chest. Touch lightly without resting the plates, then press again.
When the set is done, guide the handles back onto their stops before you let go, so the levers don't slam.

name: Straight Bar Dips
instructions: Position yourself above a straight bar with your arms fully extended and hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight as you lower yourself by bending your elbows.
Lower your body until your shoulders are below your elbows or as far as comfortable.
Press through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the movement and avoid swinging or using momentum.

name: Smith Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to a flat position under the Smith machine bar.
Lie back on the bench with your eyes directly under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists to release it from the safety hooks.
Lower the bar slowly to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
After completing your set, rotate your wrists to re-engage the safety hooks and rack the bar.

name: Pec Deck Chest Fly
instructions: Set the seat so that, sitting tall, your elbows are level with your shoulders or slightly below and your shoulders sit right under the machine's pivots.
Before you sit, set the start-position adjuster, if there is one, so your elbows open only to the line of your body. Pick the weight now too.
Sit with your back and shoulder blades flat on the backrest, chest up, and feet flat on the floor a little wider than your hips.
Put your forearms upright against the pads with your elbows at the bottom end, bent about 90°. Your hands just rest on the top handles.
Breathe out and drive your elbows toward the middle of your chest until the pads touch. Squeeze for a second while your upper back stays on the backrest.
Breathe in as the pads open over about 2 seconds, back to the line of your body with a stretch across your chest. Keep the stack off its rest until the last rep.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the decline bench to an angle of about 15 to 30 degrees.
Lie back on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and hold it above your chest with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly to your lower chest, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lying Chest Press
instructions: Load the same plates on both weight horns, then lie back on the pad with your head toward the frame.
Slide up or down until the resting handles sit beside your mid-chest, around the nipple line, not at your neck or over your stomach.
Plant your feet flat and wider than your hips, knees bent about 90°. Hips, upper back and head stay on the pad.
Take the handles with your palms facing each other and thumbs toward your head, wrists straight over vertical forearms.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the pad. A small natural arch in your lower back is fine; a big bridge is not.
Exhale and press both handles up until your arms are nearly straight over your shoulders. The levers' arc carries your hands slightly toward your head.
Lower for about 2 seconds along the same arc, elbows 30–45° from your sides, until the handles are back beside your chest and you feel a stretch.
Touch lightly and press again before the plates settle on the stops. After the last rep, set both handles down on the stops, then let go.

name: Incline Bench Cable Fly
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline and position it between two cable pulleys.
Attach D-handle attachments to the low pulleys.
Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, and grasp each handle with a neutral grip.
Lean back against the bench, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows, palms facing each other.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Close Grip Dumbbell Press
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your feet flat on the floor.
Position the dumbbells directly above your chest with palms facing each other and elbows close to your body.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly towards your chest by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked in.
Pause briefly when the dumbbells are near your chest.
Exhale and press the dumbbells back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Floor Dumbbell Press
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Position your upper arms on the floor at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down until your upper arms touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Decline Push-Up
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on an elevated surface such as a bench or step, ensuring it's stable and secure.
Position your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor, directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Cable Fly
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level when you are seated.
Sit on the bench with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Start with your arms extended out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
Exhale as you bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping your elbows slightly bent throughout.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control.

name: Chest Dips
instructions: Begin by gripping the parallel bars with your palms facing inward and arms fully extended.
Lift your body off the ground by straightening your arms, keeping your torso slightly leaning forward.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Maintain a controlled motion throughout the exercise, avoiding any swinging or jerking movements.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to a decline angle of approximately 15 to 30 degrees.
Lie back on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Extend your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your chest, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press the dumbbells back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Push-Up on Parallel Bars
instructions: Place two parallettes on the floor about shoulder-width apart and grip them with your palms facing inward.
Step your feet back into a high plank with your arms straight, legs straight and feet together.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower your chest between the bars until it is level with or just below your hands.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Chest Press Hammer Grip
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level when you are seated.
Sit down and firmly plant your feet on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your back pressed against the seat and engage your core.
Press the handles forward by extending your arms fully without locking your elbows.
Pause briefly at full extension, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Position your hands shoulder-width apart on an elevated surface, such as a bench or step.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body.
Lower your chest towards the elevated surface by bending your elbows.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the surface.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Low Cable Incline Bench Press
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 30-45 degree angle in front of a cable machine.
Attach handles to the low pulleys on each side of the machine.
Sit on the bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Grab the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Position your hands at chest level, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the handles upward and slightly inward until your arms are fully extended but not locked.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control.

name: Low Incline Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting them on your thighs.
Lie back on the bench with your arms extended down by your sides, the dumbbells next to your hips and a slight bend in your elbows.
Sweep the dumbbells up and in, in a wide arc, until they meet above your upper chest.
Squeeze your upper chest briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells along the same arc back to your sides under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Svend Press
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, maintaining a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Hold a weight plate between your palms at chest level, keeping your elbows bent and close to your body.
Press your palms together to squeeze the weight plate, engaging your chest muscles.
Extend your arms forward slowly until they are fully extended in front of you, keeping the plate squeezed tightly.
Pause briefly at full extension, maintaining tension in your chest.
Slowly bring the weight plate back to the starting position at chest level while maintaining pressure on the plate.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Floor Chest Fly
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Extend your arms above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your upper arms touch the floor.
Pause briefly, then bring the dumbbells back to the starting position using the same arc.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Larsen Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your eyes directly under the barbell.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet off the ground and extend your legs straight out, keeping them parallel to the floor.
Unrack the barbell and position it directly above your chest with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly to your chest, maintaining control and keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the barbell touches your chest.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms, ensuring a controlled movement throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Press Around
instructions: Set one pulley at about shoulder height and clip on a single D-handle.
Stand side-on to the column with your working arm nearest the stack. Step away until the weight stays lifted with the handle beside your chest.
Stagger your feet: the cable-side leg back on the ball of the foot, the other foot forward and flat, knees soft.
Hold the handle palm down beside your chest, elbow out to the side and just below shoulder height.
Rest your free hand on your stomach, hips and shoulders square to the front. That hand feels it the moment your torso turns.
Press on a level arc forward and across, as if around a post, until your hand sits in front of the opposite shoulder.
With the elbow almost straight and your chest still facing forward, squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to return along the same arc, stopping beside your chest. After the last rep, turn around for the other arm.

name: Wide Push-Up
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows out to the sides.
Stop when your chest is just above the floor, ensuring your elbows are at about a 90-degree angle.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form.

name: One-Arm Low-to-High Cable Fly
instructions: Set the cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle.
Stand sideways to the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand, keeping your arm extended but slightly bent at the elbow.
Position your body so that your working arm is across your body at hip level.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Exhale as you pull the handle upward and across your body in a sweeping motion until it reaches shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position, controlling the weight throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Knee Push-Up
instructions: Start by kneeling on the floor. Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on the ground.
Position your knees together and keep your feet lifted off the ground.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Push-Up
instructions: Begin by placing a weight plate or weighted vest on your back. Ensure the weight is centered and secure.
Assume a standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and feet together.
Engage your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the ground.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your legs bent and feet flat.
Position the barbell over your chest, gripping it slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and press your upper back into the floor.
Lower the barbell until your upper arms touch the floor, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly, then press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Standing Cable Low Chest Press
instructions: Set the cable machine pulleys to the lowest position and attach handles.
Stand in the center of the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the handles with an overhand grip and step forward slightly to create tension in the cables.
Position your hands at hip level with elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Press the handles upward and forward until your arms are fully extended in front of you at chest height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows and lowering the handles back to hip level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Fly
instructions: Set the cable machine to a high pulley position and attach a single handle.
Stand sideways to the machine, with your feet shoulder-width apart, and grasp the handle with your outer hand.
Step away from the machine to create tension on the cable, keeping your arm slightly bent.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Pull the handle across your body in a wide arc, keeping your elbow slightly bent throughout the movement.
Squeeze your chest at the end of the motion before slowly returning to the starting position.
Perform the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Punching Bag Boxing
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, dominant foot slightly back.
Keep your knees slightly bent and weight balanced on the balls of your feet.
Raise your hands to chin level, elbows close to your body, and fists clenched.
Start with basic punches: jab with your lead hand, cross with your rear hand.
Rotate your hips and shoulders for power while keeping your core engaged.
Maintain a steady rhythm and breathe consistently throughout the exercise.
Incorporate combinations of punches such as jab-cross, hook, and uppercut.
Focus on accuracy and speed rather than just power.

name: Deep Push Up On Parallel Bars
instructions: Place a pair of parallettes on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and grip them with your palms facing each other.
Extend your legs behind you, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is below the level of the bars.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring a deep stretch in the chest muscles.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form.

name: One-Arm Low Fly Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm hanging at your side and a slight bend in the elbow.
Keep your chest up, your shoulders down and your other arm relaxed at your side.
Sweep the dumbbell forward and up in an arc across your body until your hand is in front of your face, near the midline.
Squeeze your upper chest briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell along the same arc back to your side under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Barbell Pullover
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip the barbell with both hands, shoulder-width apart, and hold it above your chest with arms extended.
Engage your core and keep your back flat against the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell in an arc over your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Return to the starting position by reversing the motion, keeping control of the barbell throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hammer Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Position the dumbbells at shoulder width, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Engage your core and press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Warm-Up Dynamic Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band with both hands in front of you.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, keeping a slight tension on the band.
Slowly raise your arms overhead while maintaining tension in the band, ensuring your elbows remain slightly bent.
Once your arms are fully extended overhead, gently pull the band apart to increase the stretch across your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position by bringing your arms back down in front of you.
Repeat the movement for 10-15 repetitions, focusing on controlled motion and consistent tension.

name: Lying Cable Fly
instructions: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to the lowest position and attach single handle grips.
Lie flat on a bench positioned between the cable stacks, ensuring your feet are flat on the floor.
Grasp each handle with your palms facing each other and extend your arms straight up above your chest.
With a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then bring your arms back to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the motion.

name: Cross Body One-Arm Strength Press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your mid chest, then load the machine.
Sit with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip one handle and rest your free hand on your thigh.
Brace your core and press the handle forward and slightly across your body until your arm is extended.
Pause briefly, then slowly let the handle come back until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Seated Cable Chest Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level when seated.
Sit down with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Engage your core and keep your elbows slightly below shoulder level.
Press the handles forward by extending your arms until they are fully extended but not locked.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows and controlling the weight back.

name: Ring Push-Up
instructions: Adjust the rings to hang just above the ground.
Position yourself in a plank position with hands gripping the rings, arms fully extended, and feet together.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Descend until your chest is in line with your hands.
Push through the rings to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Pin Bench Press
instructions: Set up a flat bench inside a power rack and adjust the safety pins to the desired height, typically just above chest level.
Lie on the bench with your eyes directly under the barbell. Ensure your feet are flat on the floor and your back is slightly arched.
Grip the barbell with a slightly wider than shoulder-width grip, ensuring your wrists are straight and elbows are directly under the bar.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly until it rests on the safety pins. Pause briefly to eliminate momentum.
Press the barbell upwards explosively until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back to the pins with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Bench Press
instructions: Set up a flat bench between two low pulley machines. Attach D-handle attachments to each cable.
Lie on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, ensuring your back is in contact with the bench.
Grab each handle with an overhand grip and position your hands at chest level, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the handles upward by extending your arms, keeping your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the chest muscles.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control and tension in the cables.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Poliquin Flyes
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lie back on the bench, keeping your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed against the bench.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly in an arc motion to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring tension remains in your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Deep Push Up
instructions: Begin by placing two dumbbells on the floor shoulder-width apart. Ensure they are stable and won't roll.
Grip the dumbbells firmly and position yourself in a high plank position with your arms extended, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, allowing your chest to descend between the dumbbells.
Lower yourself until your chest is slightly below the level of the dumbbells to maximize range of motion.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then push through your palms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set the cable pulleys at chest height and attach handles.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and step forward slightly to create tension in the cables.
Position your hands at chest level with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended without locking your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position, keeping tension in the cables.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Knuckle Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Place your fists on the ground shoulder-width apart, with your knuckles facing down.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body as you lower yourself towards the ground.
Lower your chest until it is just above the ground, keeping your body straight.
Push through your knuckles to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Kneeling High To Low Fly
instructions: Position the pulleys on a cable machine at a high setting.
Attach handles to the cables and kneel down in the center of the machine.
Hold a handle in each hand with your arms extended out to the sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Pause briefly when your hands meet, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Scapula Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your arms straight and engage your core to maintain stability.
Without bending your elbows, retract your shoulder blades by squeezing them together, allowing your chest to lower slightly.
Protract your shoulder blades by pushing them apart, rounding your upper back and returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout.

name: Dumbbell Larsen Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Position yourself so that your head, shoulders, and glutes are in contact with the bench.
Lift your feet off the ground and extend your legs straight out or bend them at the knees to reduce leg drive.
Start with the dumbbells at chest level, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Neutral Grip Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor and back firmly against the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Position the dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Chest Fly
instructions: Anchor the resistance band at chest height on a sturdy support.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand.
Step forward to create tension in the band, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows, palms facing forward.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping elbows slightly bent.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance.

name: World’s Greatest Stretch
instructions: From a push-up position or standing, step one foot far forward, whole foot flat, and sink your hips low. The front knee can travel well past the toes.
Straighten the rear leg: knee off the floor, heel pushed back, weight on the ball of the foot. Squeeze that glute to open the front of the hip.
Plant the hand opposite your front leg flat on the floor inside the front foot, fingers forward, and push the floor away with a straight arm.
Let your other arm hang inside the front knee, hand reaching toward the instep, while the knee stays out over your toes.
Breathe out and turn your chest toward the front leg. The free arm sweeps past your face and up in an arc until it points at the ceiling.
Follow the hand with your eyes and pause for 2-3 seconds, both arms in one line from floor to ceiling, hips low and square.
Bring the arm back down the same arc to inside the knee. Finish all your reps on this side, then switch legs.

name: Clap Push-Up
instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Explosively push yourself upwards with enough force to lift your hands off the ground.
Quickly clap your hands together while in the air.
Return your hands to the starting position to catch yourself and immediately proceed to the next repetition.

name: One-Arm High-to-Low Cable Fly
instructions: Set the cable machine to a high position and attach a single handle.
Stand sideways to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand, keeping your arm extended but slightly bent at the elbow.
Step away from the machine to create tension in the cable.
Position your non-working hand on your hip or at your side for balance.
Engage your core and keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
Pull the handle down and across your body in a controlled motion until it reaches hip level.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control of the cable.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Archer Push-Up
instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend one arm fully to the side, keeping it straight, while the other arm remains bent.
Lower your body towards the bent arm, keeping your core tight and back straight.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your chest is close to the ground.
Push through the bent arm to return to the starting position.
Shift your weight to the opposite side and repeat the movement with the other arm.

name: Lean Planche
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and fingers pointing forward.
Lean your body forward by shifting your weight onto your hands, keeping your arms straight.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your feet together and lift them slightly off the ground, balancing on your hands.
Hold this position for as long as possible, maintaining control and stability.
Slowly return to the starting position by reversing the movement.

name: Shoulder Tap
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent your hips from swaying.
Lift your right hand off the ground and tap your left shoulder, keeping your body as still as possible.
Return your right hand to the starting position and immediately lift your left hand to tap your right shoulder.
Continue alternating taps for the desired number of repetitions or time.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, arm extended above your chest.
Place your free hand on your hip or extend it out to the side for balance.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of your chest, keeping your elbow at a 45-degree angle.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Press the dumbbell back up to the starting position by extending your arm fully.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Kneeling Wide Push-Up
instructions: Start by kneeling on the floor with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, engaging your core.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows outwards.
Stop when your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position.
Maintain a steady pace and controlled movement throughout the exercise.

name: Decline Smith Bench Press
instructions: Set the decline bench at a 15-30 degree angle under the Smith machine bar.
Lie back on the bench with your feet secured under the footpads or firmly planted on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, ensuring wrists are straight and aligned with forearms.
Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists or releasing the safety catches, keeping your arms extended.
Lower the bar slowly towards your lower chest, maintaining control and keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the bar is just above your chest, ensuring tension in the muscles.
Press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your arms, without locking elbows at the top.
Repeat for desired repetitions, then safely re-rack the bar.

name: Dumbbell Low to High Fly
instructions: Pick light dumbbells, roughly what you'd use for a front raise or a bit less, and stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Let the dumbbells hang beside your outer thighs, palms facing your legs, hands in the middle of the handles and wrists straight.
Unlock your elbows into a small bend you'll keep until the last rep. Shoulders down away from your ears, ribs down, abs lightly braced.
Sweep both dumbbells forward, up and in along a wide arc, like scooping up a big ball to hug it, palms facing each other.
Move only at the shoulders. The elbow angle doesn't change and your torso stays upright, with no lean back.
Stop with the dumbbells almost touching at eye level, upper arms near shoulder height. Squeeze your upper chest for half a second.
Lower along the same arc in about 2 seconds, hands drifting apart, until the dumbbells hang beside your thighs. Start each rep from a standstill.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Set a decline bench at an angle of 15-30 degrees and lie back on it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Position your feet securely under the foot pads to maintain stability.
Hold the dumbbells above your chest with palms facing each other, arms slightly bent.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells in an arc motion to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement to reduce strain on the joints.
Exhale and bring the dumbbells back to the starting position using the same arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout each rep.

name: Negative Push-Up
instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your elbows slightly tucked in towards your body.
Slowly lower your body towards the ground over a count of 3 to 5 seconds, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Once your chest is close to the ground, either push back up to the starting position or gently rest on the floor before resetting.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Poliquin Press
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back and bring the dumbbells to the sides of your chest.
Plant your feet flat on the floor and keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Pause briefly at the top, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the sides of your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Bench Chest Press
instructions: Anchor the resistance band securely behind a bench or sturdy object at chest height.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, ensuring stability.
Hold the band handles or ends in each hand, positioning your hands at chest level with elbows bent.
Press the bands upward by extending your arms fully, keeping wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the chest muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows, maintaining control of the band tension.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Suspension Chest Fly
instructions: Attach suspension straps to an anchor point above head height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handles with arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Lean forward slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels, and engage your core.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower your body until your chest is in line with your hands, feeling a stretch in your chest muscles.
Reverse the motion by bringing your arms back together in front of you, squeezing your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kneeling Back Rotation Stretch
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees hip-width apart. Sit back onto your heels to stabilize your lower body.
Place your right hand behind your head, keeping your elbow pointed out to the side.
Extend your left arm out in front of you, resting it on the floor for support.
Inhale deeply, then exhale as you rotate your upper body to the right, bringing your right elbow up towards the ceiling.
Hold the stretch for a moment, feeling the rotation in your upper back.
Inhale as you return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.
Perform 5-10 repetitions on each side, focusing on smooth and controlled movements.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, maintaining a stable base.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palm facing inward).
Lie back on the bench, ensuring your back is fully supported and your shoulder blades are retracted.
Position the dumbbell at shoulder height with your elbow bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Press the dumbbell upward by extending your arm until it is fully extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring your arm is straight but not locked out.
Lower the dumbbell slowly back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Resistance Band Push-Up
instructions: Anchor a resistance band around your upper back, holding the ends of the band in each hand.
Assume a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and feet together or slightly apart for stability.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle relative to your torso.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the floor.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand in a doorway with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms to the sides and bend your elbows at a 90-degree angle, forming a 'goalpost' position.
Place your forearms against the door frame, ensuring your elbows are slightly below shoulder height.
Step one foot forward through the doorway, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Gently lean forward until you feel a stretch across your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply throughout.
Slowly return to the starting position and switch feet if desired.

name: Elbow Out Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms and rest your hands on top of your head with your fingers interlaced.
Open your elbows out to the sides so they line up with your head.
Gently draw your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Release slowly and lower your arms.

name: Bench Press With Resistance Band
instructions: Loop a resistance band under the bench frame on each side and attach the ends to the barbell, ensuring equal tension on both sides.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with the band attached to the bar next to each hand.
Unrack the barbell and position it directly above your chest with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly to your chest, maintaining control and keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, engaging your chest and triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining consistent form throughout.

name: Standing Chest Opener
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Interlock your fingers behind your back, palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms gently, lifting them slightly away from your back.
Inhale deeply, expanding your chest as you pull your shoulders back and down.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Release the stretch slowly and return to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Chest Opener
instructions: Kneel on a mat and sit back on your heels with your knees about hip-width apart.
Place your hands behind your head and sit tall.
Bring your elbows together in front of your face, letting your upper back round slightly.
Inhale and open your elbows wide and back as you lift your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the open position for 2 to 3 seconds.
Exhale and bring your elbows back together in front of your face.
Repeat slowly for the planned number of reps.

name: Bent Arm Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand side-on next to a wall or the edge of a doorway, feet hip-width apart.
Raise the arm closest to the wall out to the side to shoulder height and bend the elbow to 90 degrees, hand pointing up.
Place your forearm and palm flat against the wall, with the elbow level with your shoulder.
Rest your other hand on your hip and stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Gently press your chest forward past the arm until you feel a stretch across the chest and the front of the shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, without forcing it or causing pain.
Release, then turn around and repeat with the other arm.

name: One-Arm Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart for better stability.
Place one hand directly under your shoulder while extending the other arm out to the side or behind your back.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending the elbow of the supporting arm until your chest is just above the ground.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then push through your palm to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Floor Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand with an overhand grip, positioning it close to your chest.
Extend your free arm out to the side for balance.
Press the kettlebell upward until your arm is fully extended, keeping your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulder remains stable.
Slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Paused Bench Press
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack above a flat bench. Load it evenly and use collars. Set the safety pins just below the bar path if available.
Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar. Place your feet flat on the floor, slightly behind your knees, and keep them planted throughout the set.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench. Keep your upper back, head and glutes in contact with the bench, with a small natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar evenly, slightly wider than shoulder width. Wrap your thumbs around the bar and keep your wrists stacked over your forearms.
Take a deep breath, brace your torso, and unrack the bar with straight arms. Move the bar until it is balanced over your shoulders.
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest or sternum area. Keep your elbows at a comfortable angle, not flared straight out to the sides.
Let the bar touch your chest lightly and hold it completely still for the planned pause. Maintain full-body tension and do not relax on the bench.
Press the bar up after the pause, driving through your feet and keeping your shoulder blades set. Press the bar slightly back toward the rack until your elbows are locked.

name: Superman Push-Up
instructions: Lie face down with your arms extended straight in front of your head, palms flat on the floor, and your toes tucked under.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body is rigid from head to heels.
Press your hands and toes into the floor and lift your whole body off the ground, keeping your arms extended forward.
Hold briefly at the top with your body in a straight line.
Lower yourself back to the floor under control and repeat.

name: Jack Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
As you push back up to the starting position, jump your feet out to the sides wider than hip-width apart.
Immediately jump your feet back together as you lower into the next push-up repetition.
Continue alternating between push-ups and jumping jack motions for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Bench Press with Chains
instructions: Set up a flat bench and position a barbell with chains attached on a rack at an appropriate height.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the ground and your eyes directly under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, ensuring your wrists are straight and elbows are under the bar.
Unrack the bar by straightening your arms and position it above your chest with elbows locked.
Lower the bar slowly to your chest, allowing the chains to pile on the floor, maintaining control and keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the bar back up explosively to the starting position, lifting more chain links off the ground as you extend your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining form throughout.

name: Finger Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor, but instead of using your palms, balance on your fingertips.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body as you lower yourself towards the ground.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your chest is just above the floor.
Push through your fingertips to raise your body back to the starting position.
Maintain a controlled motion throughout the exercise to avoid injury.

name: Reverse Wrist Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands shoulder-width apart and your fingers pointing back towards your feet.
Slowly lean forward, placing your weight onto your hands while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Keep your wrists under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is close to the ground, keeping your core engaged.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Korean Dip
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself between parallel bars, gripping them firmly with your palms facing inward.
Lift your body off the ground by straightening your arms, ensuring your shoulders are directly above your wrists.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
As you lower into the dip, lean your torso well forward and let your straight legs travel back behind you, so your body tilts at about 45 degrees.
Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping your core engaged and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Return to the starting position by reversing the movement, bringing your legs back under you and pushing up through your arms.

name: Standing Downward Dog
instructions: Stand facing a bench or another stable surface at about hip height, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward at the hips and place your hands on the edge of the surface, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back until your arms and torso form a straight line, roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep your legs straight but not locked, allowing a slight bend in the knees if necessary.
Let your chest sink towards the floor and your head drop between your arms until you feel a stretch in your lats, shoulders and chest.
Hold the position for several breaths, maintaining even breathing.
To release, walk your feet forward and return to standing.

name: Decline Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set a decline bench at a 15-30 degree angle in front of a cable machine.
Attach handles to the low pulleys on both sides of the machine.
Lie down on the decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grab the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward, and position your hands at chest level.
Engage your core and press the handles upward and slightly inward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring tension in the chest muscles.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Open Book Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with the hips and knees bent and the knees stacked.
Extend both arms in front of your chest with palms together.
Keep the knees together and open the top arm in an arc across your body.
Let the upper back rotate and follow the moving hand with your gaze.
Stop within a comfortable range, then return the hand slowly to the other palm.
Repeat, then change sides.

name: Barbell Guillotine Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the racked bar and your feet planted on the floor.
Take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Unrack the bar and hold it on straight arms above your neck and upper chest.
Lower the bar slowly toward the base of your neck, letting your elbows flare out to the sides.
Stop with the bar just above your collarbones without letting it rest on your throat.
Press the bar straight up to full arm extension, keeping it above your neck.
Complete the planned repetitions, then return the bar to the uprights.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight, legs extended, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes, and keep your neck neutral by looking slightly ahead of your hands.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them angled about 30 to 45 degrees from your body.
Push through your palms as forcefully as possible to drive your upper body away from the floor.
Allow your hands to leave the floor briefly, then prepare to absorb the landing with soft elbows.
Land with your hands in the same position, bend your elbows to cushion the impact, and immediately move into the next repetition.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bench Press
instructions: Set a flat bench in a power rack and position the barbell so you can unrack it with nearly straight arms. Use a lighter weight than for a regular bench press and set the safety pins just below the bar path if available.
Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar. Place your feet firmly on the floor, keep your glutes on the bench, and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing toward your face. Keep your hands about shoulder width apart or slightly wider, and wrap your thumbs fully around the bar.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms. Ask a spotter for a lift-off if possible, because the underhand grip can make the unrack less secure.
Unrack the bar and stabilize it above the chest with straight arms.
Lower toward the lower chest, keeping the elbows close to your sides and the wrists supported over the forearms.
Press upward and slightly back until the arms are straight, keeping the upper back on the bench.
After the last repetition, guide the stable bar back onto both rack hooks.

name: Band Standing Chest Press
instructions: Anchor the resistance band securely behind you at chest height, using a stable post or anchor point that will not move.
Stand facing away from the anchor and hold one handle in each hand at chest level, with your elbows bent and slightly behind your torso.
Step forward until the band has light tension, then place your feet about hip-width apart with one foot slightly in front for balance.
Brace the abdomen and keep the torso upright while allowing the shoulder blades to move naturally during the press.
Press both handles forward until your arms are straight in front of your chest, without locking your elbows hard or letting your shoulders rise.
Slowly bend your elbows and return the handles to the starting position, controlling the band as it pulls back.

name: Suspension Chest Press
instructions: Set the suspension straps to mid length and place the handles at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand with palms facing down.
Lean forward until the straps are taut, keeping both feet on the floor. Keep your body aligned from head to heels and brace your abdomen and glutes.
Start with your arms straight in front of your chest, hands slightly wider than shoulder width. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Bend your elbows and slowly lower your chest between your hands. Keep your body rigid and allow your elbows to travel at about a 45 degree angle from your torso.
Lower until your hands are beside your chest or until you reach a comfortable depth with control. Do not let your hips sag or your lower back arch.
Press through the handles to straighten your arms and return to the starting position. Keep the straps under tension throughout the movement.
Choose a more upright body angle for less resistance, or a more horizontal angle for greater resistance.

name: Barbell Wide Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar. Plant your feet firmly on the floor, keep your hips on the bench, and create a small natural arch in your lower back.
Take a grip wider than shoulder width, with your hands placed evenly on the bar. Keep your wrists straight over your forearms and wrap your thumbs around the bar.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench. Keep your chest lifted and brace your core before lifting the bar out of the rack.
Unrack the bar with straight arms and hold it directly above your shoulders. Keep your shoulders firmly supported on the bench.
Lower the bar under control toward the lower to middle part of your chest. Let your elbows travel out to the sides, but do not force them into an extreme flare.
Lightly touch the bar to your chest without bouncing it. Keep your feet planted, hips down, and shoulder blades pulled back.
Press the bar up and slightly back toward the rack, following the same path. Drive through your hands while keeping your wrists stacked over your forearms.
After the last repetition, guide the bar back into the rack with straight arms and make sure both sides are securely racked before releasing your grip.

name: Dumbbell Around the World
instructions: Lie face up on a flat bench with your head on the bench and your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and extend your arms so the dumbbells sit just above your hips.
Brace your core and keep a slight bend in your elbows for the whole set.
Raise the dumbbells together over your chest, keeping your arms almost straight.
Continue the arc and lower the dumbbells behind your head until your arms are roughly in line with your body.
Spread your arms and sweep the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc at about bench height, then down to your hips.
Repeat the circle in the same direction for every rep.

name: Inchworm Push-Up
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and brace your core.
Hinge at your hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees slightly if needed.
Walk your hands forward until you reach a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping your body rigid and your elbows angled slightly back.
Press through your palms to return to the high plank.
Keep your feet in place, walk your hands back toward them and stand up.
Repeat the movement smoothly, keeping your hips from sagging during the plank and push-up.

name: Push-Up Plus
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, arms straight, legs extended and feet about hip-width apart.
Brace your abdomen, squeeze your glutes and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor as in a standard push-up. Keep your elbows angled slightly back rather than flared wide.
Press through your palms to return to the top position with your elbows fully straight.
Without bending your elbows, push the floor away further by spreading your shoulder blades apart and lifting your upper back slightly toward the ceiling.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid letting your hips sag, rise or rotate during the extra shoulder blade movement.
Pause briefly at the top of the shoulder blade protraction, then let your shoulder blades return to neutral and repeat.

name: Planche Dips
instructions: Begin in a planche position on parallel dip bars, arms straight and body parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and maintain a hollow body position to keep your body stable.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower your body towards the ground while keeping your legs elevated and straight.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your elbows do not flare out excessively.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting planche position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Wall Push-Up
instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, with your feet about hip-width apart.
Place your palms flat on the wall at shoulder height, about shoulder-width apart, with your fingers pointing up.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lean your whole body toward the wall, keeping your elbows pointing down and slightly back rather than out to the sides. Your heels can lift off the floor as you lean in.
Pause briefly when your chest is close to the wall.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and push your body back to the upright starting position.
Do the planned number of reps at a slow, steady pace.

name: Hand-Release Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under or slightly wider than your shoulders, legs straight, and feet about hip-width apart.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest to the floor under control by bending your elbows.
Once your chest, thighs, and hips are on the floor, briefly lift both hands off the ground by squeezing your upper back.
Replace both palms in their starting positions and press your body up as one unit until the arms are straight.
Keep your hips from sagging or rising ahead of your chest, then repeat for the required number of repetitions.

name: Push-Up to Side Plank
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, legs straight, feet about hip-width apart, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your neck neutral by looking slightly ahead of your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled push-up. Keep your elbows angled back rather than flared wide.
Press through both palms to return to the high plank position without letting your hips sag or rise.
Shift your weight onto your right hand and turn your chest to the left, pivoting onto the sides of your feet.
Reach your left arm straight toward the ceiling and hold briefly, keeping your hips lifted and your body long and straight.
Return your left hand to the floor, perform the next push-up, then rotate into a side plank on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides.

name: Alternating Punches
instructions: Stand with your feet parallel, knees slightly bent and fists in front of your chest.
Keep your core braced, chest lifted, and chin slightly tucked while looking straight ahead.
Extend one arm straight forward at shoulder height, rotating the fist so the palm faces down at full extension.
Retract the punching hand quickly back to your guard position.
Immediately punch forward with the opposite arm, returning the first hand to guard as the second arm extends.
Continue alternating controlled punches at a steady pace, exhaling with each punch and keeping your shoulders relaxed.

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight as you hang from the bar with your arms fully extended.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and back, then pull your body upwards by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, keeping your chest open and shoulders away from your ears.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Bent Over Row
instructions: Load the bar on the floor, or set it in a rack at mid-thigh height.
Take an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
Pick the bar up the way you start a deadlift: flat back, bar close to your legs. Feet end up hip-width apart, toes forward.
Soften your knees and push your hips back until your torso sits about 15–30° above parallel. That's the starting position: arms straight, bar hanging around mid-shin.
Breathe into your belly, pull your ribs down and brace. Look at the floor about a meter ahead so your head stays in line with your back.
Drive your elbows back toward your hips and pull the bar up along your thighs to your stomach, between your lower ribs and your navel.
In the top position your elbows are behind your torso, roughly 30–45° from your sides, and your shoulder blades are squeezed together. Hold it for a second.
