Lower the bar in 1–2 seconds until your arms are straight again. Your torso, hips and knees stay put, and the plates don't touch the floor.
To finish, bend your knees and set the bar down with a flat back, or stand up and return it to the rack.

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Clip a short straight bar to the low pulley and sit facing the stack, feet on the foot plate, knees clearly bent but never locked.
Grab the bar overhand, hands about shoulder-width apart, and slide back until your arms are straight and the selected plates lift off the stack.
Sit tall on your sit bones, torso vertical, chest up. That's the start: arms long at lower-chest height, shoulder blades spread forward.
Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows straight back along your ribs, upper arms about 15–35° out from your sides.
Finish with the bar on your upper stomach, just below the ribs, and hold a second: elbows behind your torso, shoulder blades squeezed together and down.
Let the bar travel forward over about 2 seconds until your arms are straight. Only your arms and shoulder blades move.
Keep the plates off the stack until the last rep, then bend your knees and set the bar on the foot plate with a flat back.

name: Wide Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit down at the lat pulldown machine and adjust the knee pad to fit snugly against your thighs to prevent your body from lifting during the exercise.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean back slightly at an angle of about 30 degrees while keeping your chest up and core engaged.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by squeezing your shoulder blades together and driving your elbows down and back.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the lats.
Slowly release the bar back to the starting position with controlled movement, fully extending your arms.

name: Cable Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit facing the stack and set the thigh pad so your thighs are locked in, feet flat and knees bent about 90°.
Stand back up and take the bar overhand on the straight part just inside the bends, about one and a half shoulder widths apart, thumbs around it.
Sit down with the bar at arm's length and let your shoulders rise. Chest up, lean back 10–15° from the hips, and keep that angle until the set is done.
Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears, before your elbows bend.
Drive your elbows down and slightly back toward your sides until the bar passes in front of your face and reaches your upper chest, just below the chin.
Pause for a moment with your shoulder blades down and together, then let the bar rise over 2–3 seconds until your arms are straight and you feel a stretch under your armpits.
At the end of the set, let the bar go all the way up (or stand up with it) before you let go, so the plates don't slam into the stack.

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row
instructions: Set a dumbbell beside the front half of a flat bench, on the side you'll train. Any sturdy support at knee height works too.
For a right-arm set, put your left knee and shin on the bench and your left hand flat ahead of the knee, arm straight under your shoulder.
Plant your right foot a little back and out to the side, knee soft. Flat back, torso about parallel to the floor, eyes on the floor just past the bench.
Pick up the dumbbell with your palm facing the bench, fingers hooked around the handle and wrist straight. Let the arm hang under your shoulder, shoulder blade drifting forward.
Pull the shoulder blade toward your spine first, then drive your elbow up and back toward your hip, upper arm brushing your side.
Stop with the dumbbell beside your hip and the elbow just above your back. Hold a second, then lower in about 2 seconds to a full hang.
Finish all reps on this side and set the dumbbell down, then swap knee, hand and arm for the same number on the other side.

name: Chest Supported Machine Row
instructions: Load the same plates on both horns while the handles rest in their start position. The arms move independently, so mismatched plates mean mismatched sides.
Set the seat so the top of the chest pad sits at your breastbone, below the collarbones, with the handles level with your lower chest.
Sit tall with your feet on the foot plate, knees bent about 90°, and lean your chest lightly into the pad.
Take the vertical handles with a neutral grip, hands about shoulder-width apart. If you can't reach them with straight arms, adjust the chest pad.
Start the pull with your shoulder blades: draw them back and down, then drive your elbows back along your sides, about 30–45° from your body.
Row until your elbows pass your torso and your hands reach your lower ribs. Squeeze for a second, chest still on the pad.
Take 2–3 seconds on the return, until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread. Don't let the plates touch down between reps.
At the end of the set, walk the handles back to their resting spot before you let go and stand up.

name: Rope Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown
instructions: Set the pulley at the very top of the column and clip on a triceps rope.
Hold one rope end in each hand just above the knobs, palms facing each other and hands about a fist apart.
Walk back about two steps, until the plates lift with your arms reaching up toward the pulley. Feet hip-width, knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and lean your torso to roughly 30–40° above horizontal. Back flat, head neutral, arms in line with your torso.
Pull your shoulders down, away from your ears, and set a slight elbow bend that stays fixed for the whole set.
Moving only at the shoulders, sweep the rope down in a wide arc to the front of your thighs, just above the knees. Pause a beat.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the rope rise along the same arc, until you feel a stretch under your armpits. Keep the plates off the stack.
When you finish, step toward the column and let the rope ride up before you let go, so the stack doesn't slam.

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an underhand grip, palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground. Engage your core and keep your body straight.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and back, then pull your chest towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar. Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Wide Neutral Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Hang the wide parallel-grip bar on the high pulley; its short end handles sit at right angles to the bar, so your palms face each other.
Lower the thigh pad until it locks your thighs in, feet flat and knees bent about 90°, so you can't rise off the seat.
Stand, take one end handle in each hand and sit down with the bar, the cable hanging just in front of your face.
Start with straight arms and let your shoulders ride up. Sit tall, chest lifted, leaning back only about 10° for the whole set.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears first, then drive your elbows down and in toward your ribs.
Stop with the handles beside your head at shoulder or collarbone height, forearms vertical. The bar passes in front of your face, never behind your neck, so keep your head still.
Pause briefly, shoulder blades down and together, then let the bar rise over 2–3 seconds until your arms are straight and your armpits stretch.
Let go only once your arms are straight again, or stand up with the bar. Dropped at the bottom, it shoots up and slams the stack.

name: Wide Grip Chest Supported Row
aliases: Wide Grip Chest Supported Machine Row
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with your shoulders or upper chest once your chest rests on the pad.
Move the chest pad until you can just reach the handles with straight arms and your shoulder blades drawn forward.
Sit tall, breastbone on the pad and feet on the foot supports, and take the outer horizontal handles overhand with your thumbs wrapped around.
Start each rep by pulling your shoulder blades back, then drive your elbows back and out, about 45–60° from your sides.
Row until your elbows pass your torso and your hands reach your lower chest. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold for a second.
Let the handles go forward over about 2 seconds, until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread. Your chest never leaves the pad.
Finish the set by guiding the handles back to their resting spot instead of letting the stack drop.

name: Chest Supported T-Bar Row
instructions: Load plates onto the horn at the front of the lever while it sits on its stop, evenly if both sides take plates.
If the footplate adjusts, set it so the top edge of the pad meets your lower chest and your shoulders clear the front of the pad.
Step onto the angled footplate with your knees well bent and lie onto the pad, chest and upper stomach supported. Eyes on the floor.
Grip the horizontal handles overhand, thumbs wrapped, hands wider than your shoulders, and lift the lever off its stop with straight arms.
Start each rep from that full reach, shoulder blades spread: pull them back first, then drive your elbows up and out, roughly 60–80° from your sides.
Stop when your hands reach the front edge of the pad at lower-chest height and your elbows are level with your back. Squeeze and hold a second.
Lower over 2–3 seconds until your arms hang straight, and start the next rep just before the plates touch the stop.
When you're done, set the lever down on its stop before you let go or step off the footplate.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your arms straight and let the dumbbells hang naturally.
Inhale deeply, then exhale as you lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, ensuring you feel the tension in your trapezius muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Neutral Grip Incline Bench Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lie face down on the bench, ensuring your chest is supported and feet are firmly planted on the floor.
Extend your arms fully downward, allowing the dumbbells to hang naturally.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing up) at shoulder width.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips to lower your torso until it's almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Engage your core and keep your head in line with your spine.
Pull the barbell towards your lower ribcage, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Assisted Pull-Up
instructions: Adjust the weight on the assisted pull-up machine to provide the necessary support.
Stand on the platform or kneel on the pad, depending on the machine design.
Grasp the pull-up handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight as you begin the movement.
Pull yourself upward by driving your elbows down and back until your chin is above the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lever High Row
instructions: Set the seat so you reach the handles with almost straight arms while your chest is on the pad.
If you have to shrug or rise off the seat to get them, raise it.
Lock your thighs under the roller pad just above the knees, feet flat on the floor and knees bent about 90°.
Your lower chest rests on the vertical pad and stays there until the set is over.
Take the vertical handles with a neutral grip, palms facing, about shoulder-width apart. Wrists straight: your hands are just hooks.
Begin each rep by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears, before your elbows bend.
Drive your elbows down and back toward your back pockets, so the handles sweep in an arc from above your forehead to your upper chest.
At the finish, your hands are at upper-chest height and your elbows just behind your torso, about 30–45° from your sides. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds on the way back, until your arms are long and your shoulder blades spread. After the last rep, ride the handles to the start before you let go.

name: Seated Cable Low Row Neutral Grip
instructions: Clip a close neutral-grip handle (V-bar) to the cable, sit facing the stack and put your feet on the foot plate, knees softly bent.
Hold both grips with your palms facing each other and slide back until your arms are straight and the plates you're using lift off.
Sit tall with your torso vertical, chest up, ribs down and lower back neutral. The cable runs roughly level from the pulley to your hands.
Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows straight back along your ribs, upper arms about 20–30° from your sides.
Bring the handle to your upper stomach, just below the ribcage, elbows ending just behind your torso. Hold that squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the handle forward until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades glide forward into a lat stretch.
Keep the plates off the stack until the set ends, then bend your knees and lower the handle to the foot plate with a flat back.

name: Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown
instructions: Clip a short straight bar to the high pulley and pick a light weight to start. A lat bar held shoulder-width also works.
Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width and walk back a long step or two, until the plates stay up with your arms reaching forward.
Feet hip-width and knees soft, push your hips back until your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal. Back flat, head between your arms.
Reach your arms forward and up in line with your torso. Set a small bend in the elbows and keep that angle for the whole set.
Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears, before the bar moves.
Sweep the bar in an arc, moving only at the shoulders, until your arms are near vertical and the bar is in front of your knees.
Hold a second, then let the bar rise over about 2 seconds along the same arc until you feel a stretch under your armpits.
When the set is done, walk toward the tower and let the plates settle on the stack before you let go of the bar.

name: Cable Neutral Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the cable machine so that your feet are flat on the floor and your thighs are secured under the pads.
Attach a V-bar to the high pulley of the cable machine.
Sit down facing the machine and grasp the V-bar with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lean back slightly at an angle of about 70 degrees while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Begin the movement by pulling the V-bar down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the lats.
Slowly return to the starting position with controlled motion, fully extending your arms overhead.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Lat Pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and knee pad on the cable machine to ensure stability during the exercise.
Attach a single handle to the high pulley of the cable machine.
Sit down facing the machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pad.
Grasp the handle with one hand using a neutral or supinated grip, keeping your arm fully extended.
Lean slightly back, maintaining a straight spine and engaging your core muscles.
Exhale as you pull the handle down towards your chest, leading with your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade down and back.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the latissimus dorsi.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position, allowing your arm to fully extend without losing tension in your back.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Seated Cable Wide Grip Row
instructions: Clip a long straight bar (a lat pulldown bar works) to the cable of the seated row station.
Sit facing the stack, feet on the foot plate and knees bent to about 90°, so you can sit tall without your hips tipping back.
Grip the bar overhand near its ends, about 1.5 shoulder widths apart, and sit back until your arms are straight and the plates lift.
Set your torso vertical: chest up, ribs down, lower back neutral. The bar is in front of your chest at shoulder height, the cable roughly level.
Draw your shoulder blades back, then drive your elbows out and back, upper arms about 60–80° from your sides.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, just under the pecs, so your elbows finish behind your torso. Hold that squeeze for a second.
Return the bar over 2–3 seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread. Your torso stays still.
At the end of the set, bend your knees and bring the bar back to the foot plate with a flat back before you let go.

name: One-Arm Chest Supported Row Machine
instructions: Adjust the seat and chest pad of the row machine to fit your body size, ensuring your chest is firmly supported.
Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the floor and your chest against the pad.
Grasp the handle with one hand, keeping your arm fully extended.
Engage your core and pull the handle towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow.
Pause briefly when the handle is close to your body, ensuring maximum contraction in the back muscles.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: T-Bar Bent Over Row
instructions: Load the desired weight onto the T-bar or barbell.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Hinge at the hips to bend forward, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grip the handles of the T-bar or barbell with both hands, palms facing each other.
Engage your core and pull the weight towards your lower chest by retracting your shoulder blades.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your back muscles.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position while maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar with neutral grip handles.
Jump or step up to grab the handles with palms facing each other, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, keeping elbows close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner until arms are fully extended again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lat Pulldown Machine
instructions: Load the same plates on both horns. The two arms move independently, so uneven loading shows up as one handle lagging behind.
Set the seat so you can just reach the handles with straight arms while your thighs sit snug under the pad. Feet flat, knees bent about 90°.
Take one angled handle in each hand, overhand with your thumbs wrapped around, then sit tall with your chest up. On many machines you half-stand to reach them.
Start every rep by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears. Only then drive your elbows down and slightly back toward your sides.
Follow the machine's arc down past your face to chin or collarbone height. Both handles stay level, your head stays neutral and your torso doesn't move.
Pause for a beat with your shoulder blades down and back, then let the handles rise over 2–3 seconds until your arms are straight and you feel a stretch under your armpits.
To finish, ride the handles all the way up before you let go. Released at the bottom, the loaded levers snap up past your face.

name: Cable Reverse Grip Pulldown
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Sit on the bench or seat with your feet flat on the floor, securing your thighs under the support pads.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you), hands shoulder-width apart.
Lean slightly back at the hips while keeping your chest up and core engaged.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position, maintaining control of the weight throughout.

name: One-Arm Cable Row
instructions: Slide the pulley down to chest height for someone sitting on the floor (about knee height when you stand) and clip on a single D-handle.
Sit on the floor facing the column, legs straight, feet together and heels down. Scoot back until your arm is straight and the plates still hang above the stack.
Hold the handle with a neutral grip, thumb up and wrist straight. Sit tall on your sit bones and rest the free hand on the floor by your hip or on your thigh.
Start from a long reach: the working shoulder travels toward the pulley, your torso leans forward about 15–20° and turns slightly away from that arm.
You'll feel a stretch down the side of your back.
Drive the elbow straight back along your ribs while your torso comes up to vertical. The cable should run roughly level.
Stop with the handle beside your lower ribs and the elbow just behind your body. Pull the shoulder blade back and down and hold a second; your chest turns only slightly toward the working side.
Let the arm travel forward over about 2 seconds until it's straight and the shoulder reaches again. The plates don't touch down between reps.
Do every rep on one arm, then switch, starting with your weaker side. Never let go of the handle at full reach, or it snaps back to the column; pass it to your other hand.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
instructions: Begin by securely attaching a weight to your body using a dip belt or weighted vest.
Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and retract your shoulder blades to stabilize your body.
Initiate the pull by driving your elbows downwards and pulling your chin above the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Low Row
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the handle with one hand, palm facing inward.
Step back slightly to create tension in the cable, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Hinge forward slightly at the hips while maintaining a straight back.
Pull the handle towards your torso, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the peak of the movement.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position under control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Pull-Up Wide Grip
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands positioned wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back to stabilize your upper body.
Initiate the pull by driving your elbows down towards your sides, lifting your body until your chin is above the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner back to the starting position with arms fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Bench Dumbbell Wide Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your feet.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly on the ground.
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Pull the dumbbells up with your elbows flared out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Pullover
instructions: Set the seat so the middle of your shoulder is level with the pivot, the axis the arm levers turn around.
Sit with your hips all the way back, your back and head on the reclined pad and your feet flat. Buckle the belt if there is one.
Bring the bar into the start position, with the foot lever if your machine has one, and rest the backs of your upper arms, just above the elbows, on the pads.
Lay your hands on the crossbar overhand, about shoulder-width apart, with a light grip. Your elbows stay bent at about 90° until the set is over.
Start in the stretch: upper arms beside your head, elbows pointing up and back, ribs down and lower back flat on the pad.
Breathe out and drive your elbows forward and down into the pads in a wide arc until they reach your sides and the bar is in front of your upper stomach.
Hold a second with your shoulders down, then let the levers carry your arms back overhead over 2–3 seconds until the sides of your back stretch.
At the end of the set, take the load on the foot lever, or let the weight settle slowly, before you slide your arms off the pads.

name: One-Arm High Row Cable
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand, palm facing down, and step back to create tension in the cable.
Bend slightly at the knees and hinge forward at the hips while keeping your back straight.
Pull the handle towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow.
Pause briefly when your hand reaches your side, ensuring your elbow is close to your body.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Cable Close Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit facing the stack and set the thigh pad so your legs are locked in, feet flat on the floor and knees bent about 90°.
Stand up and grab the bar overhand in the middle, one hand on each side of the cable clamp, about a fist's width apart.
Sit back down with the bar at arm's length and let your shoulders rise. Chest up, lean back only 5–10° from the hips.
Start the pull by drawing your shoulders down, then drive your elbows down; they travel in front of your ribs and slightly out.
Bring the bar straight down close to your face until it reaches your chin, a few centimeters above the collarbones, without changing your torso angle.
Pause briefly with your shoulder blades down, then let the bar rise over 2–3 seconds until your arms are fully straight.
At the end of the set, let go only when the bar is back overhead or you've stood up with it, so the stack doesn't slam.

name: Barbell Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms fully extended and your back straight throughout the movement.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as possible, squeezing the trapezius muscles at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a brief moment before slowly lowering the shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and avoiding any jerking motions.

name: Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position a loaded barbell on the floor in front of you.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the ground, maintaining a neutral spine.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Engage your core and retract your shoulder blades.
Lift the barbell explosively from the floor to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower the barbell back to the floor under control.
Reset your position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Seated Row
instructions: Sit on the seat of the row machine with your chest against the pad and your feet firmly planted on the footrests.
Grasp one handle with one hand, keeping your arm extended and your palm facing inward.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
Pull the handle towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Pause briefly when the handle reaches your side, ensuring maximum contraction of the back muscles.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Sit on the side of a flat bench with the dumbbell standing on end on your thigh.
Lie back so only your shoulder blades rest across the pad, with your head at its edge.
Walk your feet out until your knees are bent about 90° and your hips are level with your torso. Feet flat, about hip-width.
Cup the inside of the top plate with both palms, fingers spread and thumbs around the handle, so the dumbbell hangs straight down.
Press it up over your shoulders with a soft bend in the elbows. Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down.
Breathe in and take 2–3 seconds to lower the dumbbell over your face and behind your head. The elbow angle doesn't change.
Stop when your upper arms are beside your ears, or sooner if your ribs start to lift. Your hands end up about level with the bench.
Drive your upper arms toward your hips to bring the weight back along the same arc, breathing out as your arms reach vertical. After the last rep, lower it to your chest before you sit up.

name: Dumbbell Incline Chest Supported Lateral Raises
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly planted on the ground.
Extend your arms down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Engage your core and lift the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length below your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Straight-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
instructions: Clip a single handle to the high pulley and pick a light weight; one arm moves far less than two arms on a bar.
Hold the handle like a ski pole: thumb toward the pulley, palm facing in, wrist straight. No need to squeeze it hard.
Face the tower with the pulley in line with your shoulder and step back until the stack lifts, arm straight and hand at head height.
Stand tall with feet hip-width, knees soft and ribs down, and rest your free hand on your hip.
Pull the shoulder down first, then sweep the straight arm down in front of you until your hand is beside your thigh.
Hold a second, then take 2–3 seconds to let the arm rise along the same arc until you feel a stretch under your armpit.
Do every rep on one arm, then switch. Start with your weaker side and match its reps on the other.

name: Dumbbell Kelso Shrugs
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms hanging straight down.
Engage your core and keep your neck in a neutral position.
Exhale as you retract your shoulder blades, lifting the dumbbells towards your hips.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the trapezius muscles.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Low Cable Seated Row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet firmly placed on the foot platform and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the handle with one hand using a neutral grip, keeping your arm fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
Pull the handle towards your waist by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow.
Pause briefly when the handle reaches your torso, ensuring maximum contraction in the back muscles.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position, maintaining control over the weight.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: One-Arm Landmine Bent Over Row
instructions: Position a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely wedge one end into a corner.
Stand perpendicular to the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees slightly, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grasp the end of the barbell with one hand, palm facing inward.
Brace your core and pull the barbell towards your hip by driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Smith Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to a height just below your waist.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, positioning yourself under the bar.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unlock the bar by rotating it forward, keeping your arms straight.
Lift your shoulders towards your ears in a shrugging motion, squeezing the trapezius muscles at the top.
Hold the contraction briefly, then slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Adjust the footrests so that the straps are secure over the balls of your feet.
Sit on the sliding seat and grasp the handle with both hands using an overhand grip.
Start with your knees bent and your shins vertical, leaning slightly forward at the hips.
Push off with your legs while keeping your arms straight until they are fully extended.
Once your legs are straight, lean back slightly and pull the handle towards your lower ribs.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position.

name: Incline Chest Supported Barbell Row
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to about 45 degrees (30–45 works) and lay a loaded barbell on the floor under the top of the backrest.
Straddle the seat and lean onto the backrest, chest and stomach on the pad, its top edge at your upper chest, chin just above it.
Plant both feet with your knees bent, one foot a little further back. Your hips sit at the bottom of the backrest, not on the seat.
Take an overhand grip about shoulder-width, hands just outside the pad, and lift the bar a couple of inches so it hangs from straight arms.
Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows back and up, about 30–45 degrees from your sides.
Pull the bar almost straight up until it touches the underside of the pad at your lower chest or upper stomach, and hold for a second.
Lower it over 1–2 seconds to straight arms and let your shoulder blades spread. The plates stay off the floor between reps.
Set the bar down on the floor at the end of the set before you climb off the bench.

name: Cable Seated Row Neutral Grip
instructions: Clip the neutral-grip row bar to the cable: the curved bar with an upright handle at each end, about shoulder-width apart.
Sit facing the stack with your feet on the foot plate and your knees softly bent, roughly 15–30°.
Take the handles palms-in and slide back on the seat until your arms are straight and your plates hang clear of the stack.
Sit tall: torso vertical, chest up, ribs down. The handles start at about lower-chest height and the cable runs close to level.
Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows behind your torso with your upper arms about 20–40° out from your sides.
Stop the handles at your lower ribs, just above your stomach, and hold for a second with your shoulder blades squeezed together and slightly down.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the handles forward until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread. The plates never touch down between reps.
When the set is done, bend your knees and bring the bar back to the foot plate with a flat back, then let go.

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at waist height or use a Smith machine bar.
Lie under the bar with your chest directly below it and extend your legs straight out.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and glutes to keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest towards the bar by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause at the top when your chest nearly touches the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Close Grip Landmine Row
instructions: Position a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely anchor one end in a corner.
Stand over the barbell with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Bend at the hips to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, maintaining a neutral spine.
Grip the barbell close to the weighted end with both hands using an overhand grip.
Engage your core and pull the barbell towards your lower chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Assisted Pull Up
instructions: Attach a resistance band securely to a pull-up bar.
Place one foot or knee into the loop of the band to reduce your body weight.
Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, leading with your chest.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Lever High Row
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the lever machine so that the handle is at shoulder level when seated.
Sit down and brace your feet firmly on the footrest or floor.
Grasp the handle with one hand using a neutral grip (palm facing inward).
Keep your chest pressed against the pad and maintain a straight back.
Pull the handle towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction while squeezing your back muscles.
Slowly extend your arm to return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Negative Pull-Up
instructions: Start by using a box or step to position yourself at the top of a pull-up bar with your chin above the bar.
Grip the bar with your hands shoulder-width apart, using an overhand grip.
Engage your core and maintain a straight body alignment.
Slowly lower yourself in a controlled manner, taking 3-5 seconds to descend until your arms are fully extended.
Step back onto the box or step and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
instructions: Set the safety stops a few centimeters below the bottom of your rep, around knee height, and the hooks at mid-thigh.
Stand behind the bar with your feet hip-width, placed so the bar will hang straight under your shoulders once you lean over.
Grip the bar overhand with your thumbs wrapped, hands just outside your thighs at shoulder width or a little wider.
Unhook the bar, soften your knees and push your hips back until your torso leans about 45° (lower only if your back stays flat).
Let the bar hang at arm's length and brace your stomach, neck in line and eyes on the floor just ahead of your feet.
Pull your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows up and back, about 30–45° from your sides, until the bar touches just under your ribs.
Squeeze for a second at the top, then lower over about 2 seconds to straight arms, your head at the same height every rep.
Re-hook the bar only after the last rep, with your back still flat.

name: Cable Wide Grip Behind Neck Pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height so your feet are flat on the floor and your thighs are secured under the pad.
Attach a wide grip bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Sit down facing the machine and grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Lean slightly forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the bar down behind your neck by squeezing your shoulder blades together and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly when the bar reaches just below ear level.
Slowly return to the starting position with controlled movement, fully extending your arms.

name: Gorilla Row
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
Keep your back straight and engage your core throughout the movement.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders with palms facing each other.
Row one dumbbell towards your hip by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Seal Row
aliases: Prone dumbbell row on a bench
instructions: Raise a flat bench on solid blocks or plates until your arms can hang straight with the dumbbells off the floor. It must not wobble.
Set the dumbbells on the floor under the head end of the bench, one per side, before you lie down.
Lie face down with your upper chest at the front edge and your chin just over it, legs straight and feet together.
Take the dumbbells with a neutral grip, palms facing the bench, arms hanging straight under your shoulders and shoulder blades spread.
Pull your shoulder blades toward your spine first, then drive both elbows up and back toward your hips, upper arms 20–30° from your sides.
Stop with the dumbbells level with the pad beside your lower ribs, elbows above your back. Hold one second, chest and chin down.
Take about 2 seconds to lower to a full hang and let your shoulder blades slide apart before the next pull.
Set the dumbbells on the floor first when the set is done, then slide off the bench.

name: One-Arm Cable Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
instructions: Set the cable machine to a high position and attach a single handle.
Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot flat on the floor, ensuring your torso is upright.
Grasp the handle with your arm fully extended overhead, palm facing forward.
Engage your core and pull the handle down towards your shoulder, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lat.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Lever Low Row
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your chest is comfortably against the chest pad and your feet are flat on the floor.
Select an appropriate weight on the machine that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and grasp the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Begin by pulling the handles towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position, fully extending your arms while maintaining control of the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seal Row
instructions: Set up a flat bench elevated on blocks or platforms to allow full range of motion for the weights.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet planted firmly on the ground.
Grip the weights (dumbbells or barbell) with an overhand grip, arms fully extended towards the floor.
Engage your core and keep your body stable throughout the movement.
Pull the weights towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the upper back muscles.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips to lean forward, keeping your back straight and torso almost parallel to the floor.
Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of you, keeping your arms perpendicular to the floor.
Engage your core and pull the barbell towards your lower chest by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the rear delts.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lever Back Extension
instructions: Adjust the lever machine to fit your height, ensuring that the pads rest comfortably on your upper thighs.
Position yourself face down on the machine with your feet secured under the footpads.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
Engage your core and slowly lower your upper body towards the floor by bending at the hips.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring you do not round your back.
Raise your upper body back to the starting position by extending at the hips until your body forms a straight line.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kneeling Cable Lat Pulldown
instructions: Attach a wide grip bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Kneel on the floor facing the machine, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully above your head without locking your elbows.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by squeezing your shoulder blades together and engaging your lats.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with controlled motion, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Narrow Grip Australian Pull-Up With Rings
instructions: Set up a pair of gymnastic rings at waist height.
Stand facing the rings and grab them with a narrow, neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward until your body is in a straight line from head to heels, leaning back with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight body position.
Pull your chest towards the rings by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your chest is near the rings.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Shrug
instructions: Stand facing a low pulley cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Attach a straight bar or rope handle to the low pulley.
Grasp the handle with both hands, using an overhand grip, and stand upright with your arms fully extended.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Lift your shoulders towards your ears in a shrugging motion, squeezing your trapezius muscles at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment before slowly lowering your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Close Grip Pull Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with a close grip, palms facing away from you, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground. Engage your core and keep your body straight.
Initiate the pull by squeezing your shoulder blades together and pulling your elbows down towards your sides.
Continue to pull until your chin is above the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Suspension Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension straps to hang at waist height.
Stand facing the anchor point and grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Lean back until your body is at an angle, keeping your feet shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest towards the handles by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Kettlebell Row
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance and hold a kettlebell in one hand, with the opposite foot forward.
Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in your knees and rest your free hand on your front knee for support.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Let the kettlebell hang at arm's length below your shoulder.
Pull the kettlebell towards your hip by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

name: Machine Shrugs
instructions: Load the shrug machine and stand between the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly to grip the handles, then stand up straight holding them with your arms fully extended.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears in a shrugging motion, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Seated Supine Grip Row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet securely placed on the foot platform and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the straight bar attachment with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you lean slightly forward at the hips.
Pull the bar towards your lower abdomen by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly when the bar reaches your torso, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position, maintaining control of the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Front Lever
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lats to lift your legs and torso until your body is parallel to the ground.
Keep your arms straight and maintain a hollow body position with your shoulders retracted.
Hold the position for as long as possible while maintaining control and proper form.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position.

name: Neutral Grip Weighted Pull-Up
instructions: Begin by attaching the desired weight to a dip belt or using a weighted vest for added resistance.
Grasp the pull-up bar with a neutral grip, meaning your palms face each other, and your hands are positioned shoulder-width apart on parallel handles.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight, engaging your core to maintain stability.
Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the level of your hands or the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form throughout.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Bent Over Scapula Row
instructions: Stand beside a flat bench and place your non-working hand and the same-side knee on the bench for support, keeping the working-side foot firmly on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in the working hand with a neutral grip and let the arm hang straight beneath the shoulder.
Set your torso nearly parallel to the floor, keep your spine neutral, brace your core, and keep your neck in line with your back.
Begin with the shoulder blade relaxed slightly forward, allowing the dumbbell to hang without bending the elbow.
Exhale and pull the working shoulder blade back toward the spine, moving the dumbbell slightly upward while keeping the arm straight and the torso still.
Pause briefly when the shoulder blade is fully retracted without shrugging the shoulder toward the ear or rotating the torso.
Inhale and slowly allow the shoulder blade to move forward to the starting position under control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before changing sides.

name: Barbell Bent Over Row From Pin
instructions: Set the safety pins in a power rack to knee height or slightly below.
Place the barbell on the pins and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your back straight and core engaged as you lift the barbell off the pins.
Pull the barbell towards your lower chest or upper abdomen, keeping elbows close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell back to the pins in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Front Lever Pull-Up
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip, palms facing forward.
Engage your core and lats to lift your legs and torso into a horizontal position, parallel to the ground.
Once in the front lever position, initiate the pull-up by bending your elbows and pulling your chest towards the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting front lever position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining the front lever position.

name: Band Bent Over Lat Pulldown
instructions: Loop the band around something solid at waist-to-chest height: a rack upright, a post or a door anchor at the middle hinge of a closed door.
Hold one end in each hand with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width, and walk back until the band is taut with your arms straight.
Feet hip to shoulder width, knees bent: push your hips back until your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal, back flat and head in line.
Reach your arms toward the anchor so they line up with your torso, upper arms beside your head. You should feel a stretch under your armpits.
Start the pull by drawing your shoulders down away from your ears, then drive your elbows down and back toward your sides.
Stop when your elbows are beside your ribs and your hands sit just below your chin. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and together for a second.
Let your arms travel forward over 2–3 seconds until straight, band still taut. After the last rep, walk toward the anchor before standing up.

name: Suspension Inverted Row
instructions: Attach the suspension straps to a secure anchor point above head height.
Adjust the straps so that the handles are at waist height.
Stand facing the anchor point and grab the handles with an overhand grip.
Walk your feet forward until your body is at a desired angle, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your body rigid.
Pull your chest towards the handles by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell behind your back using an overhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down behind you throughout the movement.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Lift your shoulders as high as possible towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your trapezius muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shrugs
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms fully extended by your sides.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your trapezius muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Standing Side Lat Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Raise your right arm overhead, reaching towards the ceiling.
Lean your torso gently to the left side, feeling the stretch along the right side of your body.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply throughout.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

name: One-Arm Band Kneeling Lat Pulldown
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a high anchor point, ensuring it is secure.
Kneel on one knee directly under the anchor point, with your other foot planted firmly on the ground for stability.
Grasp the band handle with one hand, palm facing forward, and extend your arm fully overhead.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
Pull the band down by driving your elbow towards your side, keeping your shoulder blade retracted.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your latissimus dorsi.
Slowly return to the starting position by extending your arm back overhead.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Australian Pull-Up Underhand Grip
instructions: Set a bar at waist height on a squat rack or Smith machine.
Lie under the bar with your chest directly beneath it.
Grab the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs out in front of you, keeping your heels on the ground.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest towards the bar by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your chest touches the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.

name: Rings Pull-Up
instructions: Adjust the rings to a height where you can hang with your arms fully extended without your feet touching the ground.
Grip the rings with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and hang with your body straight, engaging your core.
Initiate the movement by retracting your shoulder blades and pulling your chest towards the rings.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the level of the rings.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Alternate Renegade Row
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands gripping dumbbells placed shoulder-width apart. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging or rotating.
Row one dumbbell towards your hip by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the rowing motion with the opposite arm while maintaining plank form.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Neck Curl
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your head hanging off the edge.
Place a small weight plate or resistance band across your forehead.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your body stable throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl your chin towards your chest by flexing your neck.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the neck muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, avoiding any sudden movements.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band High Anchor Wide Row
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at a high point above your head level.
Stand facing the anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band handles with an overhand grip, arms extended forward.
Step back to create tension in the band while maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Pull the band towards your chest by driving your elbows out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction, ensuring full scapular retraction.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kettlebell Renegade Row
instructions: Start in a high plank position with a kettlebell in each hand, wrists aligned under your shoulders, and feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart for stability.
Engage your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Shift your weight slightly to one side and row the kettlebell on the opposite side towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower the kettlebell back to the ground with control.
Repeat the movement on the other side, alternating rows while maintaining plank position throughout.

name: Trap Bar Shrugs
instructions: Stand inside the trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and grasp the handles with a neutral grip.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you stand tall with the trap bar.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders up towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Pullover with Legs Raised
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a bench, ensuring your head and neck are supported.
Raise your legs so they are perpendicular to the floor, keeping them straight and together.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended above your chest. Your palms should be facing upward, gripping the dumbbell securely.
Inhale deeply and slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement to reduce strain on the joints.
Exhale and bring the dumbbell back to the starting position using your chest and lat muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control and form.

name: Barbell Incline Wide Grip Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Position yourself face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grasp a barbell with a wide overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Start with your arms fully extended and the barbell hanging straight down.
Pull the barbell towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulder blades are fully contracted.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Neck Side Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Gently tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear towards your shoulder without lifting the shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull along the side of your neck.
Return your head to the neutral position and repeat on the opposite side.
Perform 2-3 sets on each side.

name: Cable Thibaudeau Kayak Row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and grip the bar overhand, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Step back until the cable is tight with your arms straight out in front of you at about shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your elbows straight with only a slight bend.
Pull the bar down in an arc toward one hip, turning your torso toward that side.
Pause briefly when the bar reaches your thigh, then let it rise back to shoulder height under control.
On the next rep, pull the bar down toward the other hip and keep alternating sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Prone Swimmer
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended straight overhead and legs fully extended.
Keep your forehead gently resting on the ground to maintain a neutral neck position.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your torso throughout the movement.
Simultaneously lift your right arm and left leg off the ground, keeping them straight.
Lower them back to the starting position and immediately lift your left arm and right leg.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled manner, simulating a swimming motion.
Perform the exercise for a set number of repetitions or time duration.

name: Dip Shrugs
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself on parallel bars, supporting your body weight with your arms fully extended.
Keep your elbows straight and your body upright, engaging your core for stability.
Keeping your arms straight, let your body sink slowly until your shoulders rise toward your ears.
Press the bars down to push your shoulders away from your ears and lift your body, and hold the top briefly.
Lower back into the sunken position with control, without bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Pulldown Behind Neck
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a high anchor point.
Stand or sit facing the anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the band with both hands, palms facing forward, and arms extended overhead.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Pull the band down behind your neck by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring tension in the back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Ski Ergometer
instructions: Adjust the resistance level on the SkiErg to match your fitness level.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the machine.
Grip the handles firmly with both hands, keeping your arms extended overhead.
Engage your core and slightly bend your knees.
Pull the handles down in a smooth motion, bending at the hips and knees while keeping your back straight.
Drive through your hips and legs as you pull the handles down past your thighs.
Return to the starting position by extending your arms overhead while maintaining control.
Repeat the motion for the desired number of repetitions or time duration.

name: Flag
instructions: Find a sturdy vertical pole or similar structure that can support your weight.
Place your lower hand in an overhand grip at about waist height on the pole.
Position your upper hand in an underhand grip above your head on the pole.
Engage your core and pull with your upper hand while pushing with your lower hand to lift your body off the ground.
Keep your body straight and horizontal to the ground, maintaining tension throughout your core and legs.
Hold the position for as long as possible, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.

name: Back Lever
instructions: Begin by hanging from a bar or gymnastic rings with a pronated grip (palms facing away).
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight body position.
Slowly tuck your knees to your chest to transition into an inverted hang.
Extend your legs back and downwards while keeping your body straight, aiming to achieve a horizontal position.
Hold the position as long as possible, maintaining tension throughout your entire body.
To exit, tuck your knees back to your chest and return to the starting hang position.

name: Wide Grip Rear Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and retract your shoulder blades to stabilize your upper body.
Move your head slightly forward and pull your body up behind the bar, leading with your elbows pointing down and out.
Continue pulling until the bar is level with the base of your neck, behind your head.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Yates Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up, until your torso is at about 45 degrees to the floor.
Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of you with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull the barbell towards your lower abdomen by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows stay close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with controlled movement, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.

name: Seated Cable Flexion Row
instructions: Attach a straight bar or close-grip handle to the low cable pulley and select a light-to-moderate load that allows smooth, controlled movement.
Sit facing the cable machine with your feet braced firmly against the foot platform, knees slightly bent, and arms extended toward the handle.
Begin with your torso slightly flexed forward from the hips and upper back, allowing your shoulder blades to move apart while keeping your neck neutral.
Initiate the pull by driving your elbows back and drawing the handle toward your lower abdomen.
As you pull, gradually extend your spine to bring your torso upright, keeping your chest open and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Pause briefly with the handle close to your abdomen, elbows behind your body, and shoulders kept down away from your ears.
Return the handle slowly by extending your arms and allowing your torso to flex forward in a controlled manner, without rounding aggressively or losing tension in the cable.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, avoiding jerking, excessive lower-back movement, or using momentum to pull the weight.

name: Assisted Chin-Up
instructions: Set the assistance weight so you can complete the set with controlled form. More selected weight provides more assistance.
Grip the central bar underhand, with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Kneel on the moving pad while holding the bar and begin with straight arms.
Brace your stomach and keep your legs still. Start by pulling your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull your chest upward by driving your elbows down toward your sides. Keep your torso tall and avoid swinging or kicking.
Pull until your chin passes the bar without reaching forward with your neck.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again and your shoulders remain controlled. Do not drop into the bottom position.

name: Kettlebell Gorilla Row
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet. Stand with a wide stance, toes slightly turned out.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees until you can reach both kettlebell handles. Keep your chest open, spine neutral, and neck in line with your back.
Grip both handles with your arms straight. Brace your core and keep your weight balanced through your whole feet.
Pull one kettlebell toward the side of your ribcage by driving your elbow back. Keep your shoulder down and avoid twisting your torso.
Lower the kettlebell under control until your arm is straight again.
Row the other kettlebell to your ribcage in the same way.
Continue alternating sides while maintaining a stable hip hinge, a flat back, and controlled movement. Finish the set by placing both kettlebells on the floor before standing up.

name: Band Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band with your feet about hip-width apart and take one handle in each hand, palms facing each other.
Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back until your torso is at about 45 degrees to the floor or lower.
Keep your back flat, brace your core and let your arms hang straight down in front of your shins.
Drive your elbows back close to your sides and pull the handles to your hips.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and hold for a moment.
Lower the handles until your arms are straight again, keeping your torso at the same angle.
Do all the reps of the set without standing up between them.

name: Cable External Rotation
instructions: Set the pulley at about elbow height and attach a single handle.
Stand side-on to the machine with the working arm farther from the pulley, so the cable pulls your hand across your body.
Hold the handle with a neutral grip, thumb up. Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and keep it lightly pressed against your side.
Start with your forearm across your abdomen. Stand tall with your shoulders down and relaxed.
Keeping the elbow at your side, rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, as far as you can without moving the elbow.
Pause briefly, then return the forearm slowly across your abdomen.
Finish all reps on one side, then turn around and work the other arm.

name: Inverted Shrug
instructions: Grip the handles of a dip station and carefully turn upside down so your head points to the floor and your legs are tucked above the handles.
Let your body hang with straight arms beside your hips, so your shoulders are pulled down away from your ears.
Brace your core and keep your legs still to avoid swinging.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, lifting your body slightly without bending your elbows.
Hold the top position for a moment and squeeze your upper traps.
Lower yourself slowly until your shoulders are fully stretched away from your ears again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then come down carefully, feet first.

name: Table Inverted Row
instructions: Use a heavy, stable table that cannot slide, tip, or move.
Lie under the table with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Reach up and grip the table edge with both hands about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abdomen and lift your hips to align your trunk and thighs.
Pull your chest toward the table by driving your elbows down and back.
Pause when your chest is close to the table edge and your elbows are bent.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight, while keeping your body rigid and your hips from dropping.

name: L Pull-Up
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lift your legs to form a 90-degree angle at the hips, creating an 'L' shape with your body.
Keep your legs straight and parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
Pull yourself up by engaging your back and biceps until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner while maintaining the L-sit position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Standing External Rotation
instructions: Place a loop band around both wrists and stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Bend your elbows to 90 degrees and keep them lightly pressed against your sides.
Start with your forearms in front of your abdomen. Keep your shoulders down and relaxed and your wrists straight.
Keeping your elbows at your sides, rotate both forearms outward at the same time, away from your body, as far as you can without moving the elbows.
Pause briefly with the band stretched across the front of your body.
Bring your forearms back slowly in front of your abdomen, controlling the pull of the band.

name: Dumbbell Bird Dog Row
instructions: Place a dumbbell on the floor beside the bench and position yourself with one knee and the opposite hand supported on the bench.
Hold the dumbbell in your free hand and extend the free leg, opposite the rowing arm, straight behind you.
Brace your core, keep your spine neutral, square your hips and shoulders toward the floor, and let the dumbbell hang directly below your shoulder.
Pull the dumbbell toward the side of your rib cage by driving your elbow up and back, keeping your upper arm close to your torso.
Pause briefly at the top of the row while squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine without rotating your torso.
Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control until your arm is fully extended, maintaining the raised-leg position and a stable torso.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch the supporting hand and knee, dumbbell hand, and extended leg to train the other side.

name: Weighted Lying Neck Extension
instructions: Use a flat bench and a very light weight plate. Place a folded towel between the plate and the back of your head for comfort.
