Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and your head hanging just beyond the end of the bench. Keep your body still and your neck relaxed.
Hold the weight plate securely against the back of your head with both hands. Start with your chin slightly tucked, not forced toward your chest.
Raise your head slowly by extending your neck until it is in line with your upper back. Keep your chest on the bench and do not arch your lower back.
Pause briefly, then slowly lower your head back to the starting position under control.
Keep the movement small and smooth. Do not use momentum, twist your head, or let the weight shift.

name: Tuck Front Lever
instructions: Set a pull-up bar high enough that your feet cannot touch the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip and hang with straight arms.
Set your shoulders by pulling them down away from your ears and slightly back. Keep your elbows locked and your chest open.
Tighten your abdomen and bring your knees toward your chest. Keep your knees bent and close together.
Lean your torso back while pressing down on the bar with straight arms. Lift your hips until your body is nearly parallel to the floor.
Hold the tuck position with your back rounded slightly, hips lifted, and knees close to your chest. Keep your shoulders depressed and do not let your elbows bend.
To finish, lower your hips under control back to a dead hang, then step down safely.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
instructions: Start on all fours with your knees under your hips and hands under your shoulders.
Keep one hand in place and slide the other forward along the floor.
Keep the reaching elbow straight and your hips above your knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch along the reaching side.
Breathe slowly while holding a comfortable stretch.
Slide your hand back under your shoulder and repeat on the other side.

name: Prone Lat Pulldown
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight and your toes tucked under.
Lift your chest slightly off the floor and reach both arms forward past your head, hands off the floor.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs, as if pulling a bar to your upper chest.
Finish with your elbows by your sides and your hands near your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades down and together.
Hold for a moment while keeping your chest lifted.
Reach your arms forward again until they are straight.
Keep your chest and arms off the floor for the whole set, then lower down.

name: Archer Pull-Up
instructions: Grip a secure pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip and enough clearance for your feet.
Hang with straight arms, legs together or slightly in front of you, and brace your abdomen to limit swinging.
Set your shoulders by pulling them down away from your ears and keeping your chest lifted.
Pull your body toward one hand, bending that elbow while allowing the opposite arm to straighten out to the side along the bar.
Continue until your chest is close to the working hand or as high as you can control. Keep your shoulders level and avoid twisting your torso excessively.
Lower slowly back to a centered dead hang, controlling the movement through both arms.
Repeat toward the other hand. Alternate sides each repetition, or complete the planned repetitions on one side before switching.

name: Head Harness Neck Extension
instructions: Inspect the head harness, chain and weight attachment. Use a very light load the first time, because the neck muscles fatigue quickly.
Fit the harness securely and attach a light plate to its chain. Stand with your knees bent and feet planted.
Hinge forward at your hips and support your hands on your knees, leaving the plate free to move.
Start with your head lowered slightly, allowing your chin to move toward your chest without forcing the stretch.
Raise your lowered head slowly using the muscles at the back of your neck, within a comfortable range you can control and without moving your torso.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your head slowly to the starting position.

name: Sled Rope Pull
instructions: Load the sled with an appropriate amount of weight and attach a secure training rope to the sled’s front attachment point.
Stand facing the sled with your feet about shoulder-width apart, holding the rope firmly with both hands and keeping enough distance to maintain tension in the rope.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and bend your knees slightly into an athletic stance with a neutral spine.
Pull the rope toward you with one hand, then reach forward with the other and continue alternating.
After each pull, reach forward under control to take another grip on the rope while maintaining a stable torso and avoiding excessive rounding of the lower back.
Continue pulling hand over hand until the sled reaches you, keeping the rope taut and using smooth, powerful pulls rather than jerking the load.

name: Prone W Raise
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Bend your elbows and place your hands on the floor beside your head, palms down, so your arms form a W.
Keep your elbows out to the sides, a little below shoulder height.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your elbows, forearms and hands off the floor at the same time.
Hold the top for a second, then lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.

name: Reverse Snow Angel
instructions: Lie face down with your legs straight and together, arms by your sides and palms facing the floor.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes and lift your chest, arms and legs a few centimetres off the floor.
Sweep your straight arms out to the sides and up into a Y above your head, keeping them just above the floor.
At the same time, open your straight legs wide without letting them touch the floor.
Pause briefly in the Y position with your shoulders pulled away from your ears.
Sweep your arms back to your hips along the same arc as you bring your legs together.
Keep your chest, arms and legs lifted for the whole set, then lower to the floor.

name: Sleeper Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with the shoulder you want to stretch on the bottom. Keep your head supported and your torso stable.
Bring the bottom arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the forearm pointing upward.
Keep the bottom shoulder blade gently pulled back and down. Do not let the shoulder roll forward toward your ear.
Use your top hand to hold the wrist or forearm of the bottom arm.
Slowly guide the bottom forearm down toward the floor, creating a gentle stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Hold the stretch without forcing the arm down. Breathe normally, then slowly release and repeat on the other side if needed. Stop if you feel pinching or pain in the front or top of the shoulder.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Keep your arms slightly bent at the elbows and maintain this angle throughout the exercise.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slowly raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring you feel tension in your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, feet flat on the floor, and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and keep your back pressed against the bench.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead, without locking your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Set the pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle.
Grasp the handle with the hand furthest from the machine, keeping your arm straight and close to your body.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Slowly lift the handle out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring you feel the contraction in your shoulder.
Lower the handle back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
instructions: Begin by setting up a barbell on a rack at about chest height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the barbell and hold it at shoulder height with your elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms until they are fully extended but not locked out.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Face Pull
instructions: Clip a rope to one pulley of a cable station and set it at forehead height or a notch above, not at the top.
Hold one rope end in each hand just inside the stoppers, overhand: knuckles up, palms down, hands close together, wrists straight.
Face the pulley and walk back until your arms are straight at face height and the plates lift off the stack.
Set your feet hip-width apart, one foot half a step ahead, knees soft.
Stand tall, chest up, ribs down; your legs and torso stay put from here on.
Draw your shoulders down, then pull the rope toward your face with your elbows leading out to the sides at shoulder height.
In the last third, pull the rope ends apart so your hands finish beside your head at eye level, forearms vertical, knuckles up and back.
Pause for a second with the middle of the rope in front of your nose, elbows bent about 90° and shoulder blades squeezed.
Take 2–3 seconds to straighten your arms, plates still off the stack. After the last rep, step in before you set the weight down.

name: Machine Reverse Flyes
instructions: Set the seat so your hands are level with your shoulders when you sit tall. The arms should travel at shoulder height, not above it.
If there's a start-position adjuster at the top of the machine, set the handles in front of your chest about a hand's width apart.
Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad, feet flat on the floor and knees bent to about 90°.
Take the short horizontal handles with an overhand grip, palms down. Your arms point straight ahead with a slight bend in the elbows.
Keep that elbow angle fixed and sweep both arms out and back in a wide arc, as if pushing the handles apart rather than pulling.
Stop when your arms line up with your shoulders and your body makes a T. Squeeze your shoulder blades, shoulders down, and hold a second.
Let the handles travel back along the same arc over 2–3 seconds until they almost meet. The plates only touch down after your last rep.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at shoulder level or slightly below when seated.
Sit down with your back firmly against the backrest and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Engage your core and keep your chest up throughout the exercise.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your back straight and engage your core for stability.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows are slightly higher than your wrists.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys at the top, well above your head. Hold the bare cable ends or clip a single D-handle to each.
Cross the cables: right hand on the left pulley's cable, left hand on the right one. Thumbs up, elbows slightly bent.
Face the machine from the middle and step back until the cables are taut, wrists crossed in front of your chest at shoulder height.
Set your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, knees soft, ribs down and glutes lightly squeezed so the high cables can't tip you forward.
Keeping that elbow angle fixed, sweep your arms out and back at shoulder height, as if the backs of your hands push the cables apart.
Stop once your arms line up with your shoulders and your body forms a T. Hold a second, shoulder blades together, shoulders low.
Take 2–3 seconds to follow the same arc back until your wrists cross again. The plates stay off the stack between reps.
When the set is done, bring your hands back to the crossed start and lower the stacks before letting go, so the cables don't snap back.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the cable machine to the lowest setting and attach a single handle.
Stand with your side to the cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with the hand furthest from the machine, keeping your arm straight but not locked.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Lift your arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height, keeping your palm facing down.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Use the pop-pin under the seat to set your shoulder joints level with the round pivots the lever arms turn on, just behind your shoulders.
Sit tall with your feet flat, a little wider than your hips. If your machine has a chest or back pad, stay in contact with it.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees, upper arms by your sides and forearms pointing forward, with the outside of each forearm against its pad.
Hold the handles lightly with your thumbs up. They only keep your arms in place; your forearms do the pushing.
Drive your elbows out and up in a wide arc. The 90-degree bend stays, and your forearms keep pointing forward.
Stop when your elbows are level with your shoulders and your upper arms about parallel to the floor. Hold for a second, shoulders down.
Lower over 2–3 seconds until your upper arms are back at your sides, and stop just before the plates touch down.

name: Smith Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust the bench to an upright position and set it under the Smith machine bar.
Sit on the bench with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and position it just above your upper chest.
Exhale and press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Inhale as you lower the bar back to the starting position, just above your upper chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your thighs.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the dumbbells in front of you with a slight bend in the elbows until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring not to swing or use momentum.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Arnold Dumbbell Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing your body.
Keep your feet flat on the floor, core engaged, and back pressed against the bench.
Begin by rotating your palms outward as you press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring your elbows are not locked.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position while rotating your palms back to face your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Trap Y Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to about 30-45 degrees and lie face down on it with your chest supported and your feet on the floor.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand and let your arms hang straight down below your shoulders.
Turn your palms to face each other and keep your neck in line with your spine.
Engage your core and raise your arms in a Y shape until they are in line with your ears.
Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Barbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, ensuring your feet are flat on the floor for stability.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it at shoulder height with your elbows bent and aligned under your wrists.
Engage your core and press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Front Raise
instructions: Attach a straight bar or single handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing away from the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, and grasp the handle with an overhand grip.
Position your arms straight down in front of your thighs with a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift the handle forward and upward until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring tension in the shoulders.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend at the hips, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent, until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders with palms facing each other.
Engage your core and keep your neck in line with your spine.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Incline T Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Engage your core and keep your head in a neutral position.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a 'T' shape.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Face Pull
instructions: Clip a rope to one pulley of a cable station and set it level with your face as you sit on the floor, usually mid-column.
Take one rope end in each hand with an overhand grip: knuckles up, palms down, hands close together, wrists straight.
Sit facing the machine, legs out in front, knees slightly bent, heels down. Scoot back until your arms are straight at face height and the plates lift.
Sit tall with your chest up and lean back about 10–20°. The cable should now run level to the pulley; that lean stays put until the set is done.
Set your shoulders down, then pull the rope toward your face with your elbows leading out to the sides at shoulder height.
Split the rope as it nears your face. Your hands finish beside your head at eye level, forearms vertical, knuckles up and back; hold a second with your shoulder blades squeezed.
Take 2–3 seconds to straighten your arms, plates still off the stack. After the last rep, scoot forward to set the weight down, then let go.

name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, toes forward or turned out slightly, knees straight but not locked back.
Curl the dumbbells to your shoulders. With heavy ones, rest them on your thighs and kick them up with a knee, one at a time.
Hold them beside your head at ear or jaw height, palms facing forward and handles in one line, each wrist stacked straight over its elbow.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down so your torso stays vertical, eyes straight ahead.
Press both dumbbells up together and slightly inward, keeping your forearms vertical as they rise.
Lock your elbows with the dumbbells almost touching above the crown of your head, upper arms by your ears. Hold for a moment.
Take about 2 seconds to lower back to ear level with your elbows just below your shoulders. Press again without bouncing.
To finish, bring the dumbbells down to your shoulders, then to your thighs, before you put them on the floor.

name: Barbell Shoulder Grip Upright Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the barbell vertically by leading with your elbows, keeping it close to your body.
Raise the barbell until it reaches just below your chin, ensuring elbows are higher than your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Set the machine handles to the rear delt position and adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Sit sideways on the seat with the side of your non-working arm against the pad, and hold the pad with that hand.
With your working arm, grab the handle in front of you with a neutral grip, arm extended at shoulder height.
With a slight bend in your elbow, pull the handle out to the side and back in a wide arc until your arm is in line with your shoulder.
Pause briefly, squeezing the back of your shoulder.
Slowly let the handle return to the front under control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Seated Bent Over Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest slightly above your knees.
Let your arms hang down naturally with a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lever Seated Hammer Grip Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at shoulder level when seated.
Sit down and firmly plant your feet on the ground, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Engage your core and press the handles upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended but not locked.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring not to shrug your shoulders.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Upright Row
instructions: Set a low cable pulley with a straight bar attachment and select a light to moderate weight that allows controlled movement.
Stand facing the cable with your feet about hip-width apart, grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder width, and let the bar rest in front of your thighs.
Brace your abdominal muscles, keep your chest lifted, maintain a neutral spine, and keep a slight bend in your knees.
Pull the bar upward close to your body by driving your elbows out and up, keeping your wrists straight and your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Raise the bar only to upper-chest or collarbone height, or stop earlier if you feel shoulder discomfort; keep your elbows no higher than is comfortable.
Pause briefly at the top while maintaining control and avoiding leaning back or shrugging excessively.
Lower the bar slowly along the same path until your arms are fully extended in front of your thighs, keeping tension on the cable.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, using a pain-free range of motion and reducing the weight if you cannot keep the bar close to your body.

name: Cable Supinated Face Pull
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing up.
Step back slightly to create tension in the cable, keeping arms extended.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Pull the rope towards your face, leading with your elbows and keeping them high.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull.
Pause briefly when the rope is near your face, ensuring full contraction of the rear deltoids.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Pike Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a downward dog position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart.
Walk your feet closer to your hands to form an inverted V shape with your body.
Keep your legs straight and your hips high, ensuring your back is flat.
Lower your head towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them pointed outwards.
Stop when your head is just above the ground, then push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral neck position throughout the movement.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over High Row
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend forward at the hips until your torso is slightly above parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Let your arms hang down with a slight bend in the elbows, palms facing each other.
Exhale and pull the dumbbells up towards your torso by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the rear delts.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Press
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Engage your core to maintain a stable posture throughout the movement.
Press one dumbbell overhead by extending your arm fully, keeping the other dumbbell at shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position while simultaneously pressing the other dumbbell overhead.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Plate Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions.
Keep your arms straight but not locked, and hold the plate in front of your thighs.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees to stabilize your body.
Inhale and slowly lift the plate upward in a controlled motion until it reaches shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulders are engaged.
Exhale as you lower the plate back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Incline Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit sideways on the bench with your non-working side against the backrest.
Hold a dumbbell in your working hand with a neutral grip, arm hanging down naturally.
Keep your core engaged and maintain a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and switch arms.

name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the pulley to the lowest notch and clip on a single D-handle.
Stand side-on to the column with your feet together right at its base, so the pulley sits next to your near foot.
With your near hand, grab a fixed upright of the frame at about head height. Never hold the moving pulley carriage or the cable.
Take the handle in your far hand. The cable runs diagonally across the front of your thighs, not behind you.
Lean away until your support arm is almost straight and your body forms one line from feet to head, about 15–20° off vertical.
Pull the working shoulder down, then raise the arm out to the side in a wide arc, elbow slightly bent and leading.
Stop when your upper arm is roughly parallel to the floor and your palm faces down. Hips and support arm stay where they are.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower back in front of your hip without letting the plates touch. Do all your reps on one side, then switch.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip.
Keep your core engaged and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Position your working arm slightly bent at the elbow, with the dumbbell resting against your outer thigh.
Exhale as you raise the dumbbell to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your wrist is in line with your shoulder.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: One-Arm Landmine Kneeling Shoulder Press
instructions: Slide one end of a barbell into the landmine pivot (or a towel-wrapped corner), load the free end and put a pad down for your knees.
From half-kneeling, bring the bar end to the front of your working shoulder, then lower the other knee: both knees down, hip-width apart, facing the plate.
Wrap your whole hand around the tip of the sleeve beyond the plate, palm turned in. The bar sits deep in your palm, wrist straight.
Point the elbow down in front of your ribs with the bar end between collarbone and chin. Rest your free hand on your stomach.
Squeeze your glutes until your hips are straight: shoulders over hips over knees, thighs vertical, ribs pulled down.
Press up and forward along the bar's arc until your elbow is straight and your hand sits just above and in front of your head.
At the top, let your shoulder blade reach up and forward around the ribs while your chest stays square to the bar.
Lower it back to the front of your shoulder in about 2 seconds, without bouncing.
To finish, go back to half-kneeling to switch hands or set the bar down. Never drop it from the top.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Front Raise
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your arms straight but not locked, and position the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Raise one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your palm facing down.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Powell Raise
instructions: Lie on your side on a flat bench with your whole body supported and your bottom hand on the floor for balance.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand and let it hang down in front of your chest.
Keep your core engaged and your body stable throughout the movement.
Slowly raise the dumbbell in an arc until your arm points straight up toward the ceiling, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring you feel the contraction in your rear deltoid.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: One-Arm Cable Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Set the cable pulley to shoulder height and attach a single handle.
Stand sideways to the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the handle with your outside hand, keeping your arm slightly bent.
Step away from the machine to create tension in the cable.
Engage your core and keep your torso stable throughout the movement.
Pull the handle across your body in a reverse fly motion, focusing on squeezing your rear delt.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the rear deltoid.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: To work your right arm, rest your left knee and shin on a flat bench, knee under your hip, foot hanging off the end.
Plant your left hand flat on the bench just ahead of your shoulder, arm straight.
Set your right foot on the floor beside the bench, a little back, knee soft. Flat back, torso about parallel to the floor, eyes on the bench just past your hand.
Pick up the dumbbell with an overhand grip: handle across your body, palm facing your feet, knuckles toward your head.
Let the arm hang straight under the shoulder.
Lead with the elbow, driving it up and out to the side, away from your ribs. The forearm stays vertical and the dumbbell rises beside the bench toward your chest line, not your hip.
Stop when your upper arm is level with your back and the elbow is bent about 90°. Pull the shoulder blade toward your spine without shrugging and hold for 1–2 seconds.
Lower over about 2 seconds to a straight arm, letting the shoulder blade slide forward a little so you feel a stretch across the back of the shoulder.
Finish all your reps on the right, then mirror the setup and do the same number with your left arm.

name: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral T Raise
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly on the ground.
Extend your arms downward, allowing them to hang naturally with a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage your core and keep your head aligned with your spine.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Behind Neck Shoulder Press
instructions: Set up a barbell on a squat rack at about shoulder height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell with a pronated grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the barbell and position it behind your neck, resting it on your upper traps.
Engage your core, keep your chest up, and ensure your back is straight.
Press the barbell upward in a controlled motion until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position behind your neck.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Cuban Rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip and your other hand on your hip.
Raise the working arm out to the side until the elbow is at shoulder height, bent to 90 degrees with the forearm pointing down.
Rotate your shoulder to bring the forearm up until it points to the ceiling, keeping the elbow in place.
Pause briefly at the top with the forearm vertical.
Slowly rotate back down to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Hold a slam ball with both hands in front of you.
Engage your core and lift the ball overhead by extending your arms fully.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as you lift the ball for added power.
Forcefully slam the ball down to the ground in front of you by using your core and arms.
Catch the ball on the rebound or pick it up if it doesn't bounce.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Wide Grip Upright Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the barbell vertically along your body, leading with your elbows until it reaches chest level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows are higher than your wrists.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Landmine Standing Shoulder Press
instructions: Position a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely wedge one end into a corner.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the barbell with one hand at shoulder height, palm facing inward.
Engage your core and keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
Press the barbell upward by extending your arm fully, ensuring your elbow does not lock out.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side before switching to the other arm.

name: Barbell Narrow Grip Upright Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands positioned close together.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the barbell vertically along your body, leading with your elbows until they are at shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows are higher than your wrists.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length in front of you, palms facing your body.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the dumbbells vertically by bending your elbows, keeping them higher than your forearms.
Continue lifting until the dumbbells reach chest level or slightly below your chin.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows are pointing outwards.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Hammer Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your arms fully extended at your sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
Raise one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height while keeping your palm facing inward.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Simultaneously, raise the opposite dumbbell to shoulder height as you lower the first one.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Standing Cuban Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a pair of dumbbells with an overhand grip.
Let the dumbbells hang by your thighs with your palms facing your body.
Pull the dumbbells up, leading with your elbows, until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your elbows in place, rotate your forearms up and back until the dumbbells are above your elbows.
From this position, press the dumbbells overhead by extending your arms fully.
Slowly reverse each step to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms straight but not locked, and engage your core for stability.
Exhale and lift the barbell forward and upward until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.

name: Banded Face Pull
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a stable anchor point at chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the ends of the band with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step back until there is tension in the band, arms extended in front of you.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Pull the band towards your face, leading with your elbows and keeping them high.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Alternate Bent Over Dumbbell Reverse Fly
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Hinge at the hips to bend forward until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Let your arms hang down naturally with a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage your core and lift one dumbbell out to the side, keeping your elbow slightly bent, until it reaches shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position while simultaneously lifting the opposite dumbbell.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Chest Supported Lateral T Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to an angle greater than 45 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms hanging straight down.
Engage your core and retract your shoulder blades slightly.
Raise your arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a 'T' shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, focusing on squeezing the rear delts.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your arm fully, keeping your wrist straight.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring your arm is in line with your ear.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: One-Arm Landmine Half Kneeling Shoulder Press
instructions: Begin by setting up a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely in a corner.
Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot flat on the ground in front of you, forming a 90-degree angle at both knees.
Hold the end of the barbell with the hand on the same side as your kneeling leg, keeping your core engaged and torso upright.
Press the barbell upward and slightly forward until your arm is fully extended, keeping your wrist straight and elbow slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Cable Y Raise
instructions: Set the cable machine to a low pulley position and attach single handles to each side.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
Step back slightly to create tension in the cables, keeping your arms straight and at your sides.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Raise your arms diagonally upward and outward in a Y shape until they are at shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Handstand Hold
instructions: Start in a standing position facing a wall.
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the ground about 6-12 inches from the wall.
Kick up one leg at a time to bring your feet to the wall, achieving an inverted position.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from hands to feet.
Keep your head neutral, looking slightly between your hands.
Hold this position for the desired duration, focusing on balance and control.
To exit, gently lower one leg at a time back to the ground.

name: Band Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your feet.
Hold the ends of the band in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and maintain an upright posture.
Press the bands overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring your arms are straight but not locked.
Slowly lower the bands back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Arm Circles
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms hanging straight by your sides.
Keeping your arms straight, lift them forward and up to start a large circle.
Continue the circle over your head, then back and down to your sides, through the full comfortable range of the shoulder.
Complete the desired number of circles in this direction.
Reverse the direction, moving the arms back, up, forward and down.
Keep the motion smooth and controlled throughout the exercise.

name: Barbell Push Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Position the barbell at shoulder height, resting on your upper chest and front deltoids.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Slightly bend your knees to initiate a dip, then explosively extend your legs to drive the barbell upward.
As the barbell passes your head, fully extend your arms overhead.
Control the descent of the barbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your back to a cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
Attach a single handle to the low pulley and set the appropriate weight.
Grasp the handle with one hand, palm facing down, and step forward slightly to create tension in the cable.
Keep your arm straight but not locked, and maintain a slight bend in your elbow.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Slowly raise the handle in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arm extended.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the shoulder muscle.
Lower the handle back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Kettlebell Around the Head Rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands in front of you at chest level.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Lift the kettlebell over your head, starting to rotate it around your head in a clockwise direction.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled, ensuring the kettlebell stays close to your head.
Complete the rotation by bringing the kettlebell back to the starting position in front of your chest.
Repeat the movement in a counterclockwise direction.
Perform the desired number of repetitions for each direction.

name: Lying Cable Face Pull
instructions: Clip a rope to the top pulley of a cable column (a lat pulldown station works).
Set a flat bench lengthwise in front, one end against the column.
Lie face up with your head at the column end so the rope hangs straight down over your face. Knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
Reach up and take one rope end in each hand just above the stoppers: palms facing each other, thumbs toward the pulley, wrists straight.
Start with your arms straight up above your shoulders and the plates lifted off the stack. If they touch down, slide the bench or use a higher pulley.
Press your shoulders down, away from your ears, then pull the rope toward your forehead as your elbows bend and travel out to the sides, down toward the floor.
As the rope reaches your face, pull the ends apart until your hands sit beside your temples, upper arms level with your shoulders and elbows bent about 90°.
Squeeze your shoulder blades into the bench for a second, then take 2–3 seconds to return along the same path to straight arms, plates still off the stack.
After the last rep, let the stack down with your arms straight before you let go or sit up. Let go early and the rope whips up past your face.

name: Lying Cross Lateral Cable Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys of a cable crossover to the lowest position and attach a single handle to each.
Lie on your back on the floor between the pulleys, with your shoulders in line with the cables.
Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, so the cables cross over your body.
Start with your arms straight down in front of your hips, hands crossed and elbows slightly bent.
Keeping your arms close to the floor, sweep them out to the sides in a wide arc until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly, then slowly bring your arms back to the crossed start position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Shoulder External Rotation
instructions: Sit tall on a flat bench and put your working-side foot up on the bench beside your hip, so that knee rises high.
Keep the other foot flat on the floor and rest your free hand on that knee.
Hold a light dumbbell overhand and rest the back of your upper arm, just above the elbow, on the raised knee. Shoulder down and back.
Your elbow, bent to 90 degrees, sits at or just below shoulder height, and the forearm hangs in front of your stomach.
Keeping the elbow on the knee, turn at the shoulder so the forearm swings forward and up like a windshield wiper.
Stop when the forearm is vertical and the dumbbell is beside your head, palm facing forward. Hold for a second or two.
Take about 2 seconds to lower until the forearm points down again.
After the last rep, put the other foot up on the bench and switch the dumbbell to the other hand.

name: Smith Seated Behind Neck Press
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the Smith machine so that the barbell is at shoulder level when seated.
Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width with your palms facing forward.
Unrack the bar by pushing it up slightly and moving it forward to clear the hooks.
Lower the bar slowly behind your head until it is just above your shoulders.
Press the bar back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms but avoiding locking your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Powell Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie on your side on the bench, resting on your lower forearm with your legs extended for balance.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with a neutral grip, letting it hang in front of your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and brace your core.
Raise the dumbbell up and back in an arc until your arm points straight up over your shoulder.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back in front of your chest with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

name: Handstand Push-Up
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself in a handstand against a wall, with your hands shoulder-width apart and fingers spread for stability.
Ensure your body is in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core to maintain balance.
Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body, until your head nearly touches the ground.
Press through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the movement and focus on using your shoulder and tricep muscles.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Supported Bent Over Lateral Raise
instructions: Start by standing beside a bench or stable surface with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, palm facing inward.
Bend at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Place your non-working hand on the bench for support.
With a slight bend in your elbow, raise the dumbbell laterally to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Dumbbell Poliquin Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing in.
Brace your core and keep your back straight throughout the exercise.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees and raise your upper arms out to the sides until your elbows reach shoulder height.
At the top, straighten your arms out to the sides until they are fully extended and parallel to the floor.
Keeping your arms straight, slowly lower the dumbbells back to your sides.
Bend your elbows again and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Seated Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the cable machine to the lowest setting and attach a single handle.
Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor.
Lean slightly forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Grab the handle with one hand using a neutral grip, palm facing inward.
Start with your arm extended in front of you, slightly below shoulder height.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm to the side and slightly back until it is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, focusing on squeezing the rear deltoid.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position under control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions and switch arms.

name: Seated Shoulder Press Neutral Grip
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, ensuring your feet are flat on the floor and your back is straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at shoulder height.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and keep your elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, maintaining control.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Pike Push-Up On Bench
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself in front of a bench. Place your feet on the bench and your hands on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your hands back towards the bench until your body forms an inverted V shape, with your hips elevated and head pointing downwards.
Keep your legs straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lower your head towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them slightly flared out.
Pause briefly when your head is close to the floor, then push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slightly bend your knees to initiate a small dip.
Explosively extend your legs while simultaneously pressing the dumbbells overhead.
Fully extend your arms at the top of the movement without locking your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height while controlling the descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Cuban Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Position your upper arms parallel to the floor, with forearms pointing forward.
Rotate your shoulders externally to bring the dumbbells up, aligning your forearms vertically.
Press the dumbbells overhead by extending your arms fully.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position by reversing the motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Shoulder Press Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Press the dumbbell overhead by extending your elbow until your arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arm is straight but not locked.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Side Lying External Rotation
instructions: Lie on your side with the arm you want to exercise on top and bent at a 90-degree angle at the elbow, resting against your side.
Keep your elbow tucked close to your body throughout the movement to isolate the shoulder muscles.
Hold a lightweight dumbbell or resistance band in your top hand, allowing your forearm to rest across your abdomen.
Slowly rotate your forearm upward, lifting the dumbbell or band away from your body while keeping your elbow fixed in place.
Raise your forearm until it is approximately perpendicular to your torso or as far as comfortable without pain.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower your forearm back to the starting position with control, avoiding any sudden movements.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise with the other arm to ensure balanced shoulder strength.

name: Lateral to Front Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet between hip and shoulder width, knees soft, a dumbbell hanging beside each thigh and palms facing in.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and set a slight bend in your elbows. That angle stays the same until the last rep.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, elbows leading, palms turning to face down.
Without letting them dip, sweep both arms forward in a wide arc at shoulder height until they point straight ahead, about shoulder width apart.
Lower the dumbbells straight down in front of you, taking 2 to 3 seconds to reach the front of your thighs.
Let them drift back to your sides, palms in, and start the next rep without a bounce. Set them down after the last one.

name: Half Kneeling Shoulder Dumbbell Press
instructions: Begin in a half-kneeling position with your right knee on the ground and left foot flat in front of you, forming a 90-degree angle at both knees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Engage your core to maintain stability and keep your torso upright.
Press both dumbbells overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch the kneeling leg on the next set.

name: Weighted Woodchopper
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight (dumbbell or medicine ball) with both hands.
Start with the weight positioned near one shoulder, keeping your arms slightly bent.
Engage your core and rotate your torso as you bring the weight diagonally across your body towards the opposite hip.
Allow your hips and knees to pivot naturally as you perform the movement.
Reverse the motion, bringing the weight back to the starting position near your shoulder.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Static Front Hold
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold a weight (plate, dumbbell, kettlebell or medicine ball) with both hands in front of your thighs.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your torso stays upright.
Keeping your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows, raise the weight in front of you to shoulder height.
Hold the weight at shoulder height for the set time, keeping your shoulders down and breathing steadily.
Lower the weight slowly back to your thighs.

name: Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a kettlebell between your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the kettlebell with one hand, keeping your back straight.
Drive through your heels to lift the kettlebell off the ground, extending your hips and knees explosively.
As the kettlebell rises, pull it close to your body and rotate your wrist to bring it to shoulder height in a rack position.
Once stabilized, dip slightly by bending your knees and then drive through your legs to press the kettlebell overhead.
Lock out your arm at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbow is straight and bicep is close to your ear.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position at your shoulder before returning it to the ground with control.

name: Plate Bus Driver
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent swaying.
Rotate the plate to the left, as if turning a steering wheel, until your right hand is higher than your left.
Return to the starting position and then rotate the plate to the right until your left hand is higher than your right.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled manner for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Bent Over Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the cable machine to a low pulley position and attach a single handle.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing away from the machine.
Bend at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the handle with one hand, allowing your arm to hang straight down.
Engage your core and keep your knees slightly bent for stability.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blade.
Slowly lower the arm back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Band Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of a resistance band under your feet.
Hold one end of the band in each hand, arms at your sides with palms facing inward.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows as you raise your arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulders are not shrugged.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Landmine Lateral Raise
instructions: Position a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely anchor one end in a corner.
Stand perpendicular to the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the end of the barbell with one hand, keeping your arm straight and at your side.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Lift the barbell out to the side and up in a wide arc until your arm is overhead, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Cable Incline Y Raise Back Supported
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 30-45 degree angle and place it in front of a cable machine with both pulleys set low.
Attach single handle attachments to each cable pulley.
Sit on the bench facing the cable machine, with your back supported against the incline pad.
Grab each handle with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Start with your arms extended downward in front of you, maintaining a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise your arms upward and outward in a Y shape until they are in line with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lu Raises
instructions: Hold a light plate in each hand (1.25–5 kg) upright by its inner edge, fingers hooked through the center hole. Light dumbbells held thumbs forward work the same way.
Stand tall with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and knees soft, plates together in front of your thighs, faces pointing forward.
Pull your ribs down, squeeze your glutes and unlock your elbows slightly. That elbow angle stays the same until the set is over.
Sweep both arms out to the sides in one wide arc, thumbs leading, in line with your body or slightly in front. No pause at shoulder height.
Keep going until your arms are vertical, plates side by side overhead and a few inches apart so they don't clash. Hold one second without leaning back.
Lower along the same arc over 2–3 seconds, stop just short of your thighs and start the next rep from a dead stop.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand between your legs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips to lower the dumbbell towards the floor.
Explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling the dumbbell upward close to your body.
As the dumbbell reaches shoulder height, quickly rotate your elbow under it and extend your arm overhead.
Lock out your arm at the top position, keeping your core engaged and body stable.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to the appropriate height, at about mid-thigh level.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
Unlock the bar from the safety catches and let it hang in front of your thighs.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lift the bar vertically along your body by driving your elbows upward and outward.
Continue lifting until your elbows are at shoulder height or slightly above.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows are higher than your wrists.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Turkish Get Up
instructions: Lie on your back with your right leg bent and foot flat on the floor. Extend your left leg straight out.
Hold a kettlebell in your right hand with your arm extended towards the ceiling. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Press through your right foot and roll onto your left hip and forearm.
Push up onto your left hand, keeping the kettlebell stable overhead.
Lift your hips off the ground by pressing through your right foot and left hand.
Sweep your left leg back into a kneeling position under your body.
Align your torso upright by adjusting your kneeling position.
Stand up by driving through your right foot to come to a standing position with the kettlebell overhead.
Reverse the steps to return to the starting position.

name: Tsunami Overhead Press
instructions: Begin by setting up the Tsunami Bar on a squat rack at shoulder height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip.
Unrack the bar and step back, keeping your core engaged and feet firmly planted.
Position the bar at shoulder level with your elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press the bar overhead by extending your arms fully, ensuring your head moves slightly forward as the bar passes your face.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bird Dog Plank
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core muscles to maintain stability.
Simultaneously lift your right arm and left leg, keeping them straight and parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for a few seconds while maintaining balance.
Return your right arm and left leg to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left arm and right leg.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Wall Angel
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart, and heels about 6 inches away from the wall.
Ensure your lower back is flat against the wall by engaging your core and slightly tucking your pelvis.
Raise your arms to shoulder height and bend your elbows at 90 degrees, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Press your entire arm, from fingertips to elbows, against the wall.
Slowly slide your arms upward along the wall while maintaining contact with the wall. Stop when you feel any discomfort or if your arms lose contact with the wall.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly slide your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form throughout.

name: Plate Front Raise Drive
instructions: Pick a plate you can grip firmly by the rim. Stand tall with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, knees soft and ribs down.
Hold the plate at 3 and 9 o'clock, palms facing each other and fingers wrapped around the edge, and let it rest flat in front of your thighs.
With your arms almost straight, raise the plate in an arc for about 2 seconds until your hands reach shoulder height. It tips upright on the way and ends up facing you.
Turn the plate a quarter turn to your left, like a steering wheel: your right hand goes over the top and your left hand drops to the bottom. Come back to the center.
Now a quarter turn to the right with the left hand on top, and back to the center. Belly button and chest keep pointing straight ahead, and you keep breathing.
Lower the plate in 2-3 seconds until it lies flat in front of your thighs again. One raise with both turns counts as one rep.
End the set as soon as the plate starts sinking during the turns: bring it down to your thighs first, then bend your knees to set it on the floor.

name: Plate-Loaded Shoulder Press
instructions: Set the seat height so the handles start around shoulder level and you can grip them without reaching or shrugging your shoulders.
Load an appropriate weight evenly on both sides of the machine. Sit with your back flat against the pad, feet firmly on the floor, and your head in a neutral position.
Grip the handles with a full, secure grip. Keep your wrists straight and align your elbows slightly in front of or directly under your hands.
Brace the abdomen while keeping your back on the pad.
Press the handles upward by extending the elbows, letting the shoulder blades move naturally.
Finish with straight arms without snapping the elbows or lifting your hips from the seat.
Lower the handles slowly and under control until they return to shoulder level or to a comfortable depth with no shoulder pain.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions. After the last repetition, return the handles fully to the starting position before releasing your grip.

name: Dumbbell Half Kneeling Shoulder Press
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your right knee down and left foot flat on the ground in front of you, forming a 90-degree angle with your left knee.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Engage your core to maintain an upright torso and stabilize your position.
Press both dumbbells overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your wrists straight and stacked over your shoulders.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left knee down and right foot forward on the next set.

name: Band Pass Through Shoulders
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band with both hands. The band should be taut but not overly stretched.
Start with your hands in front of your thighs, keeping your arms straight and maintaining tension in the band.
Slowly raise your arms overhead, keeping them straight and maintaining tension in the band.
Continue moving your arms backward until the band reaches behind your back, or as far as your shoulder mobility allows.
Reverse the motion by bringing your arms back over your head to the starting position in front of your thighs.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, focusing on maintaining tension in the band throughout.

name: Ring Face Pull
instructions: Set the gymnastic rings at about chest height.
Stand facing the rings with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the rings with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Step back so your body is at an angle, keeping tension on the rings.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Pull the rings towards your face by driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Arm Circle
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Keep your palms facing down and your arms parallel to the ground.
Begin making small circles with your arms by rotating them forward.
Gradually increase the size of the circles while maintaining control and stability.
After completing a set number of rotations, reverse the direction and perform backward circles.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern throughout the exercise.

name: Band Upright Row
instructions: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the ends of the band with an overhand grip, arms extended downward in front of your thighs.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Pull the band upwards by bending your elbows and raising your hands towards your chin.
Ensure your elbows are higher than your wrists at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
instructions: Stand or sit with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Extend one arm across your body at shoulder height.
Use your opposite hand to gently pull the extended arm towards your chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch in the back of your shoulder.
Release and repeat on the other side.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold a kettlebell in one hand and press it overhead, keeping your arm straight.
Turn your feet approximately 45 degrees away from the arm holding the kettlebell.
Shift your weight onto the leg on the kettlebell side and push that hip out to the side.
Keeping your eyes on the kettlebell, slowly lower your torso by bending at the hips. Your free hand should slide down your leg towards the floor.
Continue lowering until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings or until your hand reaches the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom position, then engage your core and glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about hip height and stand with your back to it.
Reach behind you, grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your hips, and step forward to lift it off the hooks.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms straight and the bar against the back of your hips.
Lead with your elbows and draw them out and back, lifting the bar a short way up behind you while keeping it close to your body.
Pause at the top and squeeze the back of your shoulders, keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then step back and return the bar to the rack.

name: Full Planche
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and fingers pointing forward.
Engage your core and glutes to keep your body in a straight line.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands while keeping your arms straight.
Lift your feet off the ground by engaging your core and lower back muscles.
Maintain a parallel position to the ground with your legs fully extended.
Hold the position for as long as possible while maintaining form.
To exit, slowly lower your feet back to the ground and return to a plank position.

name: Dumbbell Standing Driver
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, maintaining a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands at chest level, gripping it firmly on each end.
Engage your core to maintain an upright posture and avoid arching your back.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping a slight bend in the elbows to reduce joint strain.
Rotate the dumbbell to the left as if turning a steering wheel, then return to the center.
Rotate the dumbbell to the right, then return to the center.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Lean-Away Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand beside a sturdy support and grip it with one raised hand to support your lean.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with your palm facing your thigh. Walk your feet slightly toward the support and lean your body away, keeping your feet planted and your body in a straight line.
Brace your core, keep your chest open, and let the working arm hang slightly in front of your hip with a soft bend in the elbow.
Raise the dumbbell to the side in a smooth arc, keeping the wrist straight and the elbow slightly bent.
