Lift until your upper arm is about parallel with the floor, or stop earlier if you cannot keep your torso still and shoulder position controlled.
Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbell slowly back to the starting position without swinging or using momentum.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch sides.

name: Straddle Planche
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands, keeping your arms straight.
Engage your core and lift your legs off the ground, spreading them apart into a straddle position.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your toes, keeping your body parallel to the ground.
Hold the position for as long as possible while maintaining proper form.
Slowly lower your legs back to the ground to return to the starting position.

name: Pike Push-Up Between Chairs
instructions: Place two sturdy chairs shoulder-width apart for your hands and one chair behind you for your feet.
Position yourself in a pike position with your hands on the chairs and your feet elevated on the third chair.
Ensure your body forms an inverted V shape with hips raised high.
Lower your head towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them slightly flared out.
Pause briefly when your head is close to the floor, then push through your palms to return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral neck position throughout the movement.

name: Pike Push-Up Between Benches
instructions: Position two benches parallel to each other, about shoulder-width apart.
Place one hand on the near end of each bench and your feet on the far ends of the benches, forming a pike position with your hips elevated.
Keep your body inverted with your legs straight and core engaged.
Lower your head towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the movement and avoid arching your back.

name: Band Pull-Apart
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold a resistance band with an overhand grip, hands slightly narrower than shoulder width.
Raise your arms straight in front of you to shoulder height, elbows soft and the band lightly tensioned.
Brace your core, keep your ribs down and set your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping your arms straight and level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and stop when your arms are in line with your body and the band touches your chest.
Bring your arms back to the front slowly, keeping the band under tension.

name: Prone Y Raise
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Extend your arms overhead in a Y, about 30 degrees out from your head, with thumbs pointing up.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down and back.
Lift both straight arms off the floor as high as you can without shrugging or arching your lower back.
Hold the top for a second and squeeze the muscles below your shoulder blades.
Lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.

name: Two-Arm Landmine Press
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine and load a plate on the free end.
Stand facing the free end with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Clasp both hands around the very end of the bar, one hand over the other, and hold it in front of your chest with your elbows pointing down.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar forward and up along its arc until your arms are fully straight.
Lower the bar under control along the same arc until your hands are back in front of your chest.
Finish the set, then lower the end of the bar to the floor.

name: Standing Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position and attach single handles.
Stand between the pulleys holding one handle in each hand.
Place your feet side by side, brace your abdomen and keep your trunk upright.
Bring your hands to shoulder height with your palms facing forward or slightly inward.
Press both handles overhead until your arms are straight while keeping your trunk steady.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your core tight and your head in a neutral position.
Lower the handles slowly back to shoulder height, keeping control of the cables and avoiding any sudden pull from the weight stack.

name: Dumbbell Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with straight legs and heels down, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder with palms facing each other.
Sit tall with your chest up and your ribs stacked over your hips. Brace your abdominal muscles and keep your legs straight, with your heels on the floor.
Press both dumbbells overhead in a controlled motion. Keep your forearms close to vertical and avoid leaning your torso backward.
Finish with the dumbbells over your shoulders and your elbows straight but not forcefully locked. Keep your head neutral and your ribs down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to shoulder height while staying upright. Do not let your lower back round excessively or your torso rock backward.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions, using a weight that allows you to maintain a tall seated position throughout.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Push Press
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Hold a kettlebell in one hand in the rack position, with the bell resting against the outside of your forearm near your shoulder and your elbow close to your ribs.
Brace your stomach, keep your chest up, and keep your wrist straight. Your free arm can extend slightly to the side for balance.
Bend your knees and hips slightly into a short, controlled dip. Keep your heels on the floor and avoid leaning forward or letting the kettlebell drift away from your body.
Drive forcefully through your feet to stand up. Use the leg drive to start the kettlebell moving upward.
As the kettlebell rises, press it overhead until your arm is straight. Finish with the kettlebell stacked over your shoulder, hip, and foot, with your biceps close to your ear.
Lower the kettlebell under control back to the rack position, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch hands and repeat on the other side.

name: Freestanding Handstand
instructions: Stand with your feet together, fold forward and place your palms flat on the floor shoulder-width apart, a little in front of your feet. Spread your fingers wide and point them forward.
Straighten your arms and lean forward until your shoulders are over your hands and most of your weight rests on them.
Bend your knees and lift both feet off the floor at the same time with a small hop. Pull your knees toward your chest until your hips are above your shoulders.
Extend your legs straight up, keeping them together, until your body forms one vertical line from your hands to your toes.
Push the floor away with locked elbows and lift your shoulders toward your ears. Squeeze your glutes and legs, point your toes and keep your ribs pulled in.
Balance through your hands. If your legs tip past vertical, press your fingertips into the floor; if you start falling back the way you came up, shift the pressure to the heels of your hands.
After the planned time, bend your knees, lower both feet to the floor together with control and return to the forward fold.

name: Barbell Hang High Pull
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip just outside your thighs, arms straight.
Lift the bar to a hang position around mid-thigh. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, keeping your back flat, chest up and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
Keep the bar close to your body. Brace your core and keep your weight balanced through the middle of your feet.
Drive forcefully through your feet, extending your hips, knees and ankles. Shrug your shoulders upward as the bar accelerates.
After the leg and hip drive, lift your elbows high and out as the bar rises toward chest height.
Do not curl the bar or catch it on your shoulders. Your elbows should finish high, with the bar below them.
Lower the bar under control back to the hang position, then reset your posture before the next repetition.

name: Prone T Raise
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height so your body forms a T, with thumbs pointing up.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift both straight arms off the floor.
Raise them as high as you can without shrugging or arching your lower back.
Hold the top for a second, then lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.

name: Power Jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width apart. Grip the bar just outside your shoulders, with elbows slightly in front of the bar and your chest lifted.
Take the bar out of the rack and step back. Keep the bar resting on the front of your shoulders, brace your core, and keep your eyes forward.
Dip straight down by bending your knees and hips slightly. Keep your torso upright, your heels on the floor, and let your knees track over your toes.
Immediately drive hard through the floor with your legs. Extend your hips, knees, and ankles to accelerate the bar upward.
Move quickly under the rising bar and receive it in a shallow squat with both feet parallel.
Lock your arms fully overhead. Keep the bar directly over the middle of your feet, with your head slightly forward between your arms and your shoulders active.
Stabilize the catch position, then stand fully upright with the bar locked overhead. Your knees and hips should be fully extended before lowering the bar.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders, bending your knees slightly to absorb the weight. Reset your position before the next repetition.

name: Front Crawl Swimming
instructions: Push off the wall face-down with your arms extended in front, your body long and level, and your eyes looking down and slightly ahead.
Kick continuously from the hips with long legs, soft knees and pointed feet, keeping the kick small and close to the surface.
Reach one arm forward in line with your shoulder, then bend the elbow slightly so your hand and forearm face backward and catch the water.
Pull the water back under your body with a high elbow and push it past your hip, letting the hand leave the water by your thigh.
Bring the arm forward over the water with a relaxed, bent elbow leading, and enter the hand in front of your shoulder without crossing your centerline.
Alternate your arms without pausing, letting your shoulders and hips roll together from side to side while your body stays level.

Exhale steadily into the water. To breathe, turn your head with the body roll as that arm finishes its pull, inhale quickly with one goggle lens still underwater, and turn your face back down as the arm comes forward.
Keep an even rhythm of strokes, kicks and breaths for the planned time.

name: Suspension Face Pull
instructions: Set the suspension trainer handles to about chest height and stand facing the anchor point.
Hold one handle in each hand with an overhand or neutral grip, then walk your feet forward until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Start with your arms straight in front of you, shoulders down, chest lifted and core braced.
Pull your body toward the handles by driving your elbows out and back at shoulder height.
Bring the handles toward the sides of your face, around forehead or ear level, while squeezing your upper back and rear shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly straighten your arms to return to the starting position with control.

name: Barbell Z Press
instructions: Set the bar in a rack or on safety pins at about your seated shoulder height, then sit on the floor so the bar is just in front of your shoulders.
Straighten your legs in front of you, slightly apart, and sit tall on your sit bones with your torso upright.
Take a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack the bar so it rests at the front of your shoulders, elbows under the bar and slightly in front of it.
Brace your core, pull your ribs down and tense your thighs so your knees stay straight.
Press the bar straight up, pulling your head back slightly so the bar can pass your face.
Once the bar passes your forehead, push your head through between your arms and lock out your elbows with the bar over your shoulders and hips.
Lower the bar under control to the front of your shoulders and start the next rep without leaning back. After the last rep, return the bar to the rack.

name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
instructions: Place two dumbbells on the floor beside your feet and take a neutral grip.
Bend your hips and knees, brace your trunk and keep your back neutral.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift the dumbbells close to your body.
Move your elbows under the weights and catch them at your shoulders in a squat.
Rise from the squat and press both dumbbells overhead.
Finish with straight arms, the weights above your shoulders and ribs controlled.
Lower to the shoulders, then toward the floor with bent hips and knees to reset.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Overhead Carry
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart. Hold the dumbbell in one hand at shoulder level with your wrist straight.
Press the dumbbell overhead until your elbow is fully straight. Keep the weight stacked above your shoulder, with your biceps close to your ear.
Brace your core and keep your ribs down. Do not arch your lower back or lean away from the dumbbell.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps, keeping your head neutral and eyes forward. Let the loaded shoulder stay active overhead.
Walk for the planned distance or time, then lower the dumbbell carefully back to shoulder level before setting it down.
Repeat on the other side, using the same distance or time for each arm.

name: Supported Headstand
instructions: Practice near a wall with a clear, padded surface, and avoid this exercise if you have neck, shoulder, eye-pressure, blood-pressure, or balance concerns unless cleared by a qualified healthcare professional.
Kneel facing the wall and place your forearms on the floor, interlacing your fingers to create a stable cup for the back of your head.
Set your elbows about shoulder-width apart; keep them from sliding outward by checking that each hand can lightly hold the opposite elbow before interlacing your fingers again.
Place the crown of your head gently on the floor with the back of your head supported by your interlaced hands, keeping pressure light through the neck.
Tuck your toes, lift your knees, and walk your feet toward your torso until your hips are stacked as closely as possible over your shoulders.
Press firmly through your forearms and shoulders, drawing your shoulder blades away from your ears so most of the load is supported by your upper body rather than your head and neck.
Bend one knee and draw it toward your chest, then bring the other knee in to balance in a compact tuck position without kicking off the floor.
When stable, slowly extend both legs upward until your body forms a straight line, keeping your core engaged, legs together, and gaze neutral.
Hold the position while breathing steadily and maintaining active pressure through your forearms; stop immediately if you feel neck pain, tingling, dizziness, or loss of control.
To exit, bend both knees into the tuck position, lower one foot and then the other to the floor with control, and rest briefly in Child’s Pose before standing.

name: Barbell Bradford Press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell across the front of your shoulders with an overhand grip clearly wider than shoulder width.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your ribs down and your torso upright.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended, tilting your head slightly back to let it pass.
Lower the bar under control behind your head until it rests on your upper traps.
Press the bar overhead again to straight arms, then lower it in front of your head to your shoulders.
Keep alternating the front and back positions for the planned number of repetitions.

name: Prone Shoulder CARs
instructions: Lie face down with your legs straight and both hands on the back of your head, elbows out to the sides.
Keep your hips and legs on the floor and your neck long, with your eyes on the floor.
Slowly move both arms out to the sides, straightening your elbows until your arms form a T with your hands just above the floor.
Keep sweeping your arms toward your hips, then bend your elbows and turn your arms inward to rest your hands on your lower back.
Reverse the path: straighten your arms out to the sides, then bend your elbows and bring your hands back behind your head.
Repeat at a slow, even pace, keeping your torso still throughout.

name: Landmine Viking Press
instructions: Set a barbell securely into a landmine base or anchored corner and load an appropriate amount of weight onto the free end.
Attach a Viking press handle to the sleeve of the barbell and make sure the attachment is locked in place and balanced.
Stand facing the loaded end of the barbell with your feet about shoulder-width apart, positioning yourself so the handles start at upper-chest or shoulder height.
Grip the handles firmly with both hands, keep your wrists neutral, brace your abdominal muscles, and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Press the handles upward and forward by extending your elbows, allowing the barbell to travel along its natural arc.
Finish with your arms nearly straight overhead in front of you, keeping your shoulders controlled and avoiding an exaggerated lower-back arch.
Lower the handles slowly and under control back to shoulder height, keeping your core braced and elbows tracking comfortably.

name: Wall Walk
instructions: Start in a high plank with your feet close to a clear wall. Place your hands under your shoulders and brace your core.
Walk your feet up the wall slowly while walking your hands back toward the wall. Keep your arms straight and your body tight.
Continue until you reach the planned height. Beginners can stop before vertical, while advanced athletes can bring their chest close to the wall.
At the top, push firmly through your hands, keep your ribs pulled in, and look between your hands rather than at the wall.
To come down, walk your hands forward as you lower your feet down the wall under control.
Finish in a strong high plank, then lower your knees or step away from the wall.

name: Handstand Walk
instructions: Stand in a clear area and fold forward to prepare to place your hands on the floor.
Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart and kick one leg up, then bring the other leg up to reach a controlled handstand.
Stack your shoulders over your hands, keep your elbows locked and push tall through your shoulders.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes and keep your legs together with pointed toes. Avoid arching your lower back.
Shift your body weight slightly onto one hand, then lift the opposite hand and place it a small step forward.
Transfer your weight onto the hand you just placed, then repeat with the other hand. Take short, controlled steps rather than reaching too far.
To finish safely, lower one leg at a time into a lunge or cartwheel out to the side if you lose balance.

name: Log Clean and Press
instructions: Stand close to the log with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Squat down and take the handles with a neutral grip.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and drive through your legs to lift the log to your thighs.
Keep the log tight to your body and roll it up onto your upper chest, driving your elbows high.
Stand tall with the log resting on your chest and your elbows up.
Dip by bending your knees, then drive hard with your legs to send the log upward.
Bend your knees again to get under the log and catch it on straight arms.
Stand up with your elbows locked and the log over your midfoot.
Lower the log to your chest, then to your thighs and back to the floor under control.

name: Barbell Squat
instructions: Position the barbell on a squat rack at about shoulder height.
Step under the bar and place it across your upper back, ensuring it rests comfortably on your trapezius muscles.
Grip the bar with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the bar off the rack by straightening your legs and stepping back carefully.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Begin the squat by bending at the hips and knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Ensure your knees track over your toes without caving inward.
Push through your heels to return to a standing position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Leg Extension Machine
instructions: Adjust the seat so that your knees align with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit back against the backrest and place your feet under the padded bar, ensuring it rests just above your ankles.
Grip the handles on either side of the seat for stability.
Begin by extending your legs fully while exhaling, keeping your back pressed against the backrest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement with your legs fully extended.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position while inhaling, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Hip Adduction
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the hip adduction machine to ensure comfort and proper alignment.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest and feet placed on the footrests.
Position your legs apart, placing your knees against the padded levers.
Grip the handles on either side of the seat for stability.
Exhale and slowly bring your knees together by contracting your inner thigh muscles.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction point, ensuring full range of motion.
Inhale and gradually return to the starting position, controlling the resistance throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Position the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the bar just outside your knees with an overhand or mixed grip.
Keep your chest up, back straight, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift the bar by extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Keep the bar close to your body as you lift it to hip level.
Once fully upright, pause briefly before lowering the bar back to the ground by hinging at the hips and bending your knees.

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leg curl machine so that your knees align with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest, rest the back of your lower legs on the padded lever just above your heels, and lower the thigh pad onto your thighs.
Grip the handles or sides of the seat for stability.
Begin with your legs fully extended in front of you.
Exhale and slowly curl your legs back by bending your knees, bringing your heels as close to your buttocks as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment at the bottom of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with controlled movement, extending your legs fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle when seated.
Position your feet on the footplate with the balls of your feet securely placed and heels hanging off.
Place your thighs under the padded lever, ensuring it rests comfortably above your knees.
Release the safety bar if applicable, allowing free movement of the lever.
Lower your heels slowly towards the ground to achieve a full stretch in your calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calf muscles.
Hold the top position briefly for maximum contraction before lowering back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Prone Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the leg curl machine so that the roller pad sits comfortably just above your heels when you are lying face down.
Lie prone on the machine, ensuring your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Grip the handles or sides of the bench for stability.
Engage your core and keep your hips pressed against the bench.
Exhale and curl your legs by bending your knees, bringing your heels towards your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Squat
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Extend one leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench.
Keep your chest up and core engaged as you begin to lower your hips by bending your front knee.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the ground or as far as your mobility allows.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one leg before switching to the other.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Load the same plates on both sides of the sled so it runs evenly on the rails.
Sit all the way back, hips down in the seat, with your back and head on the pad.
Set your feet flat in the middle of the platform, about hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Press the sled just off the stops, turn the safety handles out to free it, then take hold of the seat handles beside your hips.
From the top, legs almost straight, bend your knees and hips and lower the sled over about 2 seconds, knees tracking over your toes.
Keep going until your thighs near your ribs, about 90 degrees at the knee or a bit deeper. Stop before your hips curl off the seat.
Without bouncing, drive the sled back up through your whole foot, heels down, and stop just short of locking your knees.
At the top of the final rep, turn the safety handles back in while the sled is at the top, then let it down onto them.

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunges
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

Step forward with your right foot, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90-degree angles. Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle and your back knee hovers just above the ground.
Push through the heel of your right foot to rise and bring your left foot forward, stepping into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions or distance.
Maintain an upright torso throughout the movement, keeping your core engaged.

name: Machine Hack Squat
instructions: Position yourself on the hack squat machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, with toes slightly pointed out.
Release the safety handles and extend your legs to lift the weight off the rack.
Lower your body by bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the platform or slightly below.
Push through your heels to extend your legs and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then safely re-rack the weight by engaging the safety handles.

name: Machine Calf Raises
instructions: Set the shoulder pads so you have to bend your knees slightly to get under them.
Step under the pads and place the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform, about hip-width apart, with your heels free.
Hold the handles and stand up straight to lift the weight, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Lower your heels slowly below the platform until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your calves.
Lower your heels under control back to the stretched position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then bend your knees to set the weight down.

name: Treadmill Run
instructions: Start by standing on the treadmill with your feet on the side rails.
Attach the safety clip to your clothing to ensure the treadmill stops if needed.
Set the treadmill to a low speed to begin and step onto the belt carefully.
Gradually increase the speed to your desired running pace.
Maintain an upright posture with your head up and shoulders relaxed.
Keep your arms bent at a 90-degree angle, swinging naturally with each stride.
Focus on landing softly on the midfoot and rolling through to the toes.
Adjust the incline setting to simulate outdoor running conditions if desired.
Cool down by gradually reducing speed before stepping off the treadmill.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Take the dumbbells from a rack or bench. If they're on the floor, squat down, lift them with a flat back and stand tall.
Set your feet hip-width apart, toes forward, and unlock your knees into a soft bend you keep until the last rep.
Rest the dumbbells on the front of your thighs, overhand grip, palms facing you and handles roughly in line. Shoulders slightly back and down.
Breathe in, brace and push your hips straight back. Your torso tips forward on its own, back flat, eyes on the floor ahead.
Take 2–3 seconds to slide the dumbbells down your thighs, arms hanging straight. Stop just below the knees, when your hips stop moving back.
Pause for a beat, then drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall without leaning back. The dumbbells never touch the floor.
To finish, bend your knees and set the dumbbells down with your back flat, or return them to the rack.

name: Calf Leg Press
instructions: Position yourself on the sled with your back firmly against the backrest and your feet placed shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Ensure that only the balls of your feet are on the platform, with your heels hanging off.
Unlock the sled safety mechanism and extend your legs fully without locking your knees.
Lower your heels slowly towards the ground to stretch your calves fully.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calf muscles.
Hold the top position for a moment before slowly lowering back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Squat
instructions: Position the bar of the Smith machine at shoulder height.
Stand under the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place the bar across your upper back and shoulders, gripping it with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and step back slightly to clear the safety stops.
Keep your chest up, core engaged, and back straight throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your knees and hips.

name: Smith Calf Raises
instructions: Position yourself under the Smith machine bar with the balls of your feet on a raised platform or block, heels hanging off.
Adjust the bar to rest comfortably across your upper back and shoulders.
Unlock the bar by rotating it forward and ensure your feet are shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your knees slightly bent throughout the exercise.
Raise your heels by extending your ankles, lifting as high as possible onto your toes.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower your heels back to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your calves.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands under the top weight, keeping it close to your chest.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a squat.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground, ensuring knees track over toes.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position, maintaining an upright torso throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raises
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging naturally by your sides.
Position your feet so that the balls of your feet are on the edge of a raised platform or step, allowing your heels to hang off.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Slowly raise your heels by extending your ankles as high as possible, contracting your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your heels back to the starting position, allowing them to drop slightly below the platform level for a full stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lever Horizontal Leg Press
instructions: Set the weight first: move the pin in the stack, or load plates if your machine takes them.
Sit with your hips all the way back and your back on the pad. There is no headrest, so hold your head level.
Put both feet flat in the middle of the footplate, about hip-width apart, toes pointing up or slightly out, heels down.
Set the seat position so your knees start bent about 90 degrees with your feet on the plate.
Hold the handles beside the seat with straight arms. They keep your hips down; don't pull on them.
Breathe out and press through your heels and midfoot. The plate stays put while you and the seat roll back.
Keep your knees tracking over your second toe and pause for a beat just before they straighten fully.
Ride the seat forward over 2–3 seconds until your knees are back at about 90 degrees, touch the bottom lightly and press again.
When the set is over, let the seat settle against the stops before you take your feet off the plate.

name: Single-Leg Extension
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leg extension machine so that your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest and your feet under the padded lever.
Select an appropriate weight on the machine's weight stack.
Grasp the handles or sides of the seat to stabilize your upper body.
Extend one leg by pushing against the padded lever until your leg is fully extended, keeping your foot flexed.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the quadriceps.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position without letting the weights touch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Stationary Bike
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your legs are slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit on the bike with your back straight and hands resting on the handlebars.
Start pedaling slowly to warm up, gradually increasing your speed.
Adjust the resistance level to a comfortable setting for your workout goals.
Maintain a steady pace and keep your core engaged throughout the session.
Cool down by gradually reducing your speed and resistance before stopping.

name: Standing Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the machine so that the pad rests comfortably against the back of your lower leg, just above the ankle.
Stand upright with your torso straight and hold onto the machine handles for support.
Position your feet hip-width apart and ensure your working leg is aligned with the machine's lever.
Engage your core and keep your supporting leg slightly bent to maintain balance.
Exhale as you curl your working leg upward by flexing your knee, bringing your heel towards your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the hamstrings.
Inhale as you slowly lower your leg back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Bulgarian Squat Smith
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to shoulder height and ensure the safety locks are in place.
Stand about two feet in front of the bench with your back to it, and position the bar across your upper back.
Place one foot on the bench behind you, ensuring your toes are securely positioned.
Grip the bar with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your back knee toward the ground by bending your front knee.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor or slightly below, ensuring your front knee does not extend past your toes.
Press through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, keeping the movement controlled.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Single Leg Press
instructions: Load the plates evenly on both sides of the sled. For your first sets, start well under half of what you press with two legs.
Slide all the way back so your hips sit deep in the seat and your back and head rest on the pad.
Put both feet on the platform, press the sled off the stops and turn the safety handles out to free it.
Take one foot down and rest it flat on the frame near the floor, well clear of the sled and the stops.
The working foot stays flat on its own side of the platform, in line with that hip, toes up or turned out a touch.
Hold the seat handles and pull down lightly so both hips stay pinned to the seat.
Bend the knee and lower the sled over about 2 seconds, the knee heading straight for the shoulder on the same side.
At about 90 degrees at the knee, before that hip rolls up, press back through the whole foot and stop short of lockout.
At the end of the set, put the free foot back on the platform, turn the safety handles in and switch legs.

name: Treadmill Climbing
instructions: Begin by setting the treadmill to a low speed and a moderate incline to warm up.
Gradually increase the incline to simulate climbing. Adjust speed as necessary to maintain a steady pace.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders back and core engaged.
Use a natural arm swing to help balance and maintain rhythm.
Focus on landing softly on your feet to reduce impact on the joints.
Continue climbing for your desired duration or until you reach your target heart rate.

name: Front Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position the barbell on the front of your shoulders, resting it on your deltoids.
Cross your arms over the barbell or use a clean grip with your fingertips under the bar for support.
Keep your elbows high and chest up to maintain an upright torso.
Engage your core and begin the squat by bending at the hips and knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Straight Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward, and the barbell over your mid-foot.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your legs straight but not locked, and engage your core.
Hinge at the hips by pushing them back while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Lower the barbell along your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive your hips forward to return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement and avoid rounding your back.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: Stand in the center of the trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the handles of the trap bar firmly.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and spine neutral.
Engage your core and push through your heels to lift the bar by extending your hips and knees.
Stand fully upright with your shoulders back and chest proud at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the ground by bending at the hips and knees, maintaining a neutral spine throughout.

name: Elliptical Trainer
instructions: Step onto the elliptical trainer and place your feet on the pedals.
Grip the handles firmly with both hands.
Start pedaling forward by pushing down with one foot while pulling up with the other.
Adjust the resistance and incline settings to match your desired intensity level.
Maintain an upright posture with your core engaged throughout the workout.
Use a smooth and controlled motion, avoiding bouncing or jerky movements.
To stop, gradually slow down your pace until the machine comes to a complete stop.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Position yourself in front of a sturdy platform or bench that is approximately knee height.
Step onto the platform with your right foot, pressing through the heel to lift your body up.
Bring your left foot up to meet your right foot on the platform, standing tall.
Step back down with your left foot first, followed by your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Barbell Calf Raise
instructions: Position a barbell across your upper back, similar to a back squat setup. Ensure it is balanced and secure.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a flat surface or an elevated platform for greater range of motion.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight throughout the movement.
Slowly raise your heels off the ground by pushing through the balls of your feet, extending your ankles fully.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise with Dumbbell
instructions: Stand side-on next to a wall and place your near hand flat on it at about shoulder height.
Hold a dumbbell in your other hand with the arm hanging straight at your side.
Shift your weight onto the leg on the dumbbell side and bend the other knee to lift that foot off the floor.
Push through the ball of your foot and raise your heel as high as you can, keeping the knee straight.
Hold the top for a moment, then lower your heel slowly until it is back on the floor.
Do all your reps on one leg, then turn around and work the other side.

name: Stair Climber
instructions: Start by stepping onto the machine and securely holding the handrails.
Select your desired workout program or manually adjust the speed and resistance to your fitness level.
Begin stepping by alternately pressing down on each pedal, simulating a stair-climbing motion.
Maintain an upright posture with your core engaged and avoid leaning heavily on the handrails.
Continue the motion for your desired duration or until you reach your fitness goal.

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step one foot forward into a lunge position, ensuring your feet are staggered and hip-width apart.
Lower your back knee towards the ground by bending both knees until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Leg Press Wide Stance
instructions: Load the plates evenly on both sides of the sled, then sit all the way back with your hips down in the seat and your head on the pad.
Place your feet flat at mid-height on the platform, clearly wider than your shoulders, each one near a side edge but fully on it.
Turn your toes out about 15–30° so your feet point where your knees are going to travel.
Press the sled off the stops, turn the safety handles out to free it, and hold the seat handles beside your hips.
Bend your knees and let the sled come down over about two seconds, knees opening out in line with your toes.
Stop at roughly 90° at the knee, or sooner if your tailbone starts to lift. Your thighs should pass beside your ribs.
Drive back up through the whole foot with your heels down and knees pushed out, stopping just short of locking out.
At the top of the final rep, turn the safety handles back in before you let the sled down onto them.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneel on a soft surface with your feet secured under a stable object or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from your head to your knees.
Cross your arms over your chest or place them at your sides.
Slowly lean forward, keeping your back straight and engaging your core.
Lower yourself as far as you can while maintaining control, then push back up to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged throughout the movement.
Initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Ensure that your knees track over your toes and do not extend past them.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs and standing upright.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Jump Rope
instructions: Choose a rope of appropriate length; when you stand on the middle of the rope, the handles should reach your armpits.
Hold the handles with a firm grip, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Stand with your feet together on a flat surface, maintaining an upright posture.
Swing the rope over your head using your wrists, not your arms.
Jump off the ground just enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady rhythm and keep your jumps consistent in height and speed.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step with the ball of one foot, heel hanging off, using a wall or sturdy object for balance.
Lift the other foot off the step and let the working heel lower slightly below the step.
Engage your core and maintain a straight posture throughout the movement.
Slowly raise your heel as high as possible, keeping your knee straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your calf muscle.
Lower your heel back below the step in a controlled manner.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Rotary Calf Raise
instructions: Adjust the seat height on the rotary calf raise machine so that your knees are slightly bent when seated.
Position your feet on the footplate with your toes pointing forward and heels hanging off the edge.
Secure your thighs under the padded lever to ensure stability during the exercise.
Begin by pushing through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, engaging your calf muscles.
Hold the top position for a moment, then slowly lower your heels back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Barbell Walking Lunges
instructions: Begin by standing upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Position a barbell across your upper back, gripping it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Engage your core and keep your chest up. Step forward with your right foot, landing on your heel first.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at about a 90-degree angle. Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle and your back knee hovers just above the ground.
Push through the heel of your front foot and bring your back foot forward past it into the next lunge.
Continue walking forward, alternating legs with each repetition.

name: Box Jumps
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart at a comfortable distance from the box.
Engage your core and bend your knees slightly to prepare for the jump.
Swing your arms back and then forward as you explode upward, using your legs to propel yourself onto the box.
Land softly on the box with both feet flat and knees slightly bent to absorb the impact.
Stand up fully on the box to complete the movement.
Step down carefully one foot at a time and reset for the next repetition.

name: Single Leg Seated Calf Machine Raise
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the calf raise machine so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle when seated.
Sit on the machine and place the ball of one foot on the platform, ensuring your heel is hanging off.
Secure your thigh under the padded lever to stabilize your leg.
Begin with your heel lowered below the platform to stretch the calf muscle.
Push through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as possible, contracting your calf muscle.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Slowly lower your heel back to the starting position for a full stretch.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Squat
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your knees and push your hips back as if sitting in a chair.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground.
Ensure your knees are tracking over your toes without collapsing inward.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.

name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart on a flat surface or on the edge of a raised platform for greater range of motion.
If using weights, hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides or position a barbell across your upper back.
Keep your core engaged and back straight throughout the exercise.
Slowly lift your heels off the ground by pushing through the balls of your feet, raising your body upward.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Single Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leg curl machine so that your knees align with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest and rest the back of one lower leg on the padded lever, just above the heel.
Secure your position by holding onto the side handles.
Begin by flexing your knee to bring your heel towards your glutes, keeping your movement controlled.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the hamstring.
Slowly extend your leg back to the starting position without locking your knee.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out, and a kettlebell placed about a foot in front of you.
Hinge at the hips by pushing your butt back while maintaining a slight bend in the knees. Keep your back straight and chest up.
Grip the kettlebell handle with both hands using an overhand grip.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping it close to your groin.
Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height. Your arms should remain straight but relaxed.
Let the kettlebell fall back down naturally as you hinge at the hips again to repeat the motion.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout.

name: Machine Reverse Hack Squat
instructions: Load the plates evenly on the carriage while it rests on the stops.
Step onto the footplate facing the machine and press your chest and stomach into the pad, with the shoulder pads resting on top of your shoulders.
Set your feet flat, hip- to shoulder-width apart with the toes turned slightly out, a little behind your hips so your body leans into the pad.
Hold the handles at the front of the shoulder pads, elbows pointing down. Your hands only pin you under the pads; they don't pull.
Stand up to lift the carriage off the stops, then release the safety lever. Take a breath and brace your stomach.
Over about 2 seconds, sit your hips back and down along the rails while your knees travel forward over your toes. Your chest stays on the pad.
Go down until your thighs are about parallel to the footplate, or a little lower if your lower back stays flat and your heels stay down.
Without bouncing, push the footplate away through your whole foot so your hips and shoulders rise together. Squeeze your glutes and stop just short of locking your knees.
At the top of the final rep, re-engage the safety lever before you let the carriage down onto it.

name: Zercher Squat
instructions: Begin by setting a barbell on a squat rack at about waist height.
Position yourself under the barbell and cradle it in the crook of your elbows, keeping your arms bent and hands clasped together.
Stand up to lift the bar off the rack, maintaining a strong posture with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and keep your chest up as you initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, ensuring your knees track over your toes.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, keeping the bar secure in your elbows throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Rear Lunge
instructions: Position the bar of the Smith machine at shoulder height.
Stand under the bar and position it across your upper back. Grip the bar with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by pushing up and stepping forward with one foot.
Step back with one leg into a lunge position, ensuring your front knee is aligned with your ankle.
Lower your back knee towards the ground without letting it touch, keeping your torso upright.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Single-Leg Lying Curl
instructions: Adjust the leg curl machine to fit your body size, ensuring the roller pad is positioned just above your ankles.
Lie face down on the machine with your knees just past the edge of the pad, aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Grip the handles or sides of the bench for stability.
Start with one leg extended straight and slowly curl it upwards by bending your knee, bringing your heel towards your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the hamstring.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Walking Cardio
instructions: Begin with a warm-up by walking at a slow pace for 5-10 minutes to prepare your muscles and joints.
Adjust the treadmill to a comfortable speed or choose a flat, safe path if walking outdoors.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders relaxed and your core engaged.
Swing your arms naturally at your sides to help maintain balance and rhythm.
Walk at a brisk pace that elevates your heart rate but still allows you to hold a conversation.
Continue walking for 20-60 minutes depending on your fitness level and goals.
Cool down by gradually slowing your pace for the last 5-10 minutes of your walk.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift Straight Legs
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Keep your knees slightly bent and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Hinge at the hips, lowering the dumbbells towards the floor while keeping them close to your legs.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, ensuring your back remains straight.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift the dumbbells back to the starting position by reversing the hip hinge.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: B Stance Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart. Shift your weight onto your right foot and place your left foot slightly behind you, toes touching the ground for balance.
Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you hinge at the hips, lowering the weight towards the floor. Your right knee should have a slight bend.
Lower the weight until you feel a stretch in your right hamstring, ensuring your back remains flat and your shoulders are pulled back.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, keeping the movement controlled.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side before switching to the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, keeping your torso upright and core engaged.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee is just above the ground.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg to complete one full repetition.

name: Cable Step Up
instructions: Attach a handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold the handle in one hand and step back to create tension in the cable.
Place one foot on an elevated platform or step, ensuring your knee is aligned over your ankle.
Push through the heel of the foot on the platform to lift your body upward.
Bring your trailing leg up to meet the leading leg on the platform.
Slowly lower the trailing leg back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Narrow Stance 45 Degree Leg Press
instructions: Load the plates evenly on both sides of the sled, a little lighter than for your usual leg press.
Sit all the way back: hips down in the seat, back and head on the pad.
Set your feet flat and parallel mid-platform, a fist's width apart or less, toes pointing up or turned out just a touch.
Press the sled off the stops, turn the safety handles out to free it, then hold the seat handles beside your hips.
Bend your knees and lower the sled for about 2 seconds, knees side by side and traveling straight toward your chest.
Lower to about 90 degrees at the knee. Your thighs reach your ribs early, so stop before your hips lift off the seat.
Drive the sled back up through your whole foot, heels down, and stop just short of locking your knees.
At the top of the last rep, turn the safety handles back in and let the sled settle onto them.

name: Lowbar Squat
instructions: Set up a barbell in a squat rack at about chest height.
Position yourself under the bar, placing it across your posterior deltoids just below the spine of your scapula.
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, keeping your wrists straight.
Step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed out.
Take a deep breath, brace your core, and initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower yourself until your hip crease is below your knee level while maintaining a neutral spine.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Exhale at the top of the movement and repeat for desired repetitions.

name: Machine Belt Squat
instructions: Begin by adjusting the machine to your height and securing the belt around your hips.
Stand on the platform with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending at the hips and knees, keeping your chest up and knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as far as your mobility allows.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Box step-up
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box or platform with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your right foot firmly on the box, ensuring your entire foot is secure.
Push through your right heel to lift your body up onto the box, bringing your left foot up to meet the right.
Stand tall on the box with both feet flat and knees slightly bent.
Step back down with your left foot first, followed by your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Bulgarian Bag Walking Lunges
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding the Bulgarian Bag securely over your shoulders.
Step forward with your right foot, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle and your back knee is hovering just above the ground.
Push through the heel of your front foot to rise and bring your back foot forward to step into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs, maintaining an upright torso and steady pace.
Complete the desired number of repetitions or distance.

name: Barbell Rack Pull
instructions: Set up a barbell on a power rack or blocks at knee height or slightly below.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position the barbell over the mid-foot.
Grip the barbell with an overhand or mixed grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you hinge at the hips to lower your torso.
Lift the barbell by extending your hips and knees simultaneously, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand fully upright with your shoulders back and chest up at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Split Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Step forward with your right foot, keeping your torso upright.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Ensure your right knee is aligned over your right ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Weighted Cossack Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands close to your chest.
Shift your weight onto your right leg, bending the knee and pushing your hips back as you lower into a squat.
Keep your left leg straight with the foot flat on the ground or with the heel slightly raised if necessary.
Lower yourself until your right thigh is parallel to the ground or as low as your flexibility allows.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the left side.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunges
instructions: Begin by standing upright with your feet hip-width apart and a barbell resting across your upper back. Grip the barbell with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.

Step backward with your right foot, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees. Your front knee should be directly above your ankle, and your back knee should hover just above the ground.
Push through the heel of your left foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left foot stepping back to complete one full repetition.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Secure the strap around your ankle and stand sideways to the machine.
Position yourself so that the working leg is closest to the machine.
Hold onto the machine or a stable surface for support.
Start with your working leg extended out to the side.
Slowly bring your leg across your body, keeping it straight.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, feeling the contraction in your inner thigh.
Return to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Single Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Shift your weight onto your left leg, keeping a slight bend in the knee.
Hinge at the hips to lower the dumbbell towards the ground while extending your right leg straight behind you.
Keep your back flat and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lower the dumbbell until your torso is parallel to the ground or as far as your flexibility allows.
Return to the starting position by driving through your left heel and bringing your right leg forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended by your sides for stability.
Place your heels on top of a Swiss ball, legs straight and feet hip-width apart.
Lift your hips off the ground by engaging your core and glutes, forming a straight line from shoulders to heels.
Bend your knees and roll the ball towards your glutes by contracting your hamstrings.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your hips remain elevated.
Slowly extend your legs to roll the ball back to the starting position while maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Box Squat
instructions: Position a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs are parallel to the ground when seated.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Hold a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip, keeping your chest up and core engaged.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower yourself towards the box.
Descend under control until you lightly touch the box with your glutes, ensuring not to sit or rest on it.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully.

name: Jump Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees in line with your toes.
From the bottom, drive through your feet and extend your hips, knees and ankles to jump straight up.
Let your arms swing down to your sides as you leave the floor.
Land softly from the balls of your feet to your heels, with your knees bent to absorb the impact.
Bring your hands back to your chest and sink straight into the next squat.

name: Assault Air Bike
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your legs are slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit on the bike with your feet securely on the pedals and hands gripping the handlebars.
Start pedaling at a moderate pace to warm up, using both your legs and arms to move the pedals and handlebars.
Increase your speed and intensity by pedaling faster and pushing/pulling harder on the handlebars.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
Cool down by gradually reducing your speed and intensity over the last few minutes of your workout.

name: Sissy Squat
instructions: Start by standing upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Use a Sissy Squat bench or hold onto a stable surface for balance.
Engage your core and keep your torso upright. Begin to lean back by bending your knees forward, keeping your hips extended.
Lower your body by allowing your knees to travel forward while maintaining a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Descend until your knees are fully bent and your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Push through the balls of your feet to return to the starting position, extending your knees and bringing your body back upright.

name: Jefferson Curl
instructions: Begin by standing on an elevated surface with feet hip-width apart, holding a light barbell or dumbbell with both hands.
Keep your arms straight and let the weight hang in front of you.
Slowly tuck your chin to your chest and begin to roll down through your spine, vertebra by vertebra.
Allow your upper back to round as you continue to lower the weight towards the floor.
Keep your knees slightly bent and focus on maintaining control throughout the movement.
Once you reach your maximum comfortable range of motion, pause briefly.
Reverse the movement by slowly rolling up through your spine, vertebra by vertebra, until you return to the starting position.

name: Cyclist Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and place a weight plate or wedge under your heels to elevate them slightly.
Position your feet closer together than in a standard squat, with toes pointing forward.
Hold a barbell across your upper back using an overhand grip, or keep your hands at your sides if performing a bodyweight version.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower into a squat by bending at the knees.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below, ensuring your knees track over your toes.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with your legs fully extended off the end.
Place a dumbbell securely between your feet, holding it with the arches.
Keep your hips pressed against the bench and your core engaged.
Slowly curl the dumbbell upward by bending your knees, bringing your heels towards your glutes.
Pause at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the hamstrings.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Running
instructions: Begin with a warm-up: walk briskly or jog lightly for 5-10 minutes to prepare your body.
Set your pace: start at a comfortable speed that allows you to maintain a conversation without gasping for air.
Maintain proper form: keep your head up, shoulders relaxed, and arms bent at a 90-degree angle, swinging naturally with each stride.
Focus on your foot strike: land softly on the midfoot or forefoot to reduce impact on the joints.
Breathe rhythmically: inhale and exhale deeply through both your nose and mouth to optimize oxygen intake.
Cool down after your run: gradually decrease your speed to a walk for 5-10 minutes, allowing your heart rate to return to normal.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Squat
instructions: Begin by positioning a bench or platform behind you at knee height.
Place a barbell across your upper back, ensuring it is centered and secure.
Stand about two feet in front of the bench with your feet hip-width apart.
Lift one leg and place the top of your foot on the bench behind you.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body by bending the front knee.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the ground, ensuring your knee does not extend past your toes.
Press through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Weighted Sissy Squat
instructions: Begin by standing upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell close to your chest.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your knees.
Slowly bend your knees and lean back, keeping your hips extended and torso upright.
Lower yourself by pushing your knees forward and rising onto your toes until your knees are deeply bent.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive your knees back to return to the starting position.

name: Smith Chair Squat
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to shoulder height and lock it in place.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, positioning yourself under the bar so it rests comfortably across your upper back.
Grip the bar with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unlatch the bar by rotating it forward and step back slightly to clear the safety stops.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body by bending at the hips and knees.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below, ensuring your knees do not extend past your toes.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, maintaining tension in your legs.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Snatch
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes slightly turned out. Position the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Grip the barbell with a wide grip, arms straight and outside of your knees.
Lower your hips with your chest up and back straight, keeping your gaze forward.
Initiate the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your knees and hips in a smooth motion.
As the bar passes your knees, transition by pulling the bar close to your body and shrugging your shoulders.
Explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling yourself under the bar.
Catch the bar overhead in a deep squat position with arms fully extended and locked out.
Stand up from the squat position to complete the lift, keeping the bar stable overhead.

name: Power Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and position the barbell over the mid-foot. Bend at the hips and knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set your back by pulling your shoulder blades together and maintaining a neutral spine. Your chest should be up and your gaze forward.
Initiate the lift by extending your hips and knees simultaneously, keeping the bar close to your body as you pull it upwards.
As the bar passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and shrug your shoulders to accelerate the bar upward.
Quickly drop under the bar by bending your knees and catching it on your shoulders in a front rack position with elbows high.
Stand up fully to complete the lift, ensuring the bar is stable on your shoulders before lowering it back to the starting position.

name: High-Bar Squat
instructions: Position a barbell on a squat rack at shoulder height.
Step under the bar and place it on your upper traps, ensuring it is centered.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and lift your elbows to create a stable shelf.
Unrack the bar by standing up straight and take a step back.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees simultaneously.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Ensure your knees track over your toes throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees.

name: Split Squat Front Foot Elevated
instructions: Stand in front of a platform or step, about 6-12 inches high, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place your right foot on the platform, ensuring your heel is firmly planted.
Step back with your left foot, positioning it so that both knees can bend comfortably.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your right knee does not extend beyond your toes.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Lunge Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor and step your right foot forward so your right knee is bent at about 90 degrees over your ankle.
Rest your left knee and the top of your left foot or your toes on the floor behind you.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core.
Shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch in the front of your left hip and thigh.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then ease your hips back.
Repeat for the desired time, then switch sides.

name: Poliquin Step-Up
instructions: Stand on a low step on your working leg, with the other foot hanging just off the side of the step.
Keep your hands at your sides and your torso upright.
Bend the working knee forward over your toes and lower the free foot towards the floor beside the step.
Lightly tap the floor with the free foot without shifting your weight onto it.
Push through the foot on the step to straighten the working knee and return to the top.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Smith Hack Squat
instructions: Stand with your back to the Smith machine bar, set at about knee height, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, grip the bar behind your legs with an overhand grip, unrack it by rotating it, and stand up holding it with straight arms.
Keep your chest up, core engaged, and back straight throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, ensuring your heels remain flat on the ground.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your legs without locking your knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Walking Lunges
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or holding dumbbells by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, landing on the heel first.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your right foot to rise and bring your left foot forward to step into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions or distance.

name: Prowler Sled
instructions: Begin by loading the sled with an appropriate amount of weight. Start light if you are new to this exercise.
Position yourself behind the sled. Place your hands on the handles or the horizontal bar, depending on the sled design.
Adopt a forward-leaning stance with your back straight and core engaged. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drive through your legs and push the sled forward using powerful strides. Maintain a steady pace and control throughout.
