Lower your torso and lift the back leg at the same time. Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor.
Keep both hips level and facing the floor, with the toes of the raised foot pointing down.
Go down until your torso and raised leg are about parallel to the floor, or until you feel a strong stretch in the back of the standing thigh. Keep your back flat.
Press the standing foot into the floor and drive your hips forward to stand up, bringing the free foot back down beside the standing one.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

name: Barbell Kneeling Squat
instructions: Kneel with your feet behind you and hold the bar securely across your upper back, away from your neck.
Start in tall kneeling, brace your abdomen and keep the bar balanced over your body.
Start the descent by pushing your hips back toward your heels. Keep your torso controlled and avoid rounding your lower back.
Lower until your glutes lightly touch or come close to your heels, or stop earlier if you cannot maintain a neutral spine.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the tall kneeling position. Finish with your hips fully extended without leaning backward.
Repeat slowly while keeping both knees planted and the bar steady.

name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, with your toes turned out slightly if needed.
Hold a kettlebell at each shoulder in the front rack, with the bells resting against your forearms.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and maintain a neutral spine. Keep your weight balanced across your whole feet.
Begin the squat by bending your knees and hips at the same time. Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes.
Lower under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as you can go without your lower back rounding or your heels lifting.
Drive through your midfoot and heels to stand up. Extend your knees and hips together while keeping the kettlebells stable in the rack position.
Exhale as you stand, then reset your brace before the next repetition.

name: Hang Snatch
instructions: Stand tall with a barbell held in a wide snatch grip, with your hands near the outer knurling and the bar resting against your upper thighs.
Set your feet about hip-width apart, brace your core, keep your chest up, and pull your shoulders slightly back and down.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly to lower the bar to the hang position, typically just above or just below the knees, while keeping the bar close to your legs and your back neutral.
Pause in the hang position with your weight balanced through the mid-foot, arms straight, hips pushed back, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
Drive forcefully through the floor by extending your hips, knees, and ankles, keeping the bar close to your body as it accelerates upward.
As the bar reaches hip level, shrug your shoulders and then pull yourself under the bar by bending your elbows high and to the sides.
Quickly rotate your elbows under the bar and catch it overhead in a partial or full squat, with arms locked out, shoulders active, and the bar positioned over the middle of your feet.

Stand up fully from the catch position, maintaining locked elbows and a stable overhead position before lowering the bar under control or dropping it safely if appropriate equipment and space are available.

name: Cycling
instructions: Adjust the saddle so your knee remains slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke, then sit on the bicycle.
Wear supportive shoes and secure your feet on the pedals if the bike has straps or clips. Keep a light grip on the handlebars and relax your shoulders.
Lean forward naturally from your hips, lightly engage your core and keep your elbows slightly bent. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid resting heavily on the handlebars.
Start pedaling slowly and smoothly. Push down through one pedal while the opposite leg follows the motion, then alternate continuously.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet. Do not let them collapse inward or flare excessively outward as you pedal.
Ease your pace, brake smoothly and bring the bicycle to a stop before getting off.

name: Machine Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Adjust the rear pad so it rests securely above your hips when you hinge forward.
Stand on the platform with the balls of your feet supported and your heels hanging off the edge. Place your feet about hip-width apart with your toes pointing forward.
Hinge forward and rest your forearms on the front support, keeping your legs nearly straight.
Release the safety catch if the machine has one, then lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch through your calves.
Press through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as you can. Keep your hips and knees still throughout the movement.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your calves without rolling your ankles outward or inward.
Lower your heels under control to the stretched position and repeat for the planned number of repetitions.

name: Safety Bar Squat
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at a height you can step under with a slight knee bend, and set the safety pins just below the bottom of your squat.
Step under the bar so the padded yoke rests across your upper back and traps, and take one handle in each hand in front of your shoulders.
Brace your core, stand up to lift the bar off the hooks and take two or three short steps back.
Set your feet about shoulder-width apart with your toes turned slightly out, and point your elbows down and forward.
Take a deep breath, brace, and bend your knees and hips together, knees moving in line with your toes.
Lower under control until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and your whole foot on the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand up, straightening your knees and hips together, and breathe out near the top.
After the last rep, walk forward into the rack and set the bar on the hooks.

name: Jumping Lunge
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and the back heel raised, feet about hip-width apart side to side. Brace your core.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to it. Keep your torso upright.
Push hard through the whole front foot and the ball of the back foot and jump straight up, swinging your arms in opposition.
Switch legs in the air so the back foot comes forward and the front foot goes back.
Land softly in a lunge with the other foot in front, bending both knees to absorb the impact.
Go straight into the next jump and keep alternating legs until the set is done.

name: Jogging in Place
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed by your sides, and your gaze forward.
Increase your pace into a light jog, landing softly on the balls of your feet and keeping your steps quick and controlled.
Keep your chest lifted, shoulders relaxed, and core gently braced so your torso stays upright without leaning forward or backward.
Lift your knees only slightly, keeping the steps small.
Swing your arms close to your body, with your elbows bent, to help maintain rhythm and balance.
Breathe steadily throughout the movement, using a pace that allows you to stay in control.
Continue for the planned time, then slow to a march before stopping.

name: Split Jerk
instructions: Set the barbell in the front rack position, resting on your shoulders with elbows slightly in front of the bar. Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and brace your core.
Take a small controlled dip by bending your knees and hips straight down. Keep your chest upright, heels on the floor, and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive forcefully through the floor to extend your hips, knees, and ankles, sending the bar upward from your shoulders.
As the bar rises, quickly split your legs, placing one foot forward and the other behind you. Land with both knees bent, your front shin close to vertical, and your back heel raised.
Punch your arms straight overhead and lock out your elbows as you receive the bar. Keep the bar directly over the middle of your body, with your head slightly forward between your arms.
Hold the split position briefly to confirm balance and control. Keep your torso upright and do not let the bar drift forward or behind you.

Recover by stepping your front foot back partway, then bringing your back foot forward to stand with your feet together. Keep the bar locked overhead until you are fully stable, then lower it safely to the shoulders or rack.

name: Skater Squat
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other foot slightly behind you, keeping the knee bent.
Clasp your hands at your chest and brace your abdomen. Keep the supporting foot flat.
Bend your standing knee and sit your hips back as you lower into a single-leg squat. Let the knee of your lifted leg travel behind and toward the floor.
Lower until the rear knee is close to the floor, keeping it off the ground.
Drive through the middle of your standing foot to return to standing. Keep your knee tracking in line with your toes and avoid letting it collapse inward.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then repeat on the other leg.

name: Double Kettlebell Thruster
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart. Clean two kettlebells into the front rack position, with the bells resting against your forearms and upper arms, elbows slightly in front of your body.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and grip the handles firmly. Keep your wrists neutral and your heels flat on the floor.

Sit down into a squat by bending your knees and hips at the same time. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, if your mobility allows.
Drive through your whole feet to stand up powerfully. Use the force from your legs and hips to start moving the kettlebells upward.
As you reach full hip and knee extension, press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are straight. Keep your ribs down and avoid leaning back.
Finish with the kettlebells directly above your shoulders, elbows locked out, and your head in a neutral position.
Lower the kettlebells under control back to the front rack position, then begin the next repetition.

name: Sandbag Forward Lunge
instructions: Stand upright with the sandbag across your upper back and hold the handles beside your neck.
Brace your core and take a controlled step forward with one foot.
Lower your body by bending both knees.
Keep your front knee tracking in the same direction as your toes.
Push firmly through the heel and midfoot of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Return to a balanced stance, then repeat with the other leg and alternate sides.

name: Countermovement Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Brace your abdomen and balance your weight over both feet.
Dip quickly by bending your hips and knees.
Immediately extend your hips, knees and ankles to jump straight up.
Keep your hands on your hips in the air.
Land softly and bend your hips and knees to absorb the impact.
Stand up and reset before the next jump.

name: Clean Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Squat down and take an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart, with your hands just outside your knees.
Set your hips low, chest up and back flat, with your shoulders slightly in front of the bar and your arms straight.
Brace your core and pull the slack out of the bar without lifting it off the floor.
Push the floor away with your legs and keep the bar close to your shins. Raise your hips and shoulders together until the bar passes your knees.
Drive your hips forward and stand tall with your knees and hips fully extended. Do not lean back or shrug.
Lower the bar along the same path under control and set it on the floor before the next repetition.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Lunge
instructions: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand.
Press both dumbbells overhead until the arms are straight and the weights are above the shoulders.
Brace your core, keep your ribs down, and look straight ahead. Keep the dumbbells directly above your shoulders throughout the movement.
Take a controlled step forward with one foot and lower into a lunge by bending both knees.
Lower until your back knee is close to the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to the floor. Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your torso upright.
Push through the heel and midfoot of your front leg to return to standing, keeping both dumbbells stable overhead.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating sides for the planned number of repetitions.

name: Lateral Hops
instructions: Stand with your feet together on clear floor.
Bend your knees slightly and keep your arms relaxed by your sides.
Push off both feet and hop a short distance to one side.
Land on both feet with a slight bend in the knees.
Hop back to the other side without turning your torso.
Continue with low, quick hops and controlled landings.

name: Vertical Leg Press
instructions: Load the same plates on both sides and set the safety stops just below the lowest point you plan to reach.
Lie on your back on the bench with your hips under the platform and your head, back and hips flat on the pad.
Place your feet flat on the platform about hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out. Hold the handles or rest your hands beside your hips.
Press the platform up slightly to take the load off the safety stops, then release them.
Bend your knees and hips and lower the platform over about 2 seconds, knees tracking over your toes, until your thighs come close to your chest.
Stop before your hips start to lift off the pad, then press through your whole foot to drive the platform straight up.
Straighten your legs at the top without snapping your knees into lockout, then start the next rep.
After the last rep, lock the safety stops with your legs extended before you take your feet off the platform.

name: Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell on the floor a short step in front of you.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, grip the handle with one hand and hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward and stand up hard so the kettlebell floats up close to your body.
As it rises, let your elbow bend and travel up, then punch your hand through the handle at head height so the bell rolls onto the back of your forearm.
Lock out with your arm straight overhead, biceps by your ear, wrist straight and the bell over your shoulder.
Hold for a moment with your ribs down and glutes tight, keeping the free arm relaxed at your side.
Let the bell fall in front of you, close to your body, and hinge only when it reaches your hips, swinging it back between your legs.
Go straight into the next rep, finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Cable Squat
instructions: Attach a short straight bar to the low pulley and select a light weight to practice the movement.
Face the low pulley, hold the bar with both arms extended, and step back until the cable is taut.
Set your posture with your chest up, shoulders down, and spine neutral. Brace your abdominal muscles and keep your weight balanced over your mid-foot.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees. Let the cable provide forward tension, but do not let it pull your shoulders forward.
Lower under control until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as low as you can while keeping your heels down and your back neutral.
Push through your whole feet to extend your hips and knees. Keep your arms long without rowing the bar.
Finish tall without leaning back or locking your knees forcefully, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Seated Leg Extension
instructions: Sit at the end of a flat bench with both knees bent.
Hold one dumbbell securely between both feet.
Lean back slightly, support yourself with your hands on the bench and brace your abdomen.
Keep your thighs on the seat and extend both knees to raise the dumbbell.
Finish with the legs nearly straight, without snapping the knees into lockout.
Bend both knees slowly to lower the weight, keeping your torso angle unchanged.

name: Sun Salutation A
instructions: Stand at the front of your mat with your feet together or hip-width apart and your palms together at your chest.
Inhale and sweep your arms overhead.
Exhale and fold forward from your hips, bending your knees as needed to place your hands beside your feet.
Inhale and lift your chest halfway with a long spine. Exhale and step or jump back to a high plank.
Lower with control through chaturanga with your elbows close to your ribs, or lower your knees first.
Inhale into upward-facing dog with straight arms and your thighs off the floor, or into cobra.
Exhale, lift your hips up and back into downward-facing dog and hold for about five breaths.
Step or jump your feet to your hands, lift halfway, fold, then inhale and rise with your arms overhead. Exhale and bring your palms back to your chest.

name: Chair Sit-to-Stand
instructions: Sit upright on a stable chair with your feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Pull your feet back slightly so they are under or just behind your knees, and brace your core.
Lean your torso slightly forward from the hips until your weight shifts onto your feet.
Push through your whole feet and stand up by straightening your hips and knees.
Finish standing tall with your hips fully extended and your arms still at your sides.
Push your hips back, bend your knees and lower yourself slowly until you are seated again, then repeat.

name: Shrimp Squat
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with your weight centered over the middle of the foot. Bend the other knee behind you and hold that foot with the hand on the same side.
Extend your free arm forward for balance. Keep your chest lifted, hips level, and the standing foot flat on the floor.
Bend the standing knee and sit down slowly. Let the knee travel in line with your toes while keeping the held foot close behind you.
Lower until the rear knee is close to the floor without resting on it.
Press through the whole standing foot to return to standing. Keep your torso controlled and avoid pushing off the floor with the lowered knee.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch legs. Use a light hand support or reduce the depth if you cannot keep balance or control.

name: Weighted Reverse Nordic Curl
instructions: Begin by kneeling on a padded surface to protect your knees, keeping your torso upright and your core engaged.
Hold a weight plate or a dumbbell close to your chest with both hands to add resistance.
Slowly lean your torso backward while extending your knees forward, allowing your body to form a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Keep your hips and glutes tight and avoid letting your lower back arch excessively during the movement.
Lower yourself as far as comfortable without compromising form or causing pain in your knees.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement to maximize tension on the quadriceps muscles.
Engage your quadriceps to pull yourself back to the starting upright kneeling position while maintaining control and stability.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring smooth and controlled motion throughout.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly outward. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other and your elbows pointing forward.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and maintain a neutral spine. Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your feet.
Begin the squat by bending your knees and sitting your hips down between your feet. Keep the dumbbells close to your shoulders and your elbows lifted.
Lower under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as you can while keeping your heels down, chest up, and back neutral.
Push through your whole feet to stand up. Extend your knees and hips together, keeping your torso tall and the dumbbells steady.
Finish standing tall with your knees and hips fully extended. Repeat for the planned number of repetitions without letting your knees collapse inward or your lower back round.

name: Suspension Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the straps so the foot cradles hang about mid-calf height above the floor.
Lie on your back with your feet under the anchor point and place both heels in the foot cradles.
Rest your arms on the floor by your sides, palms down.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels.
Bend your knees and pull your heels toward your glutes, keeping your hips high.
Pause briefly, then straighten your legs slowly while holding your hips up.
Lower your hips to the floor only after the last rep.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your body in one line. Rest your head on your lower arm or support it with your hand.
Bend your top leg and place its foot on the floor in front of your lower thigh or knee. Keep the bottom leg straight.
Brace your abdominal muscles and keep your hips stacked, without rolling your pelvis backward or forward.
Exhale and lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling using the inner thigh muscles.
Raise the leg only as far as you can without rotating your hips or bending the knee.
Inhale and lower the leg slowly until it is just above the floor. Do not let it drop.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then turn over and repeat with the other leg.

name: Band Standing Leg Curl (Low Anchor)
instructions: Anchor the band to the base of a rack at ankle height and loop the other end around one ankle.
Stand facing the rack, step back until the band is taut and hold an upright with both hands.
Stand tall on the supporting leg with a slight bend in that knee and brace your core.
Keep the working knee next to the supporting knee, pointing down.
Bend the working knee and curl your heel back toward your glute against the band.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the foot slowly until the knee is almost straight.
Complete all reps on one leg, then move the band to the other ankle.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, toes turned slightly out. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and press them overhead with your arms straight.
Keep your shoulders active, wrists above your elbows, and dumbbells above your shoulders.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and look straight ahead.
Begin the squat by bending your knees and hips at the same time. Sit down between your hips while keeping both dumbbells overhead.
Keep your heels flat on the floor, your knees tracking in line with your toes, and your arms locked out as you descend.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as you can control without rounding your lower back or losing the overhead position.
Push through your whole foot to stand up, extending your knees and hips together while keeping the dumbbells stable overhead.

name: Suspension Squat
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer so the handles hang around waist height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet about hip to shoulder width apart.
Hold one handle in each hand with your arms extended comfortably in front of you. Step back until the straps are lightly tensioned.
Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders down and back, and your core braced. Keep your weight balanced through your whole feet.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees. Use the straps for balance, not to pull yourself into the movement.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as low as you can while keeping your heels down and your back neutral.
Press through your feet to stand up, extending your knees and hips together. Keep light tension on the straps throughout the movement.
Return to standing with the straps supporting your backward lean, then repeat without losing their tension.

name: Butt Kicks
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest.
Shift your weight onto one leg without leaning your torso.
Bend the other knee and lift that heel toward your glute, letting the thigh move slightly outward.
Lower the foot with control and settle your weight on it.
Repeat with the other leg and continue alternating at a steady pace.

name: Squat Jack
instructions: Lower into a squat with your hands together in front of your chest.
Brace your abdomen and keep your chest lifted.
Make a small hop to bring your feet closer together while staying low.
Hop your feet apart again to return to a wider squat stance.
Land with bent knees that follow the direction of your toes.
Continue opening and closing your stance without standing up between hops.

name: American Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, with the kettlebell on the floor slightly in front of you. Point your toes forward or slightly out, and keep the handle horizontal.
Hinge at your hips by pushing them back, then bend your knees slightly. Keep your chest long, back flat, and neck neutral as you grip the kettlebell handle with both hands.
Hike the kettlebell back between your thighs, keeping your arms straight and close to your body. Load your hamstrings and keep your weight balanced through your whole feet.
Drive forcefully through the floor by extending your hips and knees. Let the hip drive move the kettlebell forward and upward, rather than lifting it with your arms.

As the kettlebell rises, keep your ribs down and brace your abdominal muscles. Guide the bell overhead until your arms are straight, your biceps are close to your ears, and the kettlebell is directly above your shoulders.
At the top position, stand tall with your hips and knees fully extended. Do not lean back or let your lower back arch to reach overhead.
Let the kettlebell fall under control, keeping your arms straight. As it comes down, hinge at the hips and allow the bell to travel back between your thighs.

name: Clean Pull
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell positioned over the middle of your feet.
Grip the bar just outside your legs using a clean grip, with your hands far enough apart to allow the bar to pass close to your thighs.
Bend your knees and hips to reach the bar, keep your chest up, brace your core, and maintain a neutral spine.
Start the pull by pushing the floor away with your legs, keeping your hips and shoulders rising together and the bar close to your shins.
As the bar passes your knees, sweep it slightly back toward your thighs while continuing to extend your knees and hips.
Drive forcefully through the floor and extend your hips, knees, and ankles explosively, finishing tall with the bar close to your upper thighs.
At full extension, shrug your shoulders and allow a slight outward elbow bend as the bar rises near the hips.
Guide the bar back down under control, reset your starting position, and repeat each repetition with consistent posture and bar path.

name: Sled Drag
instructions: Load the sled and fasten its towing straps securely to a shoulder harness.
Put on the harness and face away from the sled with the straps taut.
Set your feet about hip-width apart and brace your trunk before taking the first step.
Lean your body forward into the harness while keeping your spine neutral.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps, driving through the whole foot and keeping steady tension on the straps.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and avoid twisting your torso as you move.
Continue for the planned distance or time, then slow down gradually before stopping and turning around.

name: Tuck Jump
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Push your hips back and bend your knees into a quick dip, leaning your torso forward and swinging your arms back.
Swing your arms forward and up and push hard through both feet to jump straight up.
At the top of the jump, pull both knees up toward your chest while keeping your torso upright.
Lower your legs on the way down so your feet are under you before you land.
Land softly on the balls of both feet, then lower your heels and bend your hips and knees to absorb the landing.
Stand up, regain your balance and start the next rep.

name: Sprint
instructions: Choose a flat, non-slip surface with enough room to slow down safely after the sprint.
Stand with one foot slightly ahead of the other, your weight over the front foot and your elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
Push off explosively, driving the back knee forward while the opposite arm swings forward.
For the first strides, lean slightly forward from the ankles and push the ground back behind you, then rise gradually as you gain speed.
At top speed, run tall with your hips high, drive each knee forward and up, and land on the ball of the foot under your hips.
Pump your arms forward and back from the shoulders, hands rising to about chin height and elbows driving back. Do not swing them across your body.
When the set time is up, slow down gradually over several strides, then walk back and rest before the next sprint.

name: Dumbbell Devil Press
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Hinge at the hips, bend your knees and place the dumbbells on the floor in front of your feet, shoulder-width apart.
Keep hold of the handles and jump your feet back into a high plank, with your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the floor between the dumbbells, then push back up into the plank.
Jump your feet forward so they land outside the dumbbells, with your hips back and your back flat.
Push through your feet, drive your hips forward hard and swing both dumbbells up in front of you and overhead in one motion.
Finish standing tall with your arms locked out and the dumbbells over your shoulders, then lower them in front of you, hinge and set them on the floor to start the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing your thighs.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and lower into a shallow squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Drive forcefully through your feet to stand up, extending your hips and knees while pulling the dumbbells upward close to your body.
As the dumbbells rise to chest height, quickly bend your knees again and rotate your elbows forward under the weights.
Catch both dumbbells at the shoulders in a squat with your elbows under the weights.
Stand fully upright to finish the repetition, keeping your ribs down and your core braced.
Lower the dumbbells under control to your sides, then reset your position before the next repetition.

name: Double Under
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together, a rope handle in each hand and the rope behind your heels.
Set the rope length so that, when you stand on its middle, the handles reach about your armpits.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs, hands slightly in front of your hips, and turn the rope mainly with quick wrist circles.
For a double under, jump slightly higher than for a single jump and keep your body straight, with your chest up and eyes forward.
Spin the rope twice during one jump by making faster, tighter wrist rotations.
Land softly on the balls of both feet with a small bend in your knees, then immediately prepare for the next repetition.
Keep a steady rhythm and stay relaxed through your shoulders, forearms, and grip.

name: Lotus Pose
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you.
Bend one knee and place that foot high on the opposite thigh, close to the hip crease, sole facing up.
Bend the other knee and place that foot on the opposite thigh in the same way.
Let both knees sink toward the floor without pushing them down.
Sit tall with your weight even on both sitting bones and rest your hands on your knees.
Relax your shoulders and breathe slowly for the planned time.
To come out, lift the top foot off first, then straighten both legs slowly.

name: Atlas Stone Load
instructions: Stand close behind the stone facing the platform, with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your hips and knees, bring your chest over the stone and wrap your forearms and hands under its lower half.
Pull the stone off the floor and roll it up onto your thighs, sitting into a deep squat.
With the stone on your lap, move your hands higher around it and squeeze it tightly against your torso.
Drive through your legs and stand up with the stone hugged high on your chest.
Push your hips forward, lean back slightly and roll the stone over the edge onto the platform.
Release the stone only when it rests securely on the platform.

name: Snatch Grip Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Bend at your hips and knees to reach the bar, using a very wide grip. Your hands should be close to the outer markings on the bar, wider than your normal deadlift grip.
Keep your arms straight and place your shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Keep the bar close to your shins.
Set your back in a neutral position, lift your chest slightly, brace your abdominal muscles, and pull the slack out of the bar without lifting it from the floor.
Push the floor away with your legs and extend your hips and knees together. Keep the bar in contact with, or very close to, your legs throughout the lift.
Finish standing tall with your hips and knees fully extended. Do not lean backward or shrug the bar upward.
Lower the bar by pushing your hips back first, then bend your knees once the bar passes them. Return the bar to the floor under control and reset your position before the next repetition.

name: Band Good Morning
instructions: Stand with both feet on the middle of the band and hold its handles in front of your shoulders.
Keep the handles at chin level, soften your knees and brace your abdomen.
Push your hips back as you hinge forward from the hips.
Lower your torso until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings or until your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to standing.
Repeat with controlled movement.

name: Muscle Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell over the middle of your feet. Grip the bar just outside your legs, with your arms straight and your back neutral.
Bend your knees and hips to reach the bar, keeping your chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and weight balanced through your whole feet.
Push the floor away and lift the bar close to your legs. Extend your knees and hips together, keeping your arms straight as the bar passes your knees.
As the bar reaches mid-thigh, drive forcefully through the floor and extend your hips, knees, and ankles. Shrug your shoulders upward while keeping the bar close to your body.
Continue pulling the bar upward with your elbows high and to the sides. Do not bend your knees again to move under the bar.
When the bar reaches chest height, rotate your elbows quickly forward and bring the bar onto the front of your shoulders. Catch it standing tall, with your knees and hips extended.
Keep your elbows in front of the bar, brace your core, and stabilize the bar on your shoulders for a moment.
Lower the bar under control to your thighs and then to the floor, and reset for the next repetition.

name: Zercher Squat Hold
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about waist height.
Bend your knees, place the bar in the crooks of your elbows and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Stand up to lift the bar off the rack, step back and set your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Brace your core, lift your chest and keep the bar pressed against your body.
Bend your hips and knees and lower until your thighs are close to parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for the set time with your heels down, knees in line with your toes and torso as upright as you can keep it.
Push through your whole foot to stand up, then walk the bar back into the rack.

name: Star Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and arms by your sides.
Lower into a shallow squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back. Keep your chest up and your back neutral.
Drive through both feet to jump straight up explosively.
At the top of the jump, spread your legs wide and raise your arms out and up to form a star shape.
Bring your arms and legs back in before landing.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, then lower your heels and bend your knees to absorb the impact.
Reset in the starting position or move directly into the next repetition, keeping each landing controlled.

name: Band Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Anchor the band low and securely in front of you, at about ankle height, for example to the base of a rack.
Sit tall on a chair or bench facing the anchor and loop the band around one ankle.
Move the seat back until the band is taut with the working leg extended and the knee slightly bent.
Keep the other foot flat on the floor and hold the edges of the seat.
Bend the knee and pull the heel back under the seat, keeping the thigh still on the seat.
Pause briefly, then straighten the knee slowly against the band.
Complete all reps on one leg, then move the band to the other ankle.

name: Frog Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width and toes turned out.
Lower into a deep squat and reach your hands down between your knees.
Push through both feet and extend your hips and knees to jump vertically.
Land in the same area and bend the hips and knees to absorb the impact.
Return to the deep squat with your hands between your knees.
Repeat once your balance is stable, keeping both feet coordinated.

name: Barbell Overhead Split Squat
instructions: Take the barbell from a rack, press it overhead with a grip slightly wider than shoulder width and lock your elbows.
Step into a split stance: front foot flat, back heel raised, feet about hip-width apart side to side.
Brace your core, keep your ribs down and your torso upright, with the bar over your shoulders and the middle of your stance.
Lower straight down by bending both knees until your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your front heel flat and your front knee in line with your toes.
Push through your front foot to stand back up, keeping your arms locked and the bar still.
Complete your reps and switch legs. At the end, lower the bar to your shoulders before racking it safely.

name: Rucking
instructions: Choose a sturdy backpack with a hip belt if possible, and place the load high and close to your back. Use a weight plate, sandbag, or tightly packed items that cannot shift during the walk.
Adjust the shoulder straps so the pack sits snugly without pulling your shoulders back; secure the load without restricting normal breathing.
Stand tall with your ribs stacked over your hips, your head neutral, and your eyes looking ahead. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid leaning forward under the pack.
Walk at a steady, controlled pace. Let your arms swing naturally and take short, comfortable steps rather than overstriding.
Keep your trunk steady and continue breathing naturally as you walk.

name: Snatch Balance
instructions: Grip the bar with a wide snatch grip, then place it across your upper traps behind your neck.
Step back from the rack with your feet about hip width apart.
Bend your knees and hips slightly into a short, vertical dip.
Drive forcefully through the floor to extend your legs.
Descend into a squat as you straighten the arms to receive the bar overhead.
Stabilize at the bottom with straight arms, active shoulders and a tight core.
Stand up from the squat while maintaining the locked-out overhead position.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.
Place a barbell over your hips, using a pad for comfort if necessary.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips upward.
Extend your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your glutes tightly.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at mid-thigh height, grip it and step back. Without a rack, deadlift it from the floor with a flat back.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes forward, and unlock your knees to a soft bend of about 15–20°. Keep that bend for the whole set.
Hold the bar overhand with your hands about shoulder-width, just outside your thighs. Your arms stay straight and long; they only hold the bar.
Take a breath, brace your stomach and press the bar into your thighs with your lats. Shoulders down, no shrug.
Push your hips straight back, as if closing a car door with your backside. Your torso tips forward on its own, back flat and neck in line.
Slide the bar down your thighs over 2–3 seconds, keeping it against your legs. Stop when your hips stop moving back, usually just below the knees.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, hips under your shoulders. Breathe out near the top, then breathe in for the next rep.
When you finish, walk the bar back into the rack, or bend your knees and lower it to the floor with a flat back.

name: Seated Hip Abduction
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the machine to ensure your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit on the machine with your back straight and feet flat on the footrests.
Place your knees inside the padded levers, keeping them together.
Grip the handles or sides of the seat for stability.
Exhale and slowly push your knees apart as far as comfortable, engaging your hip abductors.
Pause briefly at the widest point, ensuring tension in the muscles.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Back Extension
instructions: Position yourself face down on a hyperextension bench, securing your feet under the foot pads.
Align your hips with the edge of the pad to allow for full range of motion.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
Start with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your upper body slowly towards the floor by bending at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then engage your lower back and glutes to raise your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Glute Cable Kickback
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley cable machine and secure it around your ankle.
Stand facing the machine, holding onto the frame for support.
Shift your weight onto your non-working leg and slightly bend your knee.
With a slight bend in your working leg's knee, extend your leg backward in a controlled motion.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, ensuring your back remains straight.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Machine Hip Thrust
instructions: Adjust the machine seat and backrest to fit your body size, ensuring that your shoulders are comfortably supported.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and position your feet flat on the platform, shoulder-width apart.
Secure the lap pad across your hips, ensuring it is snug but not too tight.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Position yourself close to the barbell so that it is over the middle of your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your body, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Grip the barbell with both hands inside your knees, using a double overhand or mixed grip.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back before initiating the lift.
Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees to lift the barbell, keeping it close to your body.
Stand fully upright with shoulders back at the top of the lift.
Lower the barbell back to the ground in a controlled manner by bending at the hips and knees.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Secure the strap around your ankle.
Stand sideways to the machine with your strapped leg farthest from it.
Hold onto the machine or a stable surface for support.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core.
Slowly abduct your leg away from your body, keeping it straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Return to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and slightly bend the knee.
Hinge at the hips, extending your right leg straight behind you while lowering the dumbbell towards the ground.
Keep your back straight and shoulders retracted as you lower the weight.
Lower until your torso is parallel to the ground or you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Return to the starting position by driving through your left heel and bringing your right leg forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you take a step backward with your right foot.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees. Your front knee should be directly above your ankle.
Push through the heel of your left foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg stepping back to complete one full repetition.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Glute Machine Kickback
instructions: Set the lever so the roller meets the middle of your sole when your thigh is under your hip and your knee is bent about 90°.
Step onto the platform facing the pads, weight behind you, and lean the front of your hips into the upright pad with both hip bones square to it.
Rest your forearms on the arm pads and hold the handles. They keep you in place; you don't pull on them.
Stand on one leg, foot flat under your hip and knee soft. Put the heel and arch of the other foot on the roller, toes pointing down.
Brace your abs, ribs down, and push the roller back through your heel. Hip and knee straighten together, as if you were pushing the floor away behind you.
Stop when your thigh is about 30° behind vertical and squeeze your glute for half a second. The foot stays low; height isn't the goal.
Take about 2 seconds to bring the knee back to 90° and stop just before the weight touches down.
Finish every rep on one leg, then switch, starting with the weaker side if there is one. Step off only once your foot is off the roller.

name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes turned slightly out.
Hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands close to your chest, elbows pointing down.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body by bending at the hips and knees.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as your flexibility allows.
Ensure your knees are tracking over your toes and not caving inward.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs and keeping your back upright.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench or elevated surface.
Bend one knee and place your foot flat on the floor, while extending the other leg straight out.
Place a dumbbell on the hip of the bent leg, holding it securely with your hand.
Engage your core and drive through the heel of the bent leg to lift your hips towards the ceiling.
At the top of the movement, your body should form a straight line from shoulders to knee.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and hold for a moment before lowering back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Barbell Good Morning
instructions: Begin by setting up a barbell on a squat rack at shoulder height.
Position yourself under the barbell, resting it across your upper back and shoulders. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the bar off the rack by extending your legs and stepping back to clear the rack.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Engage your core and keep your chest up. Maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge at the hips by pushing them backward while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the ground or as far as your flexibility allows without rounding your back.
Reverse the movement by driving through your heels and extending your hips to return to the starting position.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms at your sides with palms facing down.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes as you lift your hips off the ground.
Lift until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the position for a moment, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell upright on your hips with both hands.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, ensuring your glutes are fully contracted.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
instructions: Begin by sitting on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench and your feet flat on the ground, hip-width apart.
Roll a barbell over your legs until it is positioned directly above your hips. Use a pad to cushion your hips if necessary.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes as you drive through your heels to lift your hips towards the ceiling.
Ensure that your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without touching the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Back Extension
instructions: Position yourself face down on a hyperextension bench with your hips aligned with the edge of the pad.
Secure your feet under the foot pads to maintain stability.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
Start with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly lower your upper body towards the floor by bending at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Descend until you feel a slight stretch in your hamstrings or until your torso is approximately perpendicular to the floor.
Engage your lower back muscles and glutes to raise your torso back to the starting position.
Avoid hyperextending your back at the top of the movement.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands, letting it hang between your legs.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Bend your knees and push your hips back to lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not extend past them.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Set the bar hooks at about mid-thigh height and the safety stops just below your lowest point, roughly mid-shin.
Stand behind the bar, feet hip-width and parallel, so it touches your thighs and sits over mid-foot. The track won't move; your feet set the path.
Take an overhand grip about shoulder-width, hands just outside your thighs, and rotate the bar off the hooks. No step back: you're already in position.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and unlock your knees to a soft bend of about 15–20°. That knee angle doesn't change until the last rep.
Push your hips straight back. Your torso tips forward as the bar slides down your thighs, back flat, eyes on the floor 1–2 m ahead.
Lower over 2–3 seconds and stop when your hips stop traveling back, usually with the bar just below the knees, well above the stops.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes until you stand tall, hips under shoulders. Re-hook the bar only from this upright position, never from the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge off Step
instructions: Stand on a step or platform with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Engage your core and step back with one foot, lowering your body into a lunge until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle and your back knee hovers just above the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position on the step.
Repeat on the other leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Good Morning
instructions: Set the bar of the Smith Machine at shoulder height and position yourself under it, resting the bar across your upper traps.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Unlock the bar by rotating it forward and take a step back to clear the safety stops.
Keep your chest up and core engaged as you hinge at the hips, pushing them backward.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Reverse the movement by driving through your heels and extending your hips to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hip Thrust Smith Machine
instructions: Position a bench perpendicular to the Smith machine. Sit on the ground with your upper back against the bench.
Slide your legs under the Smith machine bar and position it across your hip crease, using a pad or towel for comfort if needed. Rotate the bar off the hooks once you are set.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips upward, extending them fully while keeping your upper back in contact with the bench.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, ensuring your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position without touching the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Back Extension With Dumbbell
instructions: Begin by lying face down on a hyperextension bench, securing your feet under the foot pads.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands against your chest.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly lower your upper body towards the floor by bending at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Engage your lower back muscles to raise your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lateral Monster Walk
instructions: Place a resistance band around your legs just above your knees.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a squat position, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Engage your core and maintain tension in the band throughout the movement.
Step laterally to the right with your right foot, followed by your left foot, maintaining the squat position.
Take 3-5 steps to the right, then reverse the movement by stepping to the left with your left foot, followed by your right foot.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions or time.

name: Bulgarian Squat
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench or elevated surface.
Extend one leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench.
Keep your chest up and core engaged.
Lower your hips by bending your front knee until your thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Bird Dog
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Engage your core to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Simultaneously extend your right arm forward and left leg backward until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for a moment, ensuring your hips remain level and your back does not arch.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement with your left arm and right leg.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Band Hip Abduction
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place a resistance band around your legs, just above your knees.
Keep your back straight and engage your core muscles.
Slowly push your knees outward against the resistance of the band, keeping your feet stationary.
Hold the position for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Side Lying Hip Abduction
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor or a mat. Bend your bottom knee to about 90 degrees, shin pointing back, as your base.
Prop your upper body up on your straight bottom arm, hand flat a little ahead of the shoulder. Head up, eyes forward.
Put your top hand flat on the floor in front of your stomach. Pressing it down helps keep your pelvis from rolling back.
Straighten your top leg in line with your torso and stack your top hip over the bottom one, toes pointing forward, not up.
Lead with your heel and lift for about 2 seconds, to roughly 40-45 degrees or until your pelvis starts to roll back.
Pause briefly with the knee straight, then take about 2 seconds to lower along the same arc until the leg touches the bottom one.
Go into the next rep without bouncing. After the last one, turn over and do the same number on the other side.

name: Single Leg Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.
Rest your arms along the top of the bench for support.
Lift one foot off the floor, keeping that knee bent and raised, while the other foot stays flat on the ground.
Drive through the heel of the grounded foot to lift your hips towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Band Hip Abduction
instructions: Place a resistance band around your legs, just above your knees.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slowly move one leg out to the side against the resistance of the band, keeping your toes pointing forward.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum tension on the band.
Return your leg to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

name: Band Lying Clamshells
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above the knees.
Rest your head on your lower arm and place your upper hand on the floor in front of you for support.
Keep your feet together and engage your core.
Lift your top knee as high as possible without moving your pelvis or separating your feet.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the knee back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.
Place a dumbbell horizontally across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips towards the ceiling.
At the top of the movement, your body should form a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and hold for a moment.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without touching the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Glute Bridge Single Leg
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Extend one leg straight out, keeping it in line with your opposite thigh.
Engage your core and press through the heel of the grounded foot to lift your hips towards the ceiling.
At the top of the movement, your body should form a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the position briefly while squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Kneeling Resistance Band Glute Kickback
aliases: Resistance Band Kickback on All Fours
instructions: Pick a long loop band, light or medium to start. A mini band is too short to reach from your foot to your hand.
Get on all fours: hands flat under your shoulders, arms straight, knees under your hips, back flat, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hook one end of the band around the sole of your working foot, across the arch just in front of the heel.
Pin the other end to the floor under the heel of your palm on the same side.
Slide that hand forward or back until the band is just taut with your knee down.
Brace your stomach lightly, ribs down. Lift the working knee just off the floor and drive the foot straight back as the knee straightens.
Stop when the leg is straight and in line with your body: foot at about hip height, toes pointing down, heel pushing back.
Squeeze the glute and hold for a second. Your hips stay level and square to the floor, and your lower back doesn't move.
Take about 2 seconds to bend the knee and bring it back under your hip, tap the floor lightly and go again. Finish every rep on one leg, then switch.

name: Mini Band Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a mini resistance band just above your knees.
Engage your core and press your lower back into the floor.
Push through your heels to lift your hips towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees at the peak of the bridge.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Engage your core to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Lift one leg, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, and drive the sole of your foot towards the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a brief moment.
Lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Band Standing Balance Glute Kickback
instructions: Secure a resistance band around your ankles.
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and engage your core.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and slightly bend the knee.
Lift your right foot off the ground and extend it backward, keeping the leg straight.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position without touching the ground.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Barbell Rear Lunge On Step
instructions: Stand upright on a low step or platform with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip.
Make sure there is enough space behind the step to lunge back onto the floor.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
Step back with one leg off the step onto the floor, landing on the ball of the foot, and lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your front foot to bring the back leg onto the step and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Side Plank Hip Abduction
instructions: Begin by lying on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Place your elbow directly under your shoulder to support your upper body.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Once in the side plank position, lift your top leg as high as possible without compromising form.
Hold the position briefly, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position.
Maintain a stable core throughout the movement and avoid letting your hips drop.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Rest your arms along the top of the bench for support.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips upward, extending them fully while keeping your chin tucked.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a moment.
Lower your hips back down in a controlled manner to return to the starting position.

name: Cable Pull Through
instructions: Set the cable machine to the lowest setting and attach a rope handle.
Stand facing away from the machine, straddling the cable with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the rope handle with both hands between your legs, palms facing each other.
Step forward to create tension in the cable, keeping your arms straight.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back while maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you lower your torso until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips forward to return to the starting position.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement without hyperextending your lower back.

name: Band Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Secure a resistance band to a stable anchor point at floor level.
Lie face down on a bench with your hips at the edge and legs hanging off.
Loop the resistance band around your ankles.
Grip the sides of the bench for stability.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your legs upward by extending your hips.
Raise your legs until they are in line with your torso, keeping them straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Frog Pump
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Bring the soles of your feet together, allowing your knees to fall outward to the sides.
Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes as you lift your hips off the ground.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your glutes tightly.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without touching the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Child’s Pose
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your big toes touching and knees spread apart about hip-width.
Sit back on your heels and slowly bend forward, extending your arms in front of you on the floor.
Lower your torso between your thighs and rest your forehead on the mat.
Keep your arms extended forward with palms facing down or alongside your body with palms facing up.
Hold the position for several breaths, focusing on deep, even breathing.

name: Deadlift from Blocks
instructions: Set up blocks or plates to elevate the barbell to your desired height, typically just below or at knee level.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, positioning the mid-foot under the barbell.
Grip the barbell with a shoulder-width overhand or mixed grip.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly.
Lift the barbell by extending your hips and knees simultaneously, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand fully upright at the top of the lift, squeezing your glutes.
Lower the barbell back to the blocks in a controlled manner by hinging at the hips and bending your knees.

name: Standing Cable Hip Extension
instructions: Set the pulley to the lowest position and fasten the ankle cuff around one ankle.
Stand facing the cable tower and place both hands on the frame at chest height.
Lean your torso forward about 30 to 40 degrees, keep your back flat and brace your core.
Put your weight on the other leg with a slight knee bend and start with the cuffed foot just in front of it, with light tension in the cable.
Drive the cuffed leg straight back from the hip until the knee is straight and the leg lines up with your torso.
Squeeze your glute for a moment at the end, keeping your hips square to the machine.
Bring the leg forward slowly to the start. After the set, switch the cuff to the other ankle.

name: Split Squat Front Foot Elevated
instructions: Set a barbell across your upper back and stand in front of a platform or step, about 6-12 inches high.
Place your right foot on the platform, ensuring your heel is secure.
Step back with your left foot into a split stance, keeping your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your right knee does not extend beyond your toes and your left knee hovers just above the floor.
Push through the heel of your right foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Seated Figure 4 Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your right ankle over your left knee, forming a 'figure 4' shape with your legs.
Keep your back straight and gently lean forward from the hips, bringing your chest towards your legs.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right hip and glute.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch on the opposite side.

name: Pigeon Pose
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on your hands and knees.
Bring your right knee forward towards your right wrist. Angle your right shin under your torso and bring your right foot to the front of your left knee.
Slide your left leg back, straightening the knee and lowering the front of the thigh to the floor.
Square your hips towards the mat, ensuring they are not tilted to one side.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, and as you exhale, fold forward over your right leg, resting on your forearms or extending your arms forward.
Hold the position for 30 seconds to 2 minutes, breathing deeply.
To release, push back through the hands and lift your hips, returning to a tabletop position.
Repeat on the opposite side.

name: Lying Knee To Chest Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms at your sides.
Bend your right knee and slowly bring it towards your chest, using both hands to gently pull it closer.
Keep your left leg extended on the floor, ensuring your lower back remains in contact with the mat.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply and relaxing into the position.
Release your right knee and return to the starting position.
Repeat the stretch with your left knee.

name: Glute Bridge on Bench
instructions: Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.
Place your feet hip-width apart and position them so that your shins are vertical when you lift your hips.
Rest your arms on the bench for stability or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes as you lift your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, ensuring maximum contraction in the glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hip Hinge
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Engage your core to stabilize your spine.
Begin the movement by pushing your hips back as if reaching them toward a wall behind you.
Keep your knees slightly bent and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Lower your torso until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your chest open and shoulders back.
Reverse the motion by driving through your heels and extending your hips to return to the starting position.

name: Side Plank Clamshell
instructions: Start by lying on your side with your legs stacked and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your bottom hand on the floor directly under your shoulder and keep that arm straight.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground into a side plank position, maintaining a straight line from head to knees.
While holding the plank, keep your feet together and lift your top knee as high as possible without rotating your hips backward.
Lower the knee back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Seated Good Morning
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell across your upper back, ensuring it is not resting on your neck.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Inhale deeply, then hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and head aligned with your spine.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor or as far as your flexibility allows.
Exhale as you return to the starting position by contracting your glutes and hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Diagonal Kickback
instructions: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach an ankle cuff to the working ankle.
Face the machine and hold its frame with one hand, with the other hand on your hip.
Place the cuffed leg slightly across behind the support leg, keeping the pelvis facing the machine.
Shift your weight onto the standing leg without locking the knee.
Keeping the working leg mostly straight, move it back and diagonally out to the side in a controlled arc.
Slowly bring the leg back to the starting position while keeping tension on the cable.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then attach the cuff to the other ankle and repeat.

name: Glutes Roll
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place a foam roller under your glutes.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee to target the right glute.
Place your hands on the floor behind you for support.
Shift your weight onto the right glute and slowly roll back and forth from the top of the glute to the bottom.
Continue rolling for 30-60 seconds, focusing on any tight or tender areas.
Switch sides by crossing your left ankle over your right knee and repeat the process for the left glute.

name: Standing Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. You can hold onto a stable surface like a wall or chair for balance.
Shift your weight onto your left leg, keeping it slightly bent.
Lift your right leg out to the side as high as you can without tilting your torso. Keep your toes pointing forward.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

name: Single Leg Weighted Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place a weight, such as a dumbbell or plate, on your pelvis, holding it securely with both hands.
Extend one leg straight out, keeping it in line with your opposite thigh.
Engage your core and press through the heel of the grounded foot to lift your hips towards the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, ensuring your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the bridge position for a moment before slowly lowering your hips back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side before switching to the other leg.

name: Figure 4 Stretch on Chair
instructions: Sit upright on a sturdy chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Lift your right foot and place your right ankle on your left knee, forming a 'figure 4' shape with your legs.
Keep your back straight and gently lean forward from the hips until you feel a stretch in your right hip and glute.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply and maintaining a relaxed posture.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Belt Squat Machine Romanian Deadlift with V-Grip
instructions: Set the belt squat machine to a light starting load and attach the V-grip handle to the machine’s designated lifting point according to the equipment design.
Stand on the platform facing the machine with your feet about hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and take the V-grip with both hands using a neutral grip, keeping your arms straight and shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Stand tall to lift the load, positioning the handle close to your body with your knees softly bent, chest proud, and spine neutral.
Begin the repetition by pushing your hips backward while allowing the handle to travel downward close to your legs.
