Keep your shins nearly vertical, maintain a slight bend in the knees, and lower only until you feel a strong stretch through your hamstrings without rounding your lower back.
Drive your feet into the platform and extend your hips to return to standing, keeping the handle close and your arms relaxed.
Finish with your hips fully extended and glutes squeezed, then repeat under control without leaning backward or jerking the load.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch with Hand Support
instructions: Sit on the floor with your feet wider than your hips, knees bent about 90 degrees and heels on the floor.
Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, arms straight, and lean back just enough to feel balanced.
Lower both knees to the right: right shin across the front of your body, left shin out to the side and pointing back.
Lift your chest so your lower back stays long even with the slight lean.
Pivot on your heels and raise both knees until they point up and both feet are flat.
Carry on turning and lower the knees to the left into the opposite 90/90, left shin in front.
Pause briefly on each side, then switch back, alternating to the end of the set.

name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor and extend your bottom arm along the floor above your head. Rest your head on that arm and place your top hand on the floor in front of your chest.
Bend your hips slightly and your knees to about 90 degrees, with your hips, knees and feet stacked.
Brace your abs lightly to keep your pelvis still.
Keeping your feet together, rotate your top thigh outward and lift the knee as high as you can without your pelvis rolling back.
Pause for a moment at the top.
Lower the knee slowly until it rests on the bottom knee.
Finish all reps on one side, then roll over and repeat on the other side.

name: Band Deadlift
instructions: Stand with both feet on the middle of the band and hold one handle in each hand with straight arms.
Set your feet so the band is secure under your arches.
Brace your abdomen, pull your shoulders down and back slightly, and keep your chest open.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower the handles near your shins.
Lower the handles near the shins only as far as you can keep your back in a neutral position.
Drive through your feet and extend your hips and knees at the same time to stand tall.
Finish upright with your hips fully extended and glutes squeezed.
Lower under control by hinging at the hips and repeat for the planned number of repetitions.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your feet planted wider than your hips, knees bent about 90 degrees and heels down.
Lower both knees to the right into a 90/90: right shin across the front of your body, left shin out to the side and pointing back.
Press your palms together in front of your chest, elbows out, and sit tall with your hands off the floor.
Pivot on your heels and lift both knees until they point at the ceiling, feet flat in the middle.
Keep turning and lower both knees to the left into the opposite 90/90, left shin now in front.
Pause for a second with your chest up and both sit bones on the floor, then lift the knees and head back to the right.
Count one rep each time you arrive on a side and keep alternating to the end of the set.

name: Mini Band Hip Thrust
instructions: Put a mini band just above your knees and sit in front of a stable bench with your upper back against its edge.
Bend your knees and place both feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Brace your abdomen and keep your chin lightly tucked.
Press through both feet and keep pushing your knees out against the band as you lift your hips, with your upper back supported.
Finish when your shoulders, hips and knees form a line, then squeeze your glutes.
Lower your hips under control and repeat without bouncing.

name: Fire Hydrant Kick
instructions: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and spread your weight evenly over both hands and the supporting knee.
Keep the working knee bent at about 90 degrees and lift it out to the side until your thigh is level with your hip.
Hold the thigh at that height and straighten the knee to kick the leg out to the side.
Pause briefly with the leg fully extended at hip height.
Bend the knee back to 90 degrees with the thigh still raised, then lower the knee under your hip.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs.

name: Skater Jumps
instructions: Stand on your right leg with the knee bent and the hips back, the left leg bent behind it with the foot off the floor. Keep your chest up and core braced.
Push off hard through your right leg and jump sideways to the left.
Land softly on the ball of your left foot and let the heel settle, with the knee bent over the toes and the hips pushed back.
Let your right leg swing behind your left leg without touching the floor, and swing your right arm across your body toward the left knee.
Absorb the landing, then push off your left foot right away and jump to the right, landing on your right leg in the same position.
Keep alternating sides in a steady rhythm for the planned number of reps.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
aliases: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
instructions: Sit tall on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot on the floor outside your left thigh.
Fold the lower leg underneath you so its foot rests beside the opposite hip.
Place your right hand on the floor behind your hips for support.
Wrap your left arm around your raised right knee while keeping your chest lifted.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and gently rotate your torso to the right.
Hold the position for several slow breaths, then return to center and repeat on the other side.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Stand wider than shoulder width with your toes turned out.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand between your legs with straight arms.
Brace your abdomen and keep your back neutral.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower both weights close to the floor.
Drive through both feet and extend your hips and knees to stand.
Lower the dumbbells under control and repeat.

name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Straddle the bar facing away from the landmine anchor, with your feet hip-width apart and the loaded end in front of you.
Grip the sleeve or the end of the barbell with both hands, straighten your arms, and stand tall with your chest up, shoulders pulled down and back, and core braced.
Begin the repetition by pushing your hips backward while keeping a slight bend in your knees and maintaining a neutral spine.
Allow the bar to travel downward close to your body as your torso leans forward, keeping your arms straight and your weight balanced through your mid-foot and heels.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings while maintaining a flat back and controlled position; do not round your lower back or force excessive depth.
Drive your hips forward and press through your feet to return to standing, squeezing your glutes as you finish with your hips fully extended.
Keep the movement controlled throughout the set, avoiding jerking the bar, squatting deeply, or leaning backward at the top.

name: Lying Figure 4 Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left thigh, just above the left knee, forming a figure 4 shape.
Lift the supporting foot and hold behind that thigh with both hands.
Gently pull your left leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in your right glute and outer hip.
Keep your head, shoulders and lower back relaxed on the floor. Do not force your right knee down.
Hold the stretch while breathing slowly and steadily.
Release with control, return both feet to the floor, then repeat on the other side.

name: Sumo Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand upright holding the bar at your thighs, with feet wider than shoulder width and toes turned out.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip inside your legs and keep your knees slightly bent.
Set your back flat, brace your core, and pull your shoulders down and back. Keep your chest open and your neck neutral.
To lower the bar, keep a slight bend in your knees and push your hips back. Let the bar travel straight down close to your thighs and shins.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings and inner thighs while maintaining a flat back. Do not force the bar lower by rounding your lower back.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing, squeezing your glutes at the top. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Repeat with controlled tempo. Stop the set if you cannot keep your back neutral or the bar drifts away from your legs.

name: 45-Degree Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down with your trunk supported by the pad of a 45-degree bench and your hips near its upper edge.
Hold the foot rollers firmly with both hands and let the straight legs hang behind the pad.
Brace your abdomen and keep the torso still.
Raise both legs together by extending the hips until the legs align with the trunk.
Pause briefly, then lower the legs slowly to the starting position without changing the knee angle.
Repeat with a controlled hip movement.

name: Kneeling Hip Thrust
instructions: Kneel with your knees about hip-width apart and hold your hands together in front of your chest.
Start with your hips fully extended, glutes lightly squeezed, and ribs stacked over your pelvis. Keep your head and neck neutral.
Send your hips back toward your heels, bending at the hips and allowing your torso to incline forward with a neutral spine.
Lower only as far as you can control while keeping your knees planted and your spine neutral.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes, returning to the tall kneeling position.
Finish with your hips fully extended and glutes contracted, without leaning back or arching your lower back. Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.

name: Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands clasped in front of your chest.
Brace your core and shift your weight onto one leg. This leg stays planted for the whole set.
Step the other leg diagonally back behind the standing leg, as in a curtsy, and land on the ball of that foot.
Bend both knees and lower until the back knee is just above the floor. Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
Keep your chest up, your hips facing forward and the front knee in line with your toes.
Drive through the front foot to stand up and bring the back leg forward without setting it down.
Go straight into the next rep. Finish all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

name: Dumbbell Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing in.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and shift most of your weight onto your front foot.
Step one foot diagonally behind and across your body, placing the ball of that foot on the floor. Keep your hips and shoulders facing forward.
Bend both knees to lower into a lunge until your front thigh is close to parallel with the floor, or as far as you can control comfortably. Keep the front knee tracking in line with your toes.
Push through the heel and midfoot of the front leg to stand up, bringing the back foot back to the starting position.
Return to your starting stance, then repeat with the other leg, alternating sides.

name: Superman Swimmers
instructions: Lie face down with straight legs and both arms reaching overhead.
Brace the abdomen and lift the arms and legs slightly from the floor, keeping the pelvis supported.
Look down and keep the head in line with the trunk.
Raise the right arm and left leg slightly higher as the left arm and right leg lower toward the floor.
Switch pairs and continue alternating without resting the limbs on the floor.
Finish by lowering the arms and legs gently to the floor.

name: Machine Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Load a light plate on the lever, then lie face down on the pad with your hips at its edge and hold the handles.
Place your ankles between the two roller pads, with the rear roller against the back of your lower legs just above your heels.
Let your legs hang straight down with your knees slightly soft and brace your abs.
Exhale, squeeze your glutes and raise your legs back and up, keeping them nearly straight.
Stop when your legs are in line with your torso, with your pelvis still pressed into the pad.
Inhale and lower your legs slowly until they hang straight down again.
After the last rep, let the lever come to rest at the bottom before you take your feet out of the rollers.

name: Glute Bridge March
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, and your arms by your sides.
Place your feet close enough to your hips that your shins are nearly vertical at the top of the bridge.
Brace your stomach and gently tuck your pelvis so your lower back does not arch.
Press through both heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Keep your ribs down, squeeze your glutes, and hold your hips level at the top position.
Without letting your hips drop or twist, lift one foot from the floor and bring that knee toward your chest.
Lower that foot back to the floor with control, keeping your hips lifted.
Alternate the legs while keeping your hips lifted, then lower your hips after the last repetition.

name: Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and shift into an athletic stance with your hips back and chest up.
Keep your core braced, your back neutral, and your weight balanced over the middle of your feet.
Step sideways with the lead foot in the direction you are moving. Do not cross your feet.
Bring the trailing foot in toward the lead foot, returning to your starting stance width. Stay low throughout the movement.
Continue taking controlled side steps for the planned distance or number of repetitions, keeping your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Move back in the opposite direction by leading with the other foot. Keep your hips level, avoid bouncing up and down, and maintain control until you finish.

name: Seated Hip External Rotation
instructions: Sit tall near the front edge of a box or bench, feet flat, knees bent about 90 degrees, hands resting on the box beside your hips.
Lift the working knee a few centimetres so the foot leaves the floor.
Fix the knee at that height and in that spot; it is the pivot for every rep.
Swing the foot in toward your other shin and let the thigh turn outward in the hip.
Stop where the knee or the pelvis would start to move and hold that end for 1-2 seconds.
Swing the foot back out until it is under the knee again, at the same speed.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch legs.

name: Tire Flip
instructions: Choose a tire weight and size you can control with good form. Use a clear, level surface with enough space in front of the tire.
Stand close to the tire with your feet about shoulder width apart. Point your toes slightly outward and keep the tire centered in front of you.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips. Keep your chest up, back neutral, and head in line with your spine.
Reach under the bottom edge of the tire with both hands. Use a firm grip with your arms straight and pull the tire close to your body.
Drive through your feet and extend your knees and hips together to lift the tire. Keep your back neutral and avoid rounding or pulling mainly with your arms.
As the tire rises to about chest height, step one foot forward and bring your knee toward the tire to help guide it upright.
Move your hands from underneath the tire to the front or top edge, then push it forward until it falls onto its opposite side. Keep your fingers clear of the landing edge.

name: Bench Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Set an incline bench securely and lie prone with your hips at its upper edge.
Grip the bench with both hands and let your legs hang freely.
Keep your legs mostly straight and brace your abdomen.
Lift both legs behind you by extending at the hips, keeping your pelvis supported.
Pause briefly at the top without forcing your lower back into an arch.
Lower both legs under control and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Suitcase Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell on the floor beside one foot.
Brace your abdomen and extend your free arm for balance.
Push your hips back and bend both knees enough to reach the dumbbell without rounding your back.
Grip the dumbbell firmly with one hand.
Drive through your feet to stand up, extending your hips and knees together.
Finish standing tall with your hips fully extended and your core tight.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower the dumbbell to the floor under control.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat with the same control.

name: Sumo Deadlift with Short Pull
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, toes turned slightly out, with the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Bend your knees and hips to grip the bar with a narrow overhand grip, hands inside your knees.
Push through your feet to lift the bar, extending your knees and hips together.
When the bar reaches mid-thigh, drive your hips forward powerfully and rise onto your toes if needed.
Use the leg and hip drive to continue the pull, bending your elbows outward as the bar rises near your waist.
Finish upright with the bar near your waist and the elbows slightly bent, without leaning back.
Lower the bar under control by straightening your arms first, then guide it down your thighs and return it to the floor with a neutral back.

name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation
instructions: Sit tall near the front edge of a box or bench, feet flat, knees bent about 90 degrees, hands on the box beside your hips.
Leave the working thigh on the box and lift that foot just off the floor.
Point the knee straight ahead and keep it in that spot for every rep.
Swing the foot out to the side and let the thigh roll inward.
Stop before the knee drifts or the opposite hip lifts, and hold the end for 1-2 seconds.
Bring the foot back under the knee at the same pace.
Do all reps on one side, then change legs.

name: Seated Incline Biceps Curl
instructions: Set the backrest to about 45–60°. The lower it goes, the deeper the stretch and the harder the curl.
Sit with your hips all the way back, feet flat and wide on either side of the bench, knees bent about 90°.
Pick up the dumbbells sitting upright, rest them on your thighs, then lean back until your back, shoulders and head touch the pad.
Let your arms hang straight down beside the seat, palms facing forward. They should hang behind your torso, clear of the bench edge.
Curl both dumbbells at once. Elbows keep pointing at the floor and upper arms stay vertical as the dumbbells arc up toward your shoulders.
Stop with your forearms about vertical and palms facing your shoulders, and squeeze for a moment. Head and back stay on the pad.
Lower on the same arc over 2–3 seconds until your arms are fully straight. Pause in the stretch, then curl again without bouncing.
When you finish, bend your elbows to bring the dumbbells back onto your thighs, sit up, and only then put them down.

name: Bar Cable Biceps Curl
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Exhale and curl the bar towards your shoulders by flexing your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Curl the weights by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue lifting until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Biceps Curl
instructions: Take a straight bar you can curl without swinging from a mid-thigh rack, or deadlift it off the floor with a flat back.
Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees straight but soft and your weight over the middle of your feet.
Take an underhand grip, palms facing forward, hands about shoulder-width so your forearms hang straight just outside your thighs. Wrap your thumbs around the bar.
Start with straight arms, bar on your thighs, shoulders down and back. Lightly brace your abs and glutes so your torso can't rock.
Breathe out and bend both elbows, curling the bar up in an arc. Upper arms stay against your ribs; only your forearms move.
Stop with your forearms about vertical and the bar at shoulder height in front of your upper chest, below your chin. Squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower the bar until your elbows are straight and the bar touches your thighs. Pause briefly, then curl again.
To end the set, put the bar back in the rack, or bend your knees and lower it to the floor with a flat back.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Supinated Curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your arms fully extended and your palms facing your thighs.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and pull your shoulders gently down and back without arching your lower back.
Keeping your upper arm close to your torso, curl one dumbbell upward while rotating your palm from neutral to facing upward as the weight rises.
Continue lifting until the dumbbell is near shoulder height, squeezing your biceps at the top without allowing your elbow to drift forward excessively.
Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control, rotating your palm back toward your thigh as your arm returns to full extension.
Repeat the same movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Exhale as you curl and inhale as you lower, keeping your torso still and avoiding swinging, leaning back, or using momentum.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but soft, a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging at your sides.
Turn your palms to face forward and hold each handle in the middle, knuckles in line with your forearm.
Set your shoulders down and back, stack your ribs over your hips and lightly tense your abs and glutes. Your elbows rest against your sides.
Breathe out and bend both elbows at the same time, bringing the dumbbells up in an arc toward the front of your shoulders. Only your forearms move.
Stop when your forearms are close to vertical and the dumbbells reach shoulder height, palms facing your shoulders. Squeeze there for about a second.
Lower both dumbbells along the same arc in 2–3 seconds until your elbows are completely straight, then curl again without a bounce. Set them down only after the last slow lowering.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the preacher pad.
Sit down and grasp the handles or bar with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Ensure your upper arms are flat against the pad and your chest is pressed firmly against it.
Start with your arms fully extended, but avoid locking out your elbows.
Curl the weight upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical for maximum contraction.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad.
Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor and grasp the EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Position your upper arms on the pad, ensuring your armpits are snug against the top edge.
Start with your arms fully extended and the bar close to the floor.
Curl the bar upwards by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly beyond vertical, without lifting your elbows off the pad.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

name: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
instructions: Pick a load you can curl without swinging, then take the bar from a mid-thigh rack or deadlift it up with a flat back.
Stand with your feet about hip-width, toes slightly out, knees straight but soft. Lightly brace your abs and glutes so your torso can't rock.
Hold the outer angled bends underhand, thumbs wrapped, hands about shoulder-width and equally far from the center. Palms face forward and tilt slightly in.
Breathe out and curl the bar up in an arc from your thighs. Only your forearms move; your upper arms stay against your ribs.
Stop when your forearms are about vertical and the bar is level with your shoulders, just below your chin, and squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower until your elbows are fully straight, then pause briefly before the next rep.
When the set is over, put the bar back in the rack, or bend your knees and lower it to the floor with a flat back.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl (Face Away)
instructions: On a two-stack cable station, set both pulleys to the lowest notch, clip a single D-handle to each and load both stacks equally.
Take a handle in each hand, palms facing forward, and stand between the pulleys with your back to the machine.
Walk out about one step, until both stacks stay lifted with your arms straight and drawn slightly behind your hips.
Stagger your feet with one foot a stride ahead, rear heel up and knees soft. Chest up, shoulder blades back and down, abs braced.
Curl both handles at once, bending only at the elbows. The elbows stay back while your forearms swing forward and up.
Stop with your hands in front of your lower chest, palms facing you and elbows still behind your torso. Squeeze for about a second.
Lower over 2–3 seconds until both elbows are fully straight and the cables draw your arms back. Pause in the stretch, shoulders still back.
When the set is over, walk back toward the machine until the plates rest, and only then let go of the handles.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit on a preacher bench with your feet flat on the floor and your chest against the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, arm fully extended, and place your upper arm on the bench pad.
Keep your wrist straight and your elbow stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the dumbbell upward by contracting your biceps until your forearm is vertical or slightly beyond.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Rope Cable Hammer Curl
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Exhale as you curl the rope upwards by flexing your elbows.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale as you slowly lower the rope back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
instructions: Set the cable machine to a low pulley position and attach a single handle.
Stand facing away from the machine, holding the handle with one hand, arm extended behind you.
Step forward slightly to create tension on the cable and stagger your stance for stability.
Keep your elbow fixed in place and curl the handle towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Spider Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach supported.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, arms fully extended towards the floor.
Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the dumbbells upwards by contracting your biceps.
Pause at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Alternate Dumbbell Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and maintain a straight back.
Curl the right dumbbell upward by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Continue lifting until your forearm is vertical and the dumbbell is at shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left arm while keeping the right arm stationary.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your elbows close to your torso.
Start with your arms fully extended and palms facing forward.
Exhale as you curl the weights up towards your shoulders by bending your elbows.
Pause at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit back on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended, and palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your elbows.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Biceps Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms are comfortably resting on the pad and your elbows align with the machine's pivot point.
Select an appropriate weight on the machine's stack.
Sit down and grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing upwards.
Keep your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Exhale as you curl the handles towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad and your feet are flat on the ground.
Sit on the bench and grip the barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, allowing the barbell to hang in front of you while maintaining a slight bend in your elbows to keep tension on the biceps.
Curl the barbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly beyond, ensuring full contraction of the biceps.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your shoulders relaxed.
Starting with the right arm, curl the dumbbell across your body towards the left shoulder while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Squeeze the biceps at the top of the movement and pause briefly.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat with the left arm, curling towards the right shoulder.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip.
Lean forward slightly and rest your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Start with your arm fully extended and the dumbbell close to the floor.
Curl the dumbbell upwards towards your shoulder by flexing your elbow.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions and switch arms.

name: Zottman Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing inward).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the weights upward by flexing your elbows, rotating your wrists so that your palms face up as you lift.
At the top of the movement, pause briefly and then rotate your wrists so that your palms face downward.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with this reverse grip.
Rotate your wrists back to the neutral position to prepare for the next repetition.

name: One-Arm Machine Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the preacher curl machine so that your upper arm rests comfortably on the pad.
Select an appropriate weight on the machine.
Sit down and position your arm on the pad with your armpit snug against the top edge.
Grip the handle with an underhand grip (palm facing up).
Keep your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Slowly curl the handle upwards by contracting your bicep, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, fully extending your arm without locking the elbow.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: One-Arm Cable Biceps Curl
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand, palm facing forward, and step back slightly to create tension in the cable.
Keep your elbow close to your torso and your upper arm stationary throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl the handle upward by contracting your biceps, bringing your hand towards your shoulder.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Seated Hammer Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench with the backrest upright, vertical or one notch back, and check that the pin is locked.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and sit at the back of the seat: back, shoulder blades and head on the pad.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width apart or a little closer, knees bent to about 90 degrees.
Let your arms hang straight beside the seat, palms facing your thighs, thumbs forward. The dumbbells hang clear of the bench and your legs.
Curl both dumbbells at the same time, thumbs leading. Your palms keep facing each other and your upper arms stay against your ribs.
Stop when your forearms are about vertical and the dumbbells are in front of your shoulders, elbows still at your sides. Hold for a second.
Lower over 2–3 seconds until both elbows are straight again, then go into the next rep without touching the seat.
To finish, lower to straight arms and set the dumbbells down beside the bench with a straight back; don't drop them.

name: One-Arm Preacher Hammer Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat of the preacher bench so that your upper arm rests comfortably on the pad with your armpit at the top edge.
Sit on the bench and grasp a dumbbell with a neutral grip (thumb pointing up).
Extend your arm fully over the pad, keeping a slight bend in your elbow to maintain tension.
Curl the dumbbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your wrist straight and elbow stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your forearm is vertical.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Dumbbell Incline Alternate Supinated Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended and palms facing forward (supinated grip).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl one dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hercules Curl
instructions: Attach a handle to each side of the high pulley on a cable crossover machine.
Stand in the center of the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, arms extended out to your sides, parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows stationary and curl the handles towards your head by flexing your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the movement and avoid swinging or using momentum.

name: EZ-Bar Spider Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to approximately a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip the EZ-bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands shoulder-width apart.
Let your arms hang straight down, perpendicular to the floor.
Keeping your elbows stationary, curl the bar upwards by contracting your biceps.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical for maximum contraction.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Hammer Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the machine.
Grasp the handle with one hand using a neutral (hammer) grip, with your thumb facing up.
Step back slightly to create tension in the cable, keeping your arm fully extended.
Keep your elbow close to your torso and your wrist straight.
Exhale as you curl the handle towards your shoulder by flexing your elbow.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Spider Hammer Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench, ensuring your chest is supported and your arms hang straight down.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your elbows slightly bent and stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Squeeze at the top of the movement, focusing on contracting the brachialis.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Double Dumbbell Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest pressed against the pad and your arms extended over it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Start with your arms fully extended but not locked out.
Curl the dumbbells upward by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Continue lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Chin Up
instructions: Attach the desired weight to a dip belt securely around your waist.
Stand beneath a chin-up bar and grasp it with an underhand grip, palms facing you, shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Initiate the movement by pulling yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Hammer Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Start with your arms fully extended at your sides.
Curl one dumbbell upward by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Continue lifting until the dumbbell is at shoulder level, maintaining the hammer grip.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat with the opposite arm while keeping the first arm stationary.
Alternate arms for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad with your elbows slightly bent.
Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Sit on the preacher bench and grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Start with your arms fully extended, maintaining tension in the cable.
Curl the bar upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your forearms are vertical and your biceps are fully contracted.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining control and tension in your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your feet.
Hold the handles or ends of the band with an underhand grip, palms facing forward, and arms fully extended by your sides.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Exhale as you curl the band upwards by bending at the elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the handles are at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control over the band’s tension.

name: Close-grip EZ Bar Curl
instructions: Load a weight you can curl without hip drive. Take the bar from a mid-thigh rack, or deadlift it up with a flat back.
Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, toes turned out slightly, knees straight but not locked.
Take the two inner bends, next to the center, palms forward and thumbs wrapped. Your hands end up 6–8 in (15–20 cm) apart.
Arms hang straight, bar on your thighs, elbows at your sides. Your forearms angle in toward your hands in a V; that's normal here.
Brace lightly, breathe out and curl the bar in an arc toward your upper chest. Elbows point down and stay by your ribs, never flaring.
Stop when your forearms are vertical and the bar is at shoulder height, just under your chin. Squeeze your biceps there for about a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower to straight elbows, pause a beat at your thighs, then curl again. Rack the bar after the last rep.

name: Cable Squatting Curl
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Squat down facing the machine until your hips are below your knees, keeping your heels on the floor and your back straight.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your elbows against the inside of your knees and keep them there throughout the exercise.
Start with your arms fully extended and the cable taut.
Curl the bar towards your shoulders by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Supinated Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but soft, holding two equal dumbbells by the middle of the handles.
Let your arms hang at your sides with your palms facing your thighs, like the start of a hammer curl. Your elbows rest against your ribs.
Pull your shoulders down and slightly back and lightly tense your abs and glutes so your torso stays still for the whole set.
Curl both dumbbells up together by bending only at the elbows. Once your forearms pass horizontal, start turning your palms up.
Stop with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders and your forearms just past vertical, palms facing your shoulders and little fingers a bit higher than your thumbs. Squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower along the same arc, turning your palms back toward your thighs, until your elbows are completely straight. Pause for a beat before the next rep.

name: Preacher Hammer Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the machine so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad.
Sit on the machine and grip the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Position your upper arms on the preacher bench pad, ensuring your elbows are slightly bent to maintain tension.
Begin with your arms extended, holding the handles.
Curl the weights upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary on the pad.
Raise the handles until your forearms are vertical or just before they reach full contraction.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Single Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Pick one dumbbell, ideally a fixed one, and hold it on end: both palms face up under the top plates, hands side by side, fingers curled around the rim.
Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but not locked. Chest up, shoulders down, abs braced.
Let your arms hang straight so the dumbbell sits vertically in front of your thighs, handle pointing at the floor, elbows at your sides.
Bend both elbows together and curl the weight up. The bottom end tips forward as your forearms rise; let it tip, but don't let it swing.
Stop when your hands reach your upper chest and your forearms are almost vertical, then squeeze for about a second.
Take about 2 seconds to lower until your elbows are fully straight and the dumbbell hangs vertically again.
Bend your knees at the end of the set and set the dumbbell down on the floor or back on the rack.

name: Dumbbell Supinated Preacher Curl
instructions: Adjust the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad with your armpits at the top edge.
Sit down and hold a dumbbell in one hand with a supinated grip (palm facing up).
Extend your arm fully, allowing the dumbbell to hang down without locking your elbow.
Curl the dumbbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arm stationary against the pad.
Continue curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

name: TRX Biceps Curl
instructions: Attach the TRX straps to a secure anchor point at an appropriate height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the TRX handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Lean back slightly, keeping your body straight and core engaged.
Extend your arms fully in front of you, maintaining tension in the straps.
Pull your body towards the anchor by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue curling until your hands are near your shoulders.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Prone Incline Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and position a barbell at the foot of the bench.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly planted on the floor.
Grasp the barbell with a shoulder-width underhand grip, allowing your arms to hang straight down.
Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the barbell upwards by contracting your biceps.
Lift until your forearms are vertical, then pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Arm Blaster Biceps Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Adjust the arm blaster so it fits comfortably around your neck and rests against your upper body.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Position your elbows against the arm blaster, ensuring they remain stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the dumbbells upward by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl Seated
instructions: Set both pulleys of a cable crossover to the lowest position and attach a single handle to each.
Sit on an incline bench facing away from the machine, with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Take a handle in each hand with an underhand grip, letting your arms hang straight down slightly behind your torso.
Start with your arms fully extended, feeling a slight stretch in your biceps.
Curl the handles towards your shoulders by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Wide Grip Standing Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a wide grip, palms facing forward.
Ensure your grip is wider than shoulder-width to target the short head of the biceps.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and maintain a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Curl the barbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Drag Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and palms facing forward.
Begin the movement by curling the dumbbells upwards while dragging them along your torso.
Focus on keeping your elbows back and lifting with your biceps, minimizing shoulder movement.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly beyond.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement for a moment.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Cable Curl
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 45-degree angle in front of a low pulley cable machine.
Attach a straight bar or EZ curl bar to the low pulley.
Sit on the incline bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and arms fully extended.
Keep your elbows close to your body and stationary as you curl the bar upwards towards your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the exercise and avoid using momentum.

name: Close Grip Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell or EZ curl bar with an underhand grip. Your hands should be positioned close together, about 6-8 inches apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and maintain a slight bend in your knees for stability.
Exhale as you curl the bar upwards by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary. Focus on contracting your biceps throughout the movement.
Continue lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then inhale as you slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Drag Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) at hip level.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and slightly behind your body throughout the movement.
Initiate the curl by dragging the barbell up along your body, keeping it as close to your torso as possible.
Focus on contracting your biceps to lift the barbell, ensuring that your shoulders remain stationary.
Continue lifting until the barbell reaches chest level or as high as comfortably possible without moving your shoulders forward.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control and keeping it close to your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Wall Curl
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and pressed against the wall.
Exhale and slowly curl the barbell upwards by flexing your elbows.
Continue curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Ring Muscle Up
instructions: Begin by hanging from the rings with a false grip, ensuring your wrists are above the rings.
Engage your core and pull yourself up explosively, aiming to bring your chest to the rings.
As you reach the top of the pull-up, transition by leaning forward and pushing the rings downwards.
Press your body up into a dip position by extending your arms fully.
Control your descent back to the starting position, maintaining tension throughout your body.

name: Band Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, anchoring the middle of the resistance band under your feet.
Hold the ends of the band with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at your sides.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Curl your hands towards your shoulders by bending at the elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in your arms.
Slowly lower your hands back to the starting position, maintaining control of the band tension.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kettlebell Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your palms facing forward.
Exhale as you curl the kettlebells upward by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue lifting until the kettlebells are at shoulder level and your biceps are fully contracted.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then inhale as you slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Battle Ropes
instructions: Secure the battle rope around a stable anchor point and stand facing the anchor with one rope end in each hand.
Walk backward until there is light tension in the ropes, then place your feet about shoulder-width apart with your knees softly bent.
Hinge slightly at the hips, keep your chest lifted, brace your core, and maintain a neutral spine.
Hold the rope ends with an overhand grip, keeping your arms extended slightly in front of your body without locking your elbows.
Create alternating waves by quickly lifting one hand as you lower the other, driving the movement from your shoulders and arms while keeping your torso stable.
Continue producing even, controlled waves that travel from your hands to the anchor point without allowing excessive slack in the ropes.
Breathe steadily throughout the set and keep your knees bent to absorb the movement rather than rounding your back or shrugging your shoulders.
To finish, gradually reduce the speed and size of the waves, then stand upright and place the ropes down under control.

name: Band-Assisted Chin-Up
instructions: Loop the resistance band securely around the bar and place one bent knee in its lower loop.
Stand under the bar and take an underhand grip with your palms facing you. Place your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms straight, shoulders pulled slightly down away from your ears, and your body in a straight line. Keep your ribs down and brace your stomach.
Pull your elbows down toward your sides and raise your chest toward the bar. Let the band assist you, but keep the movement controlled.
Continue pulling until your chin is clearly above the bar. Keep your legs still and avoid swinging or kicking.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are fully straight again, keeping tension through your shoulders and core.
When finished, carefully remove the knee from the band before releasing it.

name: Lying Cable Biceps Curl
instructions: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a straight bar or EZ-curl bar.
Place a flat bench in line with the cable stack, with the head end closest to the low pulley.
Lie on your back on the bench with your head nearest the cable, plant your feet firmly on the floor, and reach overhead to grip the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Begin with your arms extended toward the pulley, keeping a slight bend in the elbows and maintaining tension on the cable.
Keep your upper arms as still as possible and curl the bar by bending your elbows, bringing it toward your forehead or just above the top of your head.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top without allowing your elbows to flare excessively or your shoulders to lift off the bench.
Slowly extend your elbows to return the bar toward the starting position, controlling the resistance and keeping tension in your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your wrists neutral and avoiding momentum throughout the movement.

name: Standing Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Bring both arms behind your back and clasp your hands together, with your palms facing each other.
Straighten your elbows gently and keep your shoulders relaxed, away from your ears.
Slowly lift your clasped hands slightly away from your lower back until you feel a stretch through the front of your upper arms, chest, and shoulders.
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back or leaning forward.
Hold the stretch while breathing steadily, then lower your hands slowly and release.

name: Rope Climb
instructions: Inspect the rope, anchor point, landing area, and any crash mats before starting.
Stand under the rope and grip it with both hands, one above the other.
Pull yourself slightly off the floor and bend your knees to bring your feet higher on the rope.
Clamp the rope securely between your feet before extending your legs.
Stand up through your legs while pressing the rope between your feet.
Once your legs are extended, slide both hands higher on the rope, one hand at a time.
Bring your knees up again, reset the foot lock, and repeat the stand and pull sequence until you reach the desired height.
Descend under control by lowering your hands and releasing the foot lock gradually.

name: One-Arm Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under the bar and grip it with one hand using a firm overhand grip. Keep your thumb wrapped around the bar.
Hang with the working arm straight and active. Pull the shoulder slightly down away from your ear, brace your abdomen, and keep your ribs from flaring.
Keep the non-working arm close to your body or use it only for balance. Avoid grabbing the working arm or swinging the free arm to create momentum.
Begin by pulling your shoulder blade down and back, then drive your elbow toward your ribs. Keep your body as still as possible.
Pull until the chin is above the bar, allowing a small natural turn toward the working arm without swinging.
Pause briefly at the top with control, then lower slowly until the elbow is fully straight and the shoulder remains active.

name: EZ-Bar Bottom-Half Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and knees soft.
Hold the angled sections of the EZ bar with an underhand grip at about shoulder width.
Let the bar hang in front of your thighs and brace your abdomen.
Keep the upper arms beside your torso and curl until the forearms are parallel to the floor.
Lower the bar slowly until the arms are nearly straight, then repeat the same lower-half motion.

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar or rope to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and forearms parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Push the bar or rope down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, allowing your forearms to come back to parallel with the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and position your hands at chest level.
Keep your elbows close to your body and bend them at a 90-degree angle.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Push the rope down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
At the bottom of the movement, separate the ends of the rope slightly to maximize triceps contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, keeping tension on the triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Dips
instructions: Attach a weight plate to a dip belt and secure it around your waist.
Grasp the parallel bars firmly with your palms facing inward.
Lift yourself off the ground by straightening your arms and support your body weight.
Lean slightly forward to engage the chest muscles more effectively.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lying Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, holding the barbell directly above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head throughout the movement.
Pause briefly when the barbell is just above your forehead.
Extend your elbows to lift the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope with both hands, palms facing each other.
Step forward to create tension in the cable and position your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms overhead, keeping your elbows close to your head and your core engaged.
Extend your arms fully by straightening your elbows, ensuring they remain stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Pushdown
instructions: Set one pulley at the top of the column and clip on a single rope grip. A triceps rope works too; hold just one end.
Take it in your working hand with a neutral grip: palm toward your thigh, thumb toward the cable, little finger by the knob, wrist straight.
Face the machine from a long step away, feet hip-width, and grab an upright of the frame at shoulder height with your free hand.
Push your hips back until your torso leans about 30–40 degrees forward, back flat and both shoulders square to the machine.
Bring the rope to the start: upper arm against your ribs, elbow bent about 90 degrees, hand in front of your lower ribs.
Straighten the elbow, pushing down and slightly back until your hand reaches your thigh and the rope lies flat under your fist. Hold half a second.
Let the forearm rise over 2–3 seconds to 90 degrees. After the last rep, let the rope rise to the start before you let go, then switch arms.

name: Close Grip Bench Press
instructions: Set a barbell in a bench press rack at a height you can safely unrack while lying on a flat bench, then load the desired weight and secure the plates with collars.
Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar, feet planted firmly on the floor, and your head, upper back, and glutes in contact with the bench.

Grip the bar with both hands approximately shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower, keeping your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms. Avoid an extremely narrow grip that causes wrist discomfort.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, brace your core, and create a stable upper-back position while maintaining a natural, slight arch in your lower back.
Unrack the bar with straight arms and position it over your lower chest or upper abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Inhale and lower the bar under control toward your lower chest, allowing the elbows to bend backward at roughly a 30–45 degree angle from your torso.
Lightly touch the bar to your chest without bouncing, then press it upward while exhaling, driving through your palms and keeping your elbows close to your body.

Finish with the elbows extended without forcefully locking them out, stabilize the bar above your lower chest, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before carefully returning the bar to the rack.

name: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, arms fully extended above your chest.
Keep your elbows stationary and close to your head throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells by bending your elbows until they are just above your forehead.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Extend your arms back to the starting position by contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Triceps Pushdown V-Bar
instructions: Set the pulley at the top of the cable column and clip the V-bar's swivel ring onto the cable.
Take one angled handle in each hand, palms down and turned slightly in, hands about 10 cm apart. Wrap your thumbs and keep your wrists straight.
Stand facing the stack about a forearm's length from the column, feet hip-width or narrower, knees soft, chest up. The cable hangs almost straight down.
Pull the bar to your lower chest and pin your elbows to your ribs, bent about 90 degrees, upper arms vertical. The plates are already lifted.
Push the bar down and slightly back in an arc until your arms are fully straight and your hands reach the front of your thighs. Only the forearms move.
Hold the lockout for half a second and squeeze the back of your arms; the stack is at its highest here and still pulling.
Let the bar rise over 2–3 seconds along the same arc. Stop when your forearms are level with the floor, before your elbows slide forward.
When the set is done, let the bar rise to chest height before letting go. Dropped at the bottom, the cable whips it toward your face.

name: Seated Dip Machine
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms are parallel to the floor when gripping the handles.
Sit down and firmly grasp the handles with a neutral grip, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Ensure your back is straight and pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Press down on the handles by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straightened.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows, maintaining control of the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Close Grip Smith Bench Press
instructions: Set a flat bench under the Smith machine. Adjust the bar height so you can comfortably un-rack it with your arms fully extended.
Lie back on the bench and position yourself so that your eyes are directly under the bar. Grip the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Un-rack the bar and lower it towards your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Stop when the bar is about an inch above your chest, then press it back up by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control of the bar throughout the movement.

name: One-Arm Katana Triceps Overhead Extension
instructions: Set one pulley of a cable station to the lowest notch and clip on a single D-handle.
Grab the handle, turn your back to the machine and stand a short step in front of it: feet hip-width, knees soft, ribs down.
Bring the handle up behind your head. Upper arm vertical by your ear, elbow pointing at the ceiling, hand behind your head toward the opposite shoulder.
Reach your free arm across in front of your face and hold the working arm just below the elbow.
Straighten the elbow so your hand travels up and over until the arm points straight above your shoulder. Squeeze there for about a second.
The lowering takes about 2 seconds and ends when the elbow is fully bent and the handle is back behind your head, upper arm still pinned.
Do all your reps on one arm, then switch and match the count.
To finish, lower the handle past your shoulder and step back to set the weight down; never let go of it behind your head.

name: Dips
instructions: Step between the parallel bars or the dip handles of a power tower. On V-shaped bars, stand where your wrists will stay under your elbows.
Grip with your palms facing each other and thumbs wrapped around, the bar in the heel of your hand so the wrists stay straight.
Jump or step up to straight arms. Push the bars down so your shoulders sit low and away from your ears, chest up.
Bend your knees and keep your feet together behind you, off the floor. A light squeeze of the glutes stops the legs from swinging.
Bend your elbows and take about 2 seconds to lower. The elbows go straight back as your torso tips forward 20–30°.
Stop when your shoulders are level with your elbows: about 90° at the elbow, forearms close to vertical. Hold for a beat without bouncing.
Push the bars down and away until your elbows are straight and you're upright again, shoulders still low.
At the top of the final rep, step down onto the frame or a box from the top instead of dropping out of the bottom.

name: High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Set the pulley at the very top of a cable station or lat pulldown tower and clip on a triceps rope.
Hold one rope end in each hand, palms facing each other, with your fists right on top of the knobs.
Turn your back to the stack and bring the rope over your head: hands behind your head, elbows pointing forward beside your ears.
Take a long step out into a split stance, front knee bent and back heel up, far enough that the plates stay lifted at the bottom.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is well past 45° from upright, back flat, abs braced and head between your arms.
From the stretch, straighten your elbows and push your hands forward until your arms line up with your torso, not up toward the ceiling.
Squeeze for a second with your fists together, then take 2–3 seconds to bend your elbows until your hands are back behind your head.
When you're finished, walk back toward the stack until the weight sets down, then lift the rope off over your head.

name: Assisted Machine Dips
instructions: Adjust the weight stack to provide the desired level of assistance.
Step onto the machine platform and grip the handles firmly.
Position your knees on the knee pad or foot platform, ensuring your body is upright.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout.

name: One-Arm Cable Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a single handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, grasp the handle with one hand using an overhand grip.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees for stability.
Keep your upper arm close to your body and your elbow fixed at your side.
Start with your forearm parallel to the floor, keeping tension on the cable.
Exhale and extend your arm downward by contracting your triceps until your arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: One-Arm Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit near the end of a flat bench or any sturdy seat, feet flat and wider than your hips, knees at about 90 degrees.
Grip the middle of the handle, bring the dumbbell to your shoulder and press it straight up until your arm is locked out, palm forward.
Set your upper arm vertical beside your ear, elbow pointing at the ceiling. Free hand on your hip, abs braced, ribs down, no leaning back.
Bend only the elbow and lower for about 2 seconds. Your forearm folds behind your head toward the opposite shoulder; the handle turns upright.
Stop when your forearm is about horizontal and the back of your arm is fully stretched, or higher if that hurts. No bounce.
Straighten the elbow along the same arc until the dumbbell is directly over your head. Hold the lockout for a second.
Do every rep on one arm, weaker arm first, then switch. Afterward, bring the dumbbell forward to your shoulder and down to your thigh.

name: Cable Cross Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach handles to the high pulleys of a cable crossover machine.
Stand in the center of the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.

Face the machine and take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, so the cables cross in front of you, with your elbows bent close to your sides and your hands in front of your chest.
Step slightly back to create tension in the cables.
Keeping your elbows close to your sides, straighten your arms and push the handles down and slightly out until your hands are beside your hips, squeezing your triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Standing One Dumbbell French Press
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, knees straight but not locked. Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your ribs stay down.
Stand the dumbbell on end and cup the top plates from underneath with both palms side by side, thumbs around the handle. The handle hangs between your forearms.
Bring the dumbbell to your chest and press it straight up. At the top your arms are vertical, upper arms by your ears, elbows about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your elbows and take 2–3 seconds to lower the dumbbell behind your head. It stays vertical; only your forearms move.
Keep going until your elbows are fully bent and the lower end of the dumbbell sits near the back of your neck, or stop higher if that depth hurts.
Straighten your arms to a full lockout without snapping into the joint, and hold the squeeze for half a second.
When you finish, bring the dumbbell back over your head to your chest and lower it to your thigh. Never let it drop behind you.

name: Lying EZ-Bar Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit at the end of a flat bench with the loaded EZ bar on your thighs, then lie back so your head rests at the very end of the pad.
Bend your knees to about 90 degrees and plant your feet flat. Glutes, upper back and head stay on the bench for the whole set.
Hold the outer angled handles, right next to the plates, overhand and about shoulder width apart. Thumbs around the bar, knuckles up, wrists straight.
Press the bar to straight arms and let it settle over your forehead, upper arms tilted slightly back toward your head rather than straight up over your chest.
Bend only at the elbows and lower the bar in an arc past your forehead to just behind the top of your head, taking 2 to 3 seconds.
When your forearms nearly touch your biceps, reverse without a bounce and straighten along the same arc until your elbows lock out over your forehead.
