To end the set, bring the bar down to your chest and sit up with it, or hand it to your spotter.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Seated Kickback
instructions: Place your left knee and left hand on a flat bench, with your right foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, palm facing your torso.
Keep your back flat and close to parallel with the floor, core engaged.
Tuck your upper arm close to your side, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend your forearm backward until your arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbow.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Seated Triceps Bench Dip
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench or chair with your hands placed next to your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Extend your legs out in front of you, keeping your heels on the ground and knees slightly bent.
Shift your hips forward off the bench, supporting your weight with your arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to about a 90-degree angle, keeping them close to your sides.
Push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms are parallel to the floor when gripping the handles.
Sit down and firmly plant your feet on the floor, ensuring your back is supported by the seat.
Grip the handles with a neutral or overhand grip, depending on machine design.
Start with your elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Extend your arms by pushing the handles down until your elbows are fully extended but not locked.
Pause briefly at full extension to maximize contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension (Bar)
aliases: Straight Bar Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Set the pulley to the lowest notch and clip on a short straight bar. An EZ cable bar works the same way.
Grab the bar overhand, hands about shoulder-width apart or a little narrower, thumbs wrapped around it and wrists straight.
Turn your back to the stack and lift the bar over your head on bent elbows until it sits behind your head.
Stagger your feet close to the stack, back foot by the frame and front foot forward, knees soft. Lean your whole body slightly forward so the cable can't pull you back.
Start in the stretch: elbows fully bent and pointing up and slightly forward, about shoulder-width apart, ribs down and the plates already lifted.
Straighten your elbows until your arms are vertical and locked out, and hold for half a second.
Only your forearms move; your upper arms stay by your ears.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower the bar along the same arc until it is behind your head again, without letting the plates touch down.
When you finish, step back toward the stack with your elbows still bent until the weight rests, then bring the bar down in front of you.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Start in a plank position with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Place your hands directly under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers touching.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows.
Lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the back of your hands.
Push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Maintain a tight core and avoid sagging or arching your back throughout the movement.

name: Cable Incline Skull Crusher
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 30-45 degree angle and position it in front of a cable machine.
Attach a straight bar or EZ-curl bar to the low pulley.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, ensuring your head is near the top of the bench.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms fully above your forehead.
Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows pointed forward as you slowly lower the bar towards your forehead by bending at the elbows.
Pause briefly when the bar is just above your forehead, ensuring tension on the triceps.
Extend your elbows to return to the starting position, focusing on squeezing your triceps at the top.

name: EZ-Bar Seated Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Grip an EZ bar with both hands using a pronated grip (palms facing forward), hands shoulder-width apart.
Lift the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows, maintaining a controlled motion.
Exhale and extend your arms back to the starting position by contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Cable Cross Body Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a single handle to a cable machine at shoulder height.
Stand sideways to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with your working hand, palm facing down.
Position your upper arm parallel to the floor, elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your non-working hand on your hip or by your side for balance.
Extend your arm fully by pushing the handle away from your body until your arm is straight.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: One-Arm Reverse Grip Triceps Cable Pushdown
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley on the cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, grasp the handle with an underhand grip (palm facing up) using one hand.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart, and slightly bend your knees for stability.
Keep your upper arm close to your body and your elbow fixed at your side.
Start with your forearm parallel to the floor, then extend your arm downward by contracting your triceps.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full extension of the elbow.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, keeping tension on the triceps throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: EZ-Bar Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Attach an EZ bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the EZ bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and slightly bent.
Start with the bar at chest level, maintaining tension in the cable.
Push the bar down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement for maximum contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Underhand Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, and grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Begin with your forearms parallel to the floor, then extend your arms downward by contracting your triceps until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, allowing the forearms to come back to parallel with the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Katana Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope with both hands above your head, elbows bent and close to your ears.
Step forward slightly to create tension in the cable.
Extend your arms fully by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Triceps Cable Kickback
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, holding the handle with one hand, and step back to create tension in the cable.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Position your upper arm parallel to your torso, elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keep your upper arm stationary and extend your forearm backward by straightening your elbow.
Squeeze your tricep at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head throughout the movement.
Pause briefly when the barbell is just above your forehead.
Press the barbell back to the starting position by extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Extend your arms straight above your shoulders, keeping the dumbbells close together.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly when you reach a comfortable stretch in your triceps.
Press the dumbbells back to the starting position by extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Close Grip Push-Up
instructions: Start in a plank position with your body straight from head to heels.
Place your hands directly under your chest, closer than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the exercise.

name: One-Arm Triceps Cable Pushdown
instructions: Attach a single handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand, palm facing down, and step back slightly to create tension in the cable.
Position your upper arm close to your body and keep your elbow fixed at your side.
Exhale and push the handle down by extending your elbow until your arm is fully straightened.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with control, allowing your elbow to bend.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Ring Dips
instructions: Adjust the gymnastic rings to a height where you can comfortably reach them while standing.
Grip the rings firmly with your palms facing inward and arms fully extended.
Lift your feet off the ground, supporting your body weight with straight arms.
Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Press through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Seated Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lift them overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your elbows close to your head and stationary throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Muscle-up
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and initiate a pull-up by pulling your chest towards the bar.
As your chest approaches the bar, lean slightly forward and begin transitioning your wrists over the bar.
Push down on the bar to extend your arms fully, bringing your torso above the bar in a dip position.
Reverse the movement by lowering yourself back to the starting hanging position in a controlled manner.

name: California Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your head, upper back and hips on the pad, knees bent about 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width or a touch narrower, hands not touching. Wrap your thumbs around it; it sits low in your palms.
Get the bar to lockout over your shoulders: unrack it, take it from a spotter, or lie back with it on your thighs and press.
Lower the bar like a skull crusher, elbows pointing at the ceiling, until it reaches your forehead and just past the top of your head (about 2 seconds).
Keep that elbow angle and pull your upper arms down to your sides; the bar travels back over your face to just above your lower chest.
Press straight up from there, exactly like a close-grip bench press, and breathe out as your elbows lock out over your shoulders.
Start each rep from straight arms. After the last, rack the bar, hand it to your spotter, or lower it to your thighs and sit up.

name: JM Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a barbell positioned above your chest, using a grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
Unrack the barbell and hold it steady with your arms fully extended.
Lower the bar toward your upper chest, just below your chin, by bending your elbows and letting them travel slightly forward while staying tucked.
Pause briefly when the bar is a few centimeters above your upper chest, maintaining control and tension.
Press the barbell upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straightened again.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form throughout.
After completing your set, carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench supports.

name: Seated Cable Horizontal French Press
instructions: Set one pulley of a cable station to the very top and clip on a short straight bar.
Put a bench with the back pad set upright right in front of the machine, so you sit with your back to the stack.
Take the bar overhand, hands about head-width apart, sit down and bring it behind your head. Elbows fully bent, pointing up, no wider than your shoulders.
Sit tall with your back on the pad and your feet flat and wide.
If the plates touch down with the bar behind your head, slide the bench a little farther from the machine.
Exhale and straighten your elbows until the bar is above your head. Your upper arms stay beside your head for this part.
With your elbows locked, push the bar forward in an arc until your arms point straight ahead at eye level. Hold it there for a second.
Reverse the path: raise the straight arms back over your head, then bend your elbows and lower the bar behind your head over 2–3 seconds.
To end the set, bring the bar back over your head before you let go or stand up, so the stack can't snap it into your head.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or a sturdy door frame.
Stand facing the anchor point, holding the ends of the band with both hands, palms facing down.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees for stability.
Start with your elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, keeping your upper arms close to your sides.
Exhale as you extend your arms downward, straightening your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position with controlled movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Reverse Grip Cable Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Set the pulley at the top of a cable column or lat-pulldown station and clip on a short straight or EZ pushdown bar.
Grab the bar underhand, palms up, hands about shoulder-width or a little closer. Wrap your thumbs around it and keep your wrists straight.
Stand about a forearm's length from the stack, feet hip-width, knees soft, torso upright. The cable hangs almost straight down in front of your chest.
Pin your upper arms to your sides, elbows fully bent and the bar near your upper chest. The plates should already be off the stack.
Straighten your elbows and push the bar down in an arc to the front of your thighs. Hold the straight-arm position for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the bar rise until your elbows are fully bent, upper arms still at your sides and the plates still up.
End the set by guiding the bar all the way up before you let go. Release it at the bottom and the bar snaps up while the plates crash down.

name: Tate Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your feet, and press them straight up above your chest.
Keep your upper arms still with your elbows pointing out to the sides, then bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells towards your chest.
As you lower the dumbbells, let their inner ends turn inward so they meet just above your chest.
Press the dumbbells back up by extending your elbows, returning to the starting position with arms fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Weighted Bench Dips
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands positioned next to your hips, fingers gripping the edge.
Place your feet flat on the floor, knees bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Have a partner place a weight plate or dumbbell on your lap for added resistance.
Slide your hips off the bench, supporting your body with your arms extended.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until they form a 90-degree angle.
Press through your palms to extend your arms and lift your body back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Close Grip Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting them on your thighs.
Lie back on the bench and bring the dumbbells to shoulder height with palms facing each other.
Position your feet flat on the floor for stability.
Press the dumbbells upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, ensuring your arms are straight but not locked.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: JM Press on Smith
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar just below chest level and position a flat bench underneath it so the bar will travel over your upper chest and lower face area.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor, your head supported, and your upper back and glutes in contact with the bench.
Grip the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower overhand grip, keeping your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your upper chest with your elbows angled forward rather than flared directly to the sides.
Lower the bar slowly by bending your elbows and allowing them to travel forward, bringing the bar toward the area between your upper chest and chin.
Keep your upper arms relatively close to your torso and stop the descent when your forearms are near vertical and you feel a strong triceps stretch without shoulder discomfort.
Press the bar back up by extending your elbows, following the Smith machine’s fixed path while keeping your wrists neutral and elbows controlled.
Finish with your arms nearly straight without aggressively locking the elbows, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
After the final repetition, fully extend your arms and rotate the bar into the Smith machine safety hooks before releasing your grip.

name: Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip.
Lift the barbell overhead, keeping your elbows close to your head and arms fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping them stationary.
Exhale and extend your arms back to the starting position by contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Decline Barbell French Press
instructions: Set a decline bench at a moderate angle and secure your feet under the foot pads.
Lie back on the bench with your head lower than your feet, ensuring your back is supported.
Grip a barbell with a shoulder-width, overhand grip (palms facing away from you).
Extend your arms fully above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows to maintain tension.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly when the barbell is just above your forehead or slightly behind it.
Exhale and press the barbell back to the starting position by extending your elbows, focusing on contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Cable Double-Arm Tricep Kickback
instructions: Attach a handle to each side of a cable machine at the lowest setting.
Stand facing the machine, holding a handle in each hand with a neutral grip.
Step back slightly to create tension in the cables, and bend forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and bend them at 90 degrees.
Extend your arms straight back by contracting your triceps, keeping your elbows stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Knee Close Grip Push-Up
instructions: Start in a kneeling position on the floor. Place your hands directly under your shoulders with fingers facing forward and thumbs almost touching.
Engage your core and keep your back straight from head to knees.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Planche Push-Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position on your toes with your hands flat on the floor beside your waist.
Lean your shoulders forward well past your hands, keeping your arms straight and your body in a straight line.
Lower your body by bending your elbows while keeping the forward lean.
Push back up to return to the starting position, keeping your body straight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Frog Planche
instructions: Begin in a squat position with your feet close together and hands placed shoulder-width apart on the ground.
Lean forward, bending your elbows slightly, and place your knees on the back of your upper arms near the elbows.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands while lifting your feet off the ground, maintaining balance.
Engage your core and keep your back flat, ensuring that your body remains parallel to the ground.
Hold this position for as long as possible while maintaining steady breathing.
To exit, gently lower your feet back to the ground and return to a squat position.

name: Suspension Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach the suspension straps securely to an anchor point above head height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handles with an overhand grip.
Extend your arms in front of you at shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
Lean forward slightly, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to lower your body forward, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Stop when your hands are near your forehead, ensuring elbows remain close to your head.
Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control and form.

name: Weighted Muscle-Up
instructions: Begin by attaching a weight belt around your waist with the desired weight.
Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and initiate the movement by pulling yourself up explosively.
As your chest reaches the bar, transition by leaning forward and pushing down on the bar.
Press your body up until your arms are fully extended above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Overhead Band Triceps Extension
instructions: Secure a resistance band to a stable anchor point near the floor.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding one end of the band in each hand.
Step forward to create tension in the band, and raise your arms overhead with elbows bent and close to your head.
Keep your core engaged and back straight throughout the exercise.
Extend your arms fully overhead by straightening your elbows, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows, maintaining control of the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Close Grip Push-Up
instructions: Position yourself in front of an elevated surface like a bench or step.
Place your hands on the edge of the surface, closer than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you, balancing on your toes, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your body rigid.
Lower your chest towards the surface by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
instructions: Stand or sit with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your right arm overhead, bending the elbow to bring your right hand down towards the middle of your upper back.
Use your left hand to gently push on your right elbow, deepening the stretch.
Hold the position for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your triceps and shoulder.
Release and switch arms, repeating the stretch on the opposite side.

name: Decline Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on an elevated surface such as a bench or step, ensuring your body is in a straight line from head to heels.
Position your hands on the floor directly under your chest, forming a diamond shape by touching your thumbs and index fingers together.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then push through your palms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form.

name: Knee Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Start in a kneeling position on the floor. Place your hands together under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
Position your knees hip-width apart and keep your back straight. Engage your core throughout the movement.
Lower your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above your hands, ensuring you maintain control and tension in the muscles.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.

name: Reverse Hand Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart.
Rotate your hands so that your fingers point towards your feet, ensuring your wrists are comfortable.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the ground.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cobra Push-Up
instructions: Start in a prone position on the floor with your legs extended and feet together.
Place your hands under your shoulders, palms flat on the ground.
Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your chest off the ground, extending your arms fully while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Simultaneously, arch your back and lift your head towards the ceiling, resembling a cobra pose.
Hold the top position briefly, then slowly lower your chest back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lying Cable Skull Crusher
instructions: Set a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley so that your head will be closest to the pulley when lying down.
Attach a straight bar, EZ-bar attachment, or rope to the low pulley and select a manageable weight.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly on the floor, then hold the attachment with an overhand grip and position your arms vertically above your chest or slightly back toward the pulley.
Keep your upper arms mostly fixed, elbows pointing upward, and brace your core to keep your lower back and shoulders stable on the bench.
Inhale and slowly bend only at the elbows, lowering the attachment toward your forehead or just behind the top of your head.
Pause briefly when your elbows are deeply bent and you feel a stretch in your triceps, without allowing your elbows to flare excessively.
Exhale and extend your elbows to press the attachment back to the starting position, squeezing your triceps at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions using controlled movement, keeping tension on the cable and avoiding shoulder movement or swinging.

name: Ring Triceps Extension
instructions: Adjust the gymnastic rings to about waist height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the rings with an overhand grip.
Extend your arms in front of you at shoulder width, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lean forward slightly, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to lower your body while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Lower until your forearms are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Press through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Maintain a controlled motion throughout the exercise.

name: Bird Dog Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a standard push-up by lowering your chest towards the floor, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle.
As you push back up to the starting position, simultaneously lift your right arm and left leg off the ground, extending them straight out in front of you and behind you respectively.
Hold this position briefly, ensuring your body remains stable and aligned.
Return your arm and leg to the starting position as you prepare for the next repetition.
Alternate sides with each push-up, lifting the opposite arm and leg.

name: Triceps Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides as you descend.
Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cross Arms Push-Up
instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Cross your right hand over your left hand so that your arms form an 'X' shape.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Perform the desired number of repetitions, then switch the arm crossing position for balance.

name: Barbell Triceps Pullover
instructions: Begin by lying flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground for stability.
Grasp a barbell with a narrow overhand grip, hands positioned about shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight above your chest, holding the barbell securely.
Bend your elbows to lower the barbell toward your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
Keeping your elbows bent, let your upper arms move back so the barbell travels in an arc behind your head to about bench level or just below.
Pause briefly when you feel a stretch in your triceps and lats, without forcing your shoulders further.
Pull your upper arms back over your face, then extend your elbows to press the barbell up above your chest.
Maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise to avoid using momentum.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form.

name: Chair Dip
instructions: Use a sturdy chair. Sit on the front edge and place your hands beside your hips with your fingers over the edge.
Move your hips off the chair and support your body with straight arms. Keep your chest lifted, shoulders down, and core braced.
Place both feet on the floor and keep your knees bent through the repetitions.
Bend your elbows and lower your hips straight down in front of the chair. Keep your back close to the chair and your elbows pointing behind you.
Lower only until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or stop earlier if you feel discomfort in your shoulders.
Press through your palms to straighten your elbows and return to the starting position. Keep your shoulders away from your ears.

name: Band-Assisted Dip
instructions: Choose a resistance band that lets you perform controlled dips without losing shoulder position or range of motion.
Secure the band around both dip handles so it forms a stable loop in the middle. Check that it cannot slide, snap, or come loose.
Use a platform if needed, grip both bars and place your bent knees in the band.
Press down on the handles to lift your body into the start position. Keep your arms straight, chest lifted, shoulders down away from your ears, and legs controlled in the band.
Begin the descent by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows angled slightly back rather than flaring widely to the sides.
Lower under control until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or until you reach a comfortable depth with no pinching in the shoulders.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the top. Let the band assist you, but keep your torso stable and do not bounce from the bottom.
Finish by supporting your feet on a platform or the floor before removing your knees from the band.

name: Band Assisted Muscle-Up
instructions: Secure a resistance band around the bar and place one foot in its hanging loop.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip. Start in a dead hang with your arms straight, shoulders active, chest lifted, and legs kept under control by the band.
Begin by pulling the bar down toward your upper chest. Drive your elbows down and back, and lean your torso slightly behind the bar as you pull.
Pull explosively until your chest reaches bar height. Keep the bar close to your body and avoid swinging your legs forward.
As your chest comes over the bar, quickly rotate your wrists and elbows over it. Bring your shoulders forward above the bar while keeping pressure through the band-supported leg.
Finish the transition in the top support position with the bar near your lower chest or upper abdomen. Your elbows should be bent and pointing back, not flared far out to the sides.
Press down through the bar to perform a straight-bar dip until your arms are fully extended. Keep your shoulders stable and your body tight at the top.
Lower under control by bending your elbows, bringing your chest back to the bar, then returning to a full hang. Reset your body position before the next repetition.

name: Full Planche Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart on the ground.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands, lifting your feet off the ground.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to toe, keeping your body parallel to the ground.
Lower your body by bending your elbows while maintaining the planche position.
Push back up to the starting position without losing form.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Feet-Elevated Bench Dip
instructions: Place two sturdy benches parallel to each other, far enough apart that you can rest your heels on one bench while supporting yourself with your hands on the other.
Sit on the edge of the bench behind you and place your hands beside your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet. Grip the bench edge firmly.
Extend your legs and place your heels on the opposite bench. Lift your hips off the supporting bench and keep them close to its edge.
Start with your arms straight but not forcefully locked, chest open, shoulders down and core braced.
Bend your elbows straight behind you and lower your body in a controlled motion. Keep your hips close to the bench and avoid letting your shoulders roll forward.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or stop earlier if you feel discomfort in the front of your shoulders.
Press through your palms to straighten your elbows and return to the starting position. Keep your legs straight and heels supported on the other bench.

name: Ring Tuck Planche
instructions: Set the rings to a low height, around hip level or lower, and ensure the straps are even and securely anchored.
Start in vertical straight-arm support with the rings close to your hips and your feet off the floor.
Lean your shoulders forward in front of your hands while keeping your elbows fully locked and your arms straight.
Draw the knees tightly toward your chest while keeping the feet suspended.
Round your upper back slightly, brace your abdominals, and keep your hips lifted until your body is balanced in the tuck position.
Hold the position without bending your elbows or allowing the shoulders to shrug toward your ears.
Bring the shoulders back over the hands and lower the legs to return to vertical ring support, keeping the feet off the floor.

name: Ring Support Hold
instructions: Set the rings to about hip height and check that both straps are even and secure.
Take a firm grip with your body between the rings.
Press down through the rings and straighten your arms until your body is supported above your hands.
Keep the rings close to your hips, with your palms facing in or turned slightly forward.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and turn the rings out slightly so the inside of your elbows faces forward.
Keep your body tight in a straight line, squeeze your glutes, brace your abs, and keep your legs together with toes pointed down.
Hold without bending your elbows, shrugging your shoulders, or letting the rings drift away from your body.
Bend your elbows and lower your body under control when the hold ends.

name: Elbow Lever
instructions: Place your palms on a firm floor at shoulder width with fingers spread and knees bent.
Bend your elbows and place them against the sides of your abdomen, usually near the hip bones or lower stomach.
Lean your shoulders forward over your hands until your weight is supported through your palms and elbows.
Brace your abdomen, bring the legs together and shift forward until both feet lift off the floor.
Straighten your legs behind you until your body is as parallel to the floor as your strength and balance allow.
Press actively through your hands and keep your fingers gripping the floor to control balance.
Hold the position briefly with steady breathing.
To come down, bend your knees and place your feet on the floor under control.

name: One-Arm Wrist Curl Dumbbell
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Rest your forearm on your thigh or a bench, with your wrist hanging over the edge and your palm facing upward.
Grip the dumbbell firmly and allow your wrist to extend downward, lowering the weight slowly.
Curl the dumbbell upward by flexing your wrist, squeezing at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Forearm Curl
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down).
Position your hands shoulder-width apart on the barbell.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Exhale and curl the barbell up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still and your wrists straight.
Pause briefly when the bar reaches chest height, keeping the forearm muscles tight.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Reverse Grip Biceps Curl
instructions: Load the bar lighter than for a regular curl and pick it up like a deadlift, not by curling it off the floor.
Stand with your feet about hip-width and knees straight but soft, the bar resting against the front of your thighs.
Take an overhand grip on the angled sections, hands about shoulder-width so your forearms run parallel, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
Tuck your elbows against your ribs, pull your shoulders down and lock your wrists so the knuckles line up with your forearms.
Curl the bar up in an arc with your knuckles leading. Your upper arms stay vertical beside your body.
Stop when your forearms are vertical and the bar is at upper-chest height, knuckles pointing at the ceiling, and hold for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower it to fully straight elbows, then start the next rep without bouncing off your thighs.

name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and close to your body, with your palms facing backward.
Slowly curl your wrists upwards, lifting the barbell as high as possible without moving your arms.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize contraction.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dead Hang
instructions: Find a sturdy pull-up bar and ensure it can support your weight.
Stand below the bar, reach up, and grasp it with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet off the ground by bending your knees or crossing your ankles.
Allow your body to hang freely with arms fully extended and shoulders engaged.
Keep your core tight and avoid swinging or excessive movement.
Hold this position for as long as you can maintain proper form.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down).
Rest your forearms on your thighs or a flat surface, allowing your wrists to extend beyond the edge.
Start with your wrists in a neutral position, holding the barbell securely.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your wrists downward as far as comfortable.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling a stretch in your forearms.
Raise the barbell by extending your wrists, lifting the backs of your hands as high as you can.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

name: Reverse Grip Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Exhale and curl the bar upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or just past perpendicular to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing the forearms and biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) and rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge of your knees.
Start with your wrists in a neutral position, then slowly curl the barbell upwards by flexing your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the forearm muscles.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner, allowing your wrists to extend fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Rest your forearm on your thigh or a flat surface, allowing your wrist to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrist in a neutral position, then slowly extend your wrist upward, lifting the dumbbell.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment, feeling the contraction in your forearm.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Farmer Carry
instructions: Select a pair of dumbbells with a challenging but manageable weight.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the dumbbells on the floor beside each foot.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips to pick up the dumbbells with a firm grip.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lift the dumbbells off the ground.
Maintain an upright posture with shoulders back and head facing forward.
Begin walking forward slowly and steadily for a set distance or time while keeping the dumbbells at your sides.
Focus on keeping your core tight and avoiding any swaying or leaning.
Once you reach the end of the distance or time, carefully set the dumbbells back down.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Set the cable machine to a low pulley position and attach a straight bar.
Sit on a bench facing the cable machine, with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl your wrists upwards by contracting your forearm muscles, keeping your forearms stationary.
Hold the contraction at the top for a brief moment.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Neutral Wrist Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing inward.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, thumb facing upward.
Allow the dumbbell to roll down to your fingers while keeping your forearm stable.
Curl the dumbbell upward by flexing your wrist, bringing it back to the starting position.
Pause at the top of the movement for a brief moment to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.

name: Farmer Walk
instructions: Select a pair of heavy dumbbells or kettlebells that you can carry comfortably for a set distance or time.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the weights resting at your sides.
Engage your core muscles to maintain a straight posture.
Lift the weights off the ground by extending your hips and knees while keeping your back straight.
Begin walking forward at a steady pace, maintaining an upright posture and keeping your shoulders back.
Continue walking for the desired distance or time, focusing on maintaining control over the weights.
Once completed, carefully lower the weights back to the ground by bending your knees and hips.

name: Wrist Roller
instructions: Attach a weight plate to the wrist roller using a secure rope or cord.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the wrist roller with both hands in front of you at shoulder height.
Extend your arms fully, keeping them parallel to the ground.
Begin rolling the weight up by rotating your wrists forward, maintaining controlled movements.
Continue until the weight reaches the top, then slowly reverse the motion to lower the weight back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Reverse Wrist Curls
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms close to your body and extend them fully downward, with your palms facing your thighs.
While keeping your elbows stationary, curl your wrists upwards by contracting your forearm extensors.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, ensuring maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, letting your wrists bend down under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Unilateral Farmer Walk
instructions: Select a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell and place it beside you.
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and engage your core.
Bend at the knees to pick up the weight with one hand, keeping your back straight.
Hold the weight securely at your side with your arm fully extended.
Begin walking forward in a straight line, maintaining an upright posture.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid leaning to one side.
Walk for a set distance or time, then switch hands and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing down).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl the weights upward by bending your elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Continue lifting until your forearms are vertical or slightly beyond, ensuring maximum contraction of the biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hanging Scapular Retractions
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight without swinging or bending at the hips.
Initiate the movement by retracting your scapulae, pulling your shoulder blades down and together.
Hold the retracted position for a moment, ensuring full engagement of the scapular muscles.
Slowly release and return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Seated Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Hold an EZ-bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge of your knees.
Start with your wrists in a neutral position, then slowly curl the bar upwards by extending your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the forearm extensors.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Supination
instructions: Kneel or sit beside a flat bench and rest one forearm on it, with your wrist and hand just past the edge.
Hold a dumbbell in that hand with a neutral grip, thumb side up.
Keep your forearm and elbow pressed into the bench throughout the set.
Slowly rotate your forearm outward until your palm faces up.
Pause briefly, then rotate back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

name: Barbell Standing Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and close to your body, allowing the barbell to rest against your thighs.
Flex your wrists upward, curling the barbell as high as possible while keeping your arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your forearms.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Position your arms by your sides, allowing your wrists to hang just in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your body and stationary throughout the movement.
Slowly curl your wrists upwards, contracting the forearm muscles.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Seated Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, positioning your legs slightly apart.
Hold an EZ bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up) and rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to extend beyond your knees.
Start with your wrists in a neutral position, then slowly curl the bar upwards by flexing your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the forearm muscles.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner, allowing your wrists to extend fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Sit on a bench facing the cable machine, with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to extend over your knees.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Hand Grip
instructions: Load a light plate on the lever horn to start. The lever changes how heavy a plate feels, so the number on it isn't the force in your hands.
Sit upright facing the handles, feet flat and hip-width apart, knees bent about 90°. The handles should sit just in front of your knees and slightly above them.
Take the handles overhand, one hand near each end. One handle lies across your palms at the base of the fingers with your thumbs around it; your fingers wrap the moving handle.
Straighten your wrists so your knuckles line up with your forearms. Let your upper arms hang close to your sides, shoulders down and away from your ears.
Squeeze with both hands at once until the handles meet or stop. The plate rises only a few centimeters, and your elbows and torso stay where they are.
Hold your fists tight for about a second, then open over about 2 seconds until your fingers are almost straight. Stop just before the plate settles and squeeze again.
At the end of the set, let the plate down slowly before you let go, and keep your feet and shins clear of the lever.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench with your chest facing upwards.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly rotate your wrists inward so that your palms face downward.
Hold the pronated position for a moment, ensuring full control over the movement.
Slowly rotate your wrists back to the starting position with palms facing each other.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Standing Wrist Roll
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with both hands, palms facing down, and arms extended in front of you.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and locked in position.
Rotate your wrists upward to roll the bar towards you, engaging the forearm muscles.
Slowly reverse the motion, rotating your wrists downward to return to the starting position.
Perform the movement in a controlled manner, avoiding any jerking motions.

name: EZ-Bar Reverse Spider Curl
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to approximately a 45-degree angle.
Position yourself face down on the bench, with your chest and stomach supported, allowing your arms to hang freely.
Grip the EZ-bar with a pronated (overhand) grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Start with your arms fully extended towards the floor.
Curl the bar upwards by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the forearms and biceps.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Wrist Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank on your toes, placing the backs of your hands on the floor with your fingers pointing towards your body.
Position your wrists under your shoulders and keep your arms straight.
Engage your core to keep a straight line from your head to your heels.
Slowly shift your shoulders forward over your hands, letting your wrists bend while your arms stay straight.
Pause briefly, then press through your hands to shift back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Reverse Grip Preacher Curl
instructions: Set the preacher bench so the pad supports your upper arms comfortably and your armpits rest near the top edge. Load an EZ-bar with a light, controlled weight.
Sit behind the preacher pad and grip the EZ-bar overhand on its angled sections, with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Rest the backs of your upper arms firmly against the pad. Keep your chest close to the bench, wrists straight, and elbows in line with the pad.
Start with your arms almost straight, keeping a small bend in the elbows instead of locking them fully.
Curl the bar upward by bending your elbows. Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad and your shoulders still as you lift.
Raise the bar until your forearms are close to vertical or until you feel a strong contraction in the upper forearms and brachialis. Do not let the bar pull your wrists back.
Lower the bar slowly and under control until your arms return to the starting position. Keep tension in the muscles and avoid dropping the weight at the bottom.

name: Wrist Curl on Machine
instructions: Adjust the machine so the wrist pad supports your forearms comfortably and the handle is within easy reach when your wrists are neutral.
Sit facing the machine with your forearms resting fully on the pad, palms facing upward, and your wrists positioned just beyond the edge of the support.
Grip the handle with an underhand grip, keeping your shoulders relaxed, elbows still, and forearms firmly against the pad.
Allow the handle to roll slightly toward your fingers as you slowly extend your wrists downward, keeping control of the weight.
Curl the handle upward by flexing your wrists and squeezing your forearm muscles, bringing your palms toward your forearms.
Pause briefly at the top without lifting your forearms or using your elbows, then lower the handle slowly to repeat.
Keep the movement isolated to your wrists throughout the set and use a light enough load to maintain a full, controlled range of motion.

name: Plate Pinch Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Pinch the rim of one plate between your thumb and fingers.
Hold the plate at your side with a straight wrist and long arm.
Brace your trunk and bend your hips and knees to squat.
Push through your feet to stand, keeping the plate off your thigh.
Repeat under control, then lower the plate carefully and change hands.

name: Timber Frame Carry
instructions: Stand inside the frame, centered between the rails, with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge at your hips, bend your knees and grip a handle on each side.
Brace your core and drive through your legs to stand up, lifting the frame off the floor.
Stand tall with your arms straight and the frame hanging level at your sides.
Walk forward with short, quick steps, keeping your torso upright and your eyes ahead.
At the finish, stop, bend your knees and hips and set the frame down under control.

name: Machine Abdominal Crunches
instructions: Set the pin in the stack. Go light the first time on a new machine, because crunch machines differ a lot in leverage.
Adjust the seat so that, sitting tall, the handles are about ear height and the padded bars rest on your lower chest.
Sit all the way back and slide your feet under the rollers so they rest on the front of your ankles, knees at about 90°.
Grab the handles beside your head with a full grip, elbows bent and pointing forward and down. Head neutral, eyes forward.
Breathe out and curl your ribs toward your pelvis, rounding from the upper back down. Your chest drives the pads; your arms just ride along.
Stop once your back is fully rounded and your elbows sit in front of your lower ribs. Squeeze a second, hips heavy on the seat.
Uncurl over 2–3 seconds to sitting tall, and start the next rep just before the plates touch down.
When you finish, let the stack settle completely before you take your hands off the handles.

name: Kneeling Cable Abs Crunches
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Kneel down facing the machine, about two feet away, with your back straight.
Grab the rope handles with both hands and position them behind your head, keeping your elbows bent.
Engage your core and pull the rope down by contracting your abs, bringing your elbows towards your thighs.
Hold the contraction briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension in your abs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Start in a kneeling position on a mat to protect your knees.
Grip the handles of the ab wheel firmly with both hands.
Position the wheel on the floor in front of you, directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body as far as you can without losing form.
Pause briefly at the extended position, ensuring your core remains tight.
Reverse the movement by pulling the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining control throughout.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Abdominal Crunches
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your hands behind your head with elbows pointing outwards. Avoid pulling on your neck.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Lift your shoulder blades off the ground by contracting your abdominal muscles. Exhale as you lift.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring not to pull with your neck or arms.
Inhale as you slowly lower back down to the starting position without letting your shoulders touch the ground completely.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hanging Knee To Chest
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Allow your body to hang freely with arms fully extended and feet off the ground.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slowly lift your knees towards your chest by flexing at the hips and knees.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your thighs are parallel to the ground or higher.
Lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Plank
instructions: Kneel on the floor and set your forearms down with your elbows right under your shoulders, forearms parallel and pointing straight ahead, palms flat.
Step your feet back one at a time onto the balls of your feet, toes tucked and feet close together. If you wobble, widen them to hip width.
Lift your knees until your body forms one straight line from head to heels, hips in line with your shoulders and heels, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Brace before you start the clock: ribs down toward your pelvis, tailbone tucked slightly toward your heels, glutes squeezed hard.
Push the floor away with your forearms so your chest doesn't sink between your shoulder blades, then hold still and keep taking short, quiet breaths.
The set is over as soon as your hips drop or start to rise. Lower your knees to the floor and sit back on your heels.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended towards the ceiling and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle above your hips.
Engage your core by drawing your navel towards your spine, ensuring your lower back is pressed into the floor.
Slowly extend your right arm behind you while simultaneously straightening your left leg towards the floor, keeping both just above the ground.
Return to the starting position by bringing your arm and leg back to the initial position.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side by extending your left arm and right leg.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Kneeling Side Crunch
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Kneel on the floor with your side facing the machine, keeping your knees hip-width apart.
Grab the handle with the hand closest to the machine, and place your other hand behind your head.
Engage your core and pull the handle down by bending your torso sideways towards the machine.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the obliques.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Lying Straight Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms at your sides, palms facing down.
Keep your legs straight and together, then slowly lift them towards the ceiling while keeping your core engaged.
Raise your legs until they form a 90-degree angle with your torso or as high as you can without lifting your lower back off the ground.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your core remains tight.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, maintaining control and avoiding any sudden drops.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Toes To Bar
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Engage your core and initiate the movement by slightly swinging your legs back.
Use your core muscles to lift your legs upward, aiming to bring your toes to touch the bar.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding excessive swinging.
Lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Captain's Chair Straight Leg Raises
instructions: Position yourself in the Captain's Chair with your back firmly against the pad and your forearms resting on the arm pads. Grip the handles for stability.
Ensure your body is stable and your shoulders are relaxed. Your legs should hang straight down, with feet together.
Engage your core by pulling your navel towards your spine.
Slowly lift your legs straight up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground, keeping them together and straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the abdominal muscles.
Lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner without swinging or using momentum.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lift your legs straight up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground.
Keep your legs straight and avoid swinging or using momentum.
Hold the top position briefly, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a dumbbell with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly to engage your core, keeping your back straight.
Lift your feet off the ground, balancing on your glutes if possible. Alternatively, keep your feet on the ground for more stability.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the dumbbell beside your hip.
Return to the center and then rotate to the left side.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled manner for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Decline Crunch
instructions: Adjust the decline bench to a comfortable angle, typically between 15 to 30 degrees.
Sit on the bench and secure your feet under the padded rollers.
Lie back with your hands placed behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core by pulling your navel towards your spine.
Exhale and lift your upper body towards your knees by contracting your abdominal muscles.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction.
Inhale and slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Lift your shoulders and legs off the ground simultaneously, keeping your lower back pressed into the mat.
Point your toes and keep your ribs pulled down so your body forms a shallow curve.
Hold this position, keeping your arms and legs straight and close to the floor without touching it.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold, maintaining tension in your core.

name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent about 90°, knees and feet together, heels down and toes pointing up.
Hold the ball at your chest with a hand on each side, palms facing and fingers spread. Keep your fingers off the bottom of the ball so the floor can't pinch them.
Lean back to about 45°, halfway between sitting upright and lying down. Chest up, spine long, and brace your abs as if someone were about to poke your stomach.
Turn your chest and shoulders to one side and lower the ball beside that hip until it touches, or nearly touches, the floor. Your knees stay put.
Rotate back through the middle, where the ball passes in front of your chest, and lower it beside the other hip. Breathe out each time you reach a side.
Take 1–2 seconds from side to side without changing the lean. Right plus left counts as one rep; finish the set with the ball back at your chest and sit up.

name: Sit Up
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your ears, keeping your elbows wide.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Exhale as you curl your upper body up towards your knees, lifting your back off the floor one section at a time.
Pause at the top of the movement, ensuring your torso is upright and spine neutral.
Inhale as you slowly lower back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Air Bike
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with your hands behind your head and your elbows wide.
Lift both legs off the floor with the knees almost straight and press your lower back into the mat.
Curl your shoulders up and twist to bring your right elbow toward your left knee as you pull that knee in toward your chest.
Keep your right leg straight and low, just above the floor.
Lower your shoulders back to the mat and straighten your left leg.
Repeat to the other side, left elbow toward right knee, and keep alternating.
Breathe out as you twist up and breathe in as you lower.

name: Reverse Crunches
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms by your sides, palms facing down.
Bend your knees at a 90-degree angle and lift your feet off the ground so that your thighs are perpendicular to the floor.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Exhale as you curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest. Keep the movement controlled.
Inhale as you slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting your feet touch the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Side Bend
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand with your arm fully extended by your side.
Place your left hand on your hip or behind your head for support.
Engage your core and slowly bend at the waist to the right side, lowering the dumbbell towards the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling a stretch in your left oblique.
Return to the starting position by contracting your left oblique muscles.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side before switching the dumbbell to the other hand and repeating on the opposite side.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and stacked from hip to feet.
Place your elbow directly under your shoulder, ensuring your forearm is perpendicular to your body.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your head in line with your spine and hold the position while breathing steadily.
Maintain the position for the desired duration, then switch sides.

name: Ankle Taps
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, a little wider than hip-width apart.
Rest your arms by your sides with your palms facing in, just off the floor.
Brace your abs and curl your head and shoulders slightly off the floor.
Bend sideways at the waist and reach your right hand toward your right heel until you tap it.
Return to the center without lowering your shoulders.
Reach to the left and tap your left heel.
Keep alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raises
instructions: Position yourself on the Captain's Chair with your back firmly against the backrest.
Grip the handles firmly to stabilize your upper body.
Allow your legs to hang freely with feet off the ground.
Engage your core by drawing your navel towards your spine.
Slowly lift your knees towards your chest in a controlled manner.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the abdominal muscles.
Lower your legs back to the starting position without swinging or using momentum.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Sitting Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground. Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest or grasp a weight if using resistance.
Keep your back straight and rotate your torso to the right, bringing your hands or weight beside your hip.
Return to the center and then rotate to the left, repeating the movement.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Twist (horizontal)
instructions: Set the cable machine to chest height and attach a single handle.
Stand sideways to the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, grasping the handle with both hands.
Extend your arms fully in front of you, keeping them parallel to the floor.
Engage your core muscles and rotate your torso away from the machine, keeping your arms extended.
Rotate until your torso faces away from the machine, then slowly return to the starting position.
Perform the desired number of repetitions and switch sides.

name: Weighted Decline Crunch
instructions: Set the ab bench to a moderate decline, about 20–30°. On most benches that's a middle hole, and steeper is harder.
Sit on the short top pad, hook the front of your ankles under the foot roller and bend your knees about 90° over the edge.
While you're still sitting up, press the plate flat against your upper chest and cross your forearms over it, hands reaching toward the opposite shoulders.
Lie back slowly until your shoulder blades touch the pad. Your head is now below your hips; keep it in line, chin slightly tucked.
Breathe out and pull your ribs toward your pelvis, peeling your head, then your shoulders, then your upper back off the pad.
Stop about 45° from the bench, with your shoulder blades and mid-back up and your lower back still on the pad. Squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to uncurl until your shoulder blades touch down, and start the next rep before your head comes to rest.
Finish by sitting up first, then set the plate down beside the bench. Light-headed? Give it a few seconds before you stand.

name: Straight Leg Raise on Dip Bars
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself between the dip bars, gripping each bar firmly with your palms facing inward.
Lift your body off the ground by extending your arms fully, keeping your shoulders engaged and down away from your ears.
Engage your core muscles and straighten your legs, keeping them together.
Slowly raise your straight legs in front of you until your hips are bent to roughly a right angle, letting your torso lean slightly forward.
Hold the position briefly at the top, ensuring your core remains tight.
Lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner without swinging or using momentum.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Twist (up down)
instructions: Set the cable machine to a high pulley position and attach a single handle.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, side-on to the machine, and grasp the handle with both hands.
Engage your core and slightly bend your knees for stability.
Pull the handle downward across your body in a controlled motion, rotating your torso as you do so.
